title.zh: 卷五十四 列傳第四十八 諸夷
title.raw: 卷五十四 列傳第四十八 諸夷 Volume 54: Various Barbarians

sentences.zh: 海南諸國

translations.literal: States of the Southern Sea
translations.idiomatic: States of the Southern Sea

sentences.zh: 海南諸國，大抵在交州南及西南大海洲上，相去近者三五千里，遠者二三萬里，其西與西域諸國接。

translations.literal: The states of the Southern Sea lie generally south of Jiao Province and on the great ocean isles to the southwest; the near ones are three to five thousand li apart, the far ones twenty or thirty thousand li; to the west they connect with the states of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Sea states lie south of Jiao Province and on great ocean isles to the southwest—near ones three to five thousand li apart, far ones twenty or thirty thousand li; westward they adjoin the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 漢元鼎中，遣伏波將軍路博多開百越，置日南郡。

translations.literal: In Han Yuanding, General Fu Bo Lu Boda was sent to open the Hundred Yue and establish Rinan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Han Yuanding, General Fu Bo Lu Boda was sent to open the Hundred Yue and establish Rinan commandery.

sentences.zh: 其徼外諸國，自武帝以來皆朝貢。

translations.literal: All the states beyond the frontiers, from Emperor Wu onward, came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: All the states beyond the frontiers, from Emperor Wu onward, came to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 後漢桓帝世，大秦、天竺皆由此道遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In Later Han during Emperor Huan's reign, Da Qin and Tianzhu both sent envoys by this route to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han during Emperor Huan's reign, Da Qin and Tianzhu both sent envoys by this route to offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 及吳孫權時，遣宣化從事朱應、中郎康泰通焉。

translations.literal: When Wu's Sun Quan ruled, he sent Director of Civilizing Affairs Zhu Ying and Gentlemen-of-Attendant Kang Tai to reach them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu's Sun Quan ruled, he sent Director of Civilizing Affairs Zhu Ying and Gentlemen-of-Attendant Kang Tai to reach them.

sentences.zh: 其所經及傳聞，則有百數十國，因立記傳。

translations.literal: The lands they passed through and heard of amounted to over a hundred states, and they therefore compiled a record account.
translations.idiomatic: The lands they passed through and heard of amounted to over a hundred states, and they compiled a record account.

sentences.zh: 晉代通中國者蓋鮮，故不載史官。

translations.literal: In Jin times those reaching China were few, so the official historians did not record them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin times few reached China, so the official historians did not record them.

sentences.zh: 及宋、齊，至者有十餘國，始爲之傳。

translations.literal: By Song and Qi, over ten states had arrived, and only then were accounts written for them.
translations.idiomatic: By Song and Qi, over ten states had arrived, and only then were accounts written for them.

sentences.zh: 自梁革運，其奉正朔，脩貢職，航海歲至，踰於前代矣。

translations.literal: Since Liang changed the dynastic mandate, those observing the calendar and fulfilling tribute duties, reaching by sea year after year, exceeded the earlier dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liang changed the dynastic mandate, those observing the calendar and fulfilling tribute duties reached by sea year after year—surpassing earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 今采其風俗粗著者，綴爲《海南傳》云。

translations.literal: Now I collect those whose customs are roughly well known and assemble them in "Account of the Southern Sea," thus.
translations.idiomatic: Now I collect those whose customs are roughly well known and assemble them in the Account of the Southern Sea, thus.

sentences.zh: 林邑國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Lin Yi
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Lin Yi

sentences.zh: 林邑國者，本漢日南郡象林縣，古越裳之界也。

translations.literal: The kingdom of Lin Yi was originally Xianglin County in Han's Rinan commandery, on the border of ancient Yuechang.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Lin Yi was originally Xianglin County in Han's Rinan commandery, on the border of ancient Yuechang.

sentences.zh: 伏波將軍馬援開漢南境，置此縣。

translations.literal: General Fu Bo Ma Yuan opened Han's southern frontier and established this county.
translations.idiomatic: General Fu Bo Ma Yuan opened Han's southern frontier and established this county.

sentences.zh: 其地縱廣可六百里，城去海百二十里，去日南界四百餘里，北接九德郡。

translations.literal: Its territory was about six hundred li north-south and east-west; the capital was a hundred and twenty li from the sea, over four hundred li from the Rinan border, and abutted Jiude commandery to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory ran about six hundred li; the capital stood a hundred and twenty li from the sea, over four hundred li from the Rinan border, and abutted Jiude commandery to the north.

sentences.zh: 其南界，水步道二百餘里，有西國夷亦稱王，馬援植兩銅柱表漢界處也。

translations.literal: At its southern border, by water and land routes it was over two hundred li; there was a Western-state barbarian who also styled himself king—it was where Ma Yuan planted two bronze columns marking Han's border.
translations.idiomatic: At its southern border, by water and land routes it was over two hundred li; a Western-state chieftain also styled himself king—where Ma Yuan planted two bronze columns marking Han's border.

sentences.zh: 其國有金山，石皆赤色，其中生金。

translations.literal: In its land was Golden Mountain; the stones were all red, and gold was produced within them.
translations.idiomatic: In its land was Golden Mountain; the stones were all red, and gold was produced within them.

sentences.zh: 金夜則出飛，狀如螢火。

translations.literal: At night the gold flew forth, looking like fireflies.
translations.idiomatic: At night the gold flew forth, looking like fireflies.

sentences.zh: 又出玳瑁、貝齒、吉貝、沉木香。

translations.literal: It also produced tortoiseshell, cowrie shells, kapok cloth, and aloeswood.
translations.idiomatic: It also produced tortoiseshell, cowrie shells, kapok cloth, and aloeswood.

sentences.zh: 吉貝者，樹名也，其華成時如鵝毳，抽其緒紡之以作布，潔白與紵布不殊，亦染成五色，織爲斑布也。

translations.literal: Kapok is the name of a tree; when its blossoms mature they are like goose down; its fibers are drawn and spun to make cloth, clean and white no different from ramie cloth—it can also be dyed five colors and woven into patterned cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Kapok is a tree; when its blossoms mature they are like goose down; its fibers are spun into cloth, clean and white like ramie—it can also be dyed five colors and woven into patterned cloth.

sentences.zh: 沉木者，土人斫斷之，積以歲年，朽爛而心節獨在，置水中則沉，故名曰沉香。

translations.literal: Aloeswood: the natives cut it down and pile it for years; though rotten the heart alone remains; placed in water it sinks—hence the name sinking incense.
translations.idiomatic: Aloeswood: natives cut it down and pile it for years; though rotten the heart alone remains; placed in water it sinks—hence the name sinking incense.

sentences.zh: 次不沉不浮者，曰𥴈香也。

translations.literal: Next, that which neither sinks nor floats is called honey incense.
translations.idiomatic: Next, that which neither sinks nor floats is called honey incense.

sentences.zh: 漢末大亂，功曹區達，殺縣令自立爲王。

translations.literal: At the end of Han amid great chaos, Chief Clerk Qu Da killed the magistrate and declared himself king.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han amid great chaos, Chief Clerk Qu Da killed the magistrate and declared himself king.

sentences.zh: 傳數世，其後王無嗣，立外甥范熊。

translations.literal: Passed through several generations; later the king had no heir and installed his sister's son Fan Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Passed through several generations; later the king had no heir and installed his sister's son Fan Xiong.

sentences.zh: 熊死，子逸嗣。

translations.literal: When Xiong died, his son Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong died, his son Yi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康三年，逸死，奴文篡立。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiankang under Jin Emperor Cheng, Yi died and the slave Wen usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiankang under Jin Emperor Cheng, Yi died and the slave Wen usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 文本日南西卷縣夷帥范稚家奴，常牧牛於山澗，得鱧魚二頭，化而爲鐵，因以鑄刀。

translations.literal: Wen was originally a slave of the Yi chieftain Fan Zhi of Xijuan County west of Rinan; he often herded cattle in mountain streams, obtained two snakehead fish that transformed into iron, and thus cast a knife.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was originally a slave of the Yi chieftain Fan Zhi of Xijuan County west of Rinan; he often herded cattle in mountain streams, obtained two snakehead fish that transformed into iron, and thus cast a knife.

sentences.zh: 鑄成，文向石而咒曰：「若斫石破者，文當王此國。

translations.literal: When it was cast, Wen cursed toward a stone, saying: "If in cutting this stone it breaks, Wen shall be king of this state.
translations.idiomatic: When it was cast, Wen cursed toward a stone, saying, "If in cutting this stone it breaks, Wen shall be king of this state.

sentences.zh: 」因舉刀斫石，如斷芻藳，文心獨異之。

translations.literal: " He then raised the knife and cut the stone—as if cutting dry grass; Wen alone marvelled at this in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: " he then raised the knife and cut the stone—as if cutting dry grass; Wen alone marvelled at this in his heart.

sentences.zh: 范稚常使之商賈至林邑，因教林邑王作宮室及兵車器械，王寵任之。

translations.literal: Fan Zhi often sent him on trading missions to Lin Yi, and thus taught the Lin Yi king to build palaces and military chariots and weapons—the king favored and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhi often sent him on trading missions to Lin Yi, and thus taught the Lin Yi king to build palaces and military chariots and weapons—the king favored and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 後乃讒王諸子，各奔餘國。

translations.literal: Later he slandered the king's sons, and each fled to other states.
translations.idiomatic: Later he slandered the king's sons, and each fled to other states.

sentences.zh: 及王死無嗣，文偽於鄰國迓王子，置毒於漿中而殺之，遂脅國人自立。

translations.literal: When the king died without heir, Wen feigned at a neighboring state to welcome the prince, put poison in syrup and killed him, then coerced the people of the state to install himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the king died without heir, Wen feigned at a neighboring state to welcome the prince, put poison in syrup and killed him, then coerced the people of the state to install himself.

sentences.zh: 舉兵攻旁小國，皆吞滅之，有衆四五萬人。

translations.literal: He raised troops to attack neighboring small states and swallowed them all, having a host of forty to fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He raised troops to attack neighboring small states and swallowed them all, having a host of forty to fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 時交州刺史姜莊使所親韓戢、謝稚，前後監日南郡，並貪殘，諸國患之。

translations.literal: At the time Jiao Province Inspector Jiang Zhuang sent his intimates Han Ji and Xie Zhi in succession to supervise Rinan commandery—both greedy and cruel, and the states were vexed by them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jiao Province Inspector Jiang Zhuang sent his intimates Han Ji and Xie Zhi in succession to supervise Rinan commandery—both greedy and cruel, and the states were vexed by them.

sentences.zh: 穆帝永和三年，臺遣夏侯覽爲太守，侵刻尤甚。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu, the court sent Xiahou Lan as administrator—invasive exactions were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu, the court sent Xiahou Lan as administrator—invasive exactions were especially severe.

sentences.zh: 林邑先無田土，貪日南地肥沃，常欲略有之，至是，因民之怨，遂舉兵襲日南，殺覽，以其屍祭天。

translations.literal: Lin Yi formerly had no farmland; coveting Rinan's fertile soil, it often wished to seize it—at this time, taking advantage of the people's resentment, it raised troops to raid Rinan, killed Lan, and sacrificed his corpse to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi formerly had no farmland; coveting Rinan's fertile soil, it often wished to seize it—at this time, taking advantage of the people's resentment, it raised troops to raid Rinan, killed Lan, and sacrificed his corpse to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 留日南三年，乃還林邑。

translations.literal: It remained in Rinan three years, then returned to Lin Yi.
translations.idiomatic: It remained in Rinan three years, then returned to Lin Yi.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史朱籓後遣督護劉雄戍日南，文復屠滅之。

translations.literal: Later Jiao Province Inspector Zhu Fan sent Supervisor Liu Xiong to garrison Rinan; Wen again slaughtered and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jiao Province Inspector Zhu Fan sent Supervisor Liu Xiong to garrison Rinan; Wen again slaughtered and destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 進寇九德郡，殘害吏民。

translations.literal: Advancing to raid Jiude commandery, he ravaged officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to raid Jiude commandery, he ravaged officials and people.

sentences.zh: 遣使告籓，願以日南北境橫山爲界，籓不許，又遣督護陶緩、李衢討之。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to inform Fan, wishing to take the Heng Mountains on Rinan's northern border as the boundary—Fan would not agree, and again sent Supervisors Tao Huan and Li Qu to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to inform Fan, wishing to take the Heng Mountains on Rinan's northern border as the boundary—Fan would not agree, and again sent Supervisors Tao Huan and Li Qu to attack him.

sentences.zh: 文歸林邑，尋復屯日南。

translations.literal: Wen returned to Lin Yi, but soon again encamped in Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen returned to Lin Yi, but soon again encamped in Rinan.

sentences.zh: 五年，文死，子佛立，猶屯日南。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Wen died; his son Fo succeeded, still encamped in Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Wen died; his son Fo succeeded, still encamped in Rinan.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍桓溫遣督護滕畯、九真太守灌邃帥交、廣州兵討之，佛嬰城固守。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the West Huan Wen sent Supervisors Teng Jun and Jiuzhen Administrator Guan Sui to lead Jiao and Guang Province troops against him; Fo defended the city obstinately.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers the West Huan Wen sent Supervisors Teng Jun and Jiuzhen Administrator Guan Sui to lead Jiao and Guang Province troops against him; Fo defended the city obstinately.

sentences.zh: 邃令峻盛兵於前，邃帥勁卒七百人，自後逾壘而入，佛衆驚潰奔走，邃追至林邑，佛乃請降。

translations.literal: Sui ordered Jun to mass troops at the front; Sui himself led seven hundred elite soldiers over the ramparts from behind; Fo's host panicked and fled; Sui pursued to Lin Yi and Fo then requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Sui ordered Jun to mass troops at the front; Sui himself led seven hundred elite soldiers over the ramparts from behind; Fo's host panicked and fled; Sui pursued to Lin Yi and Fo then requested surrender.

sentences.zh: 哀帝昇平初，復爲寇暴，刺史溫放之討破之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengping under Emperor Ai, he again raided violently; Inspector Wen Fangzhi attacked and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shengping under Emperor Ai, he again raided violently; Inspector Wen Fangzhi attacked and broke him.

sentences.zh: 安帝隆安三年，佛孫須達復寇日南，執太守炅源，又進寇九德，執太守曹炳。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longan under Emperor An, Fo's grandson Xu Da again raided Rinan, seized Administrator Jiong Yuan, and further raided Jiude, seizing Administrator Cao Bing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Longan under Emperor An, Fo's grandson Xu Da again raided Rinan, seized Administrator Jiong Yuan, and further raided Jiude, seizing Administrator Cao Bing.

sentences.zh: 交趾太守杜瑗遣都護鄧逸等擊破之，卽以瑗爲刺史。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi Administrator Du Yuan sent Protector Deng Yi and others to attack and break them, and Yuan was then made inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi Administrator Du Yuan sent Protector Deng Yi and others to attack and break them, and Yuan was then made inspector.

sentences.zh: 義熙三年，須達復寇日南，殺長史，瑗遣海邏督護阮斐討破之，斬獲甚衆。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yixi, Xu Da again raided Rinan and killed the chief clerk; Yuan sent Coastal Protector Ruan Fei to attack and break him, slaying and capturing in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yixi, Xu Da again raided Rinan and killed the chief clerk; Yuan sent Coastal Protector Ruan Fei to attack and break him, slaying and capturing in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 九年，須達復寇九真，行郡事杜慧期與戰，斬其息交龍王甄知及其將范健等，生俘須達息𨚗能，及虜獲百餘人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Xu Da again raided Jiuzhen; Du Huiqi acting for the commandery fought him, beheading his son Jiaolong Wang Zhenzhi and his general Fan Jian and others, taking alive Xu Da's son Cheneng, and capturing over a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Xu Da again raided Jiuzhen; Du Huiqi acting for the commandery fought him, beheading his son Jiaolong Wang Zhenzhi and his general Fan Jian and others, taking alive Xu Da's son Cheneng, and capturing over a hundred.

sentences.zh: 自瑗卒後，林邑無歲不寇日南、九德諸郡，殺蕩甚多，交州遂致虛弱。

translations.literal: After Yuan died, Lin Yi year after year raided Rinan, Jiude and other commanderies, killing and ravaging greatly, and Jiao Province thus became weak and depleted.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan died, Lin Yi year after year raided Rinan, Jiude and other commanderies, killing and ravaging greatly, and Jiao Province thus became weak and depleted.

sentences.zh: 須達死，子敵真立，其弟敵鎧擕母出奔。

translations.literal: When Xu Da died, his son Dizhen succeeded; his younger brother Dikai fled carrying their mother.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Da died, his son Dizhen succeeded; his younger brother Dikai fled carrying their mother.

sentences.zh: 敵真追恨不能容其母弟，捨國而之天竺，禪位於其甥，國相藏膋固諫不從。

translations.literal: Dizhen, brooding that he could not tolerate his mother and younger brother, abandoned the state and went to Tianzhu, yielding the throne to his nephew—the chief minister Zang Xiao earnestly remonstrated but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Dizhen, brooding that he could not tolerate his mother and younger brother, abandoned the state and went to Tianzhu, yielding the throne to his nephew—the chief minister Zang Xiao earnestly remonstrated but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 其甥旣立而殺藏膋，藏膋子又攻殺之，而立敵鎧同母異父之弟曰文敵。

translations.literal: The nephew once enthroned killed Zang Xiao; Zang Xiao's son in turn attacked and killed him, and enthroned Dikai's younger half-brother on his mother's side named Wen Di.
translations.idiomatic: The nephew once enthroned killed Zang Xiao; Zang Xiao's son in turn attacked and killed him, and enthroned Dikai's younger half-brother on his mother's side named Wen Di.

sentences.zh: 文敵後爲扶南王子當根純所殺，大臣范諸農平其亂，而自立爲王。

translations.literal: Wen Di was later killed by Funan prince Danggen Chun; the great minister Fan Zhunong quelled the disorder and installed himself as king.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Di was later killed by Funan prince Danggen Chun; the great minister Fan Zhunong quelled the disorder and installed himself as king.

sentences.zh: 諸農死，子陽邁立。

translations.literal: When Zhunong died, his son Yang Mai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhunong died, his son Yang Mai succeeded.

sentences.zh: 宋永初二年，遣使貢獻，以陽邁爲林邑王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu under Song, envoys were sent with tribute, and Yang Mai was made King of Lin Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongchu under Song, envoys were sent with tribute, and Yang Mai was made King of Lin Yi.

sentences.zh: 陽邁死，子咄立，慕其父，復曰陽邁。

translations.literal: When Yang Mai died, his son Dhuo succeeded; admiring his father, he again took the name Yang Mai.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Mai died, his son Dhuo succeeded; admiring his father, he again took the name Yang Mai.

sentences.zh: 其國俗：居處爲閣，名曰于蘭，門戶皆北向；

translations.literal: Its national customs: dwellings are raised pavilions called yulan, with doors and gates all facing north;
translations.idiomatic: Its national customs: dwellings are raised pavilions called yulan, with doors and gates all facing north;

sentences.zh: 書樹葉爲紙；

translations.literal: they write on tree leaves as paper;
translations.idiomatic: they write on tree leaves as paper;

sentences.zh: 男女皆以橫幅吉貝繞腰以下，謂之干漫，亦曰都縵；

translations.literal: men and women all wrap their lower bodies in horizontal strips of kapok cloth, called ganman, also called duzman;
translations.idiomatic: men and women all wrap their lower bodies in horizontal strips of kapok cloth, called ganman, also called duzman;

sentences.zh: 穿耳貫小鐶；

translations.literal: they pierce ears and thread small rings;
translations.idiomatic: they pierce ears and thread small rings;

sentences.zh: 貴者著革屣，賤者跣行。

translations.literal: the noble wear leather sandals; the lowly go barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: the noble wear leather sandals; the lowly go barefoot.

sentences.zh: 自林邑、扶南以南諸國皆然也。

translations.literal: From Lin Yi and Funan southward all states are thus.
translations.idiomatic: From Lin Yi and Funan southward all states are thus.

sentences.zh: 其王著法服，加瓔珞，如佛像之飾。

translations.literal: Its king wears dharma robes with jewelled chains, like the adornments of a Buddha image.
translations.idiomatic: Its king wears dharma robes with jewelled chains, like the adornments of a Buddha image.

sentences.zh: 出則乘象，吹螺擊鼓，罩吉貝傘，以吉貝爲幡旗。

translations.literal: Going out he rides an elephant, blows conch and beats drums, covers with a kapok-cloth umbrella, and uses kapok cloth for banners and flags.
translations.idiomatic: Going out he rides an elephant, blows conch and beats drums, covers with a kapok-cloth umbrella, and uses kapok cloth for banners and flags.

sentences.zh: 國不設刑法，有罪者使象踏殺之。

translations.literal: The state sets no penal code; those guilty are made to be trampled to death by elephants.
translations.idiomatic: The state sets no penal code; those guilty are made to be trampled to death by elephants.

sentences.zh: 其大姓號婆羅門。

translations.literal: Its great clans are called Brahmin.
translations.idiomatic: Its great clans are called Brahmin.

sentences.zh: 嫁娶必用八月，女先求男，由賤男而貴女也。

translations.literal: Marriage must take place in the eighth month; the woman first seeks the man—a lowly man and a noble woman.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage must take place in the eighth month; the woman first seeks the man—a lowly man and a noble woman.

sentences.zh: 同姓還相婚姻，使婆羅門引婿見婦，握手相付，呪曰「吉利吉利」，以爲成禮。

translations.literal: Those of the same surname still marry one another; a Brahmin leads the groom to meet the bride, hands her over with clasped hands, and intones "Auspicious, auspicious"—this constitutes completion of the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Those of the same surname still marry one another; a Brahmin leads the groom to meet the bride, hands her over with clasped hands, and intones "Auspicious, auspicious"—this constitutes completion of the rite.

sentences.zh: 死者焚之中野，謂之火葬。

translations.literal: The dead are burned in the open wilds—called cremation.
translations.idiomatic: The dead are burned in the open wilds—called cremation.

sentences.zh: 其寡婦孤居，散髮至老。

translations.literal: Its widows live alone, hair loose until old age.
translations.idiomatic: Its widows live alone, hair loose until old age.

sentences.zh: 國王事尼乾道，鑄金銀人像，大十圍。

translations.literal: The king attends the Ni'gan Way and casts gold and silver human images ten arm-spans around.
translations.idiomatic: The king attends the Ni'gan Way and casts gold and silver human images ten arm-spans around.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，陽邁侵暴日南、九德諸郡，交州刺史杜弘文建牙欲討之，聞有代乃止。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia Yang Mai raided Rinan and Jiude commanderies; Jiao Province Inspector Du Hongwen set up headquarters intending to attack, but hearing he would be replaced, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanjia Yang Mai raided Rinan and Jiude commanderies; Jiao Province Inspector Du Hongwen set up headquarters intending to attack, but hearing he would be replaced, stopped.

sentences.zh: 八年，又寇九德郡，入四會浦口，交州刺史阮彌之遣隊主相道生帥兵赴討，攻區栗城不剋，乃引還。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he again raided Jiude commandery, entering Sihui Estuary; Jiao Province Inspector Ruan Mizhi sent Squad Leader Xiang Daosheng to lead troops against him—they attacked Qu Li city but could not take it, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he again raided Jiude commandery, entering Sihui Estuary; Jiao Province Inspector Ruan Mizhi sent Squad Leader Xiang Daosheng to lead troops against him—they attacked Qu Li city but could not take it, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 爾後頻年遣使貢獻，而寇盜不已。

translations.literal: Thereafter he sent envoys with tribute year after year, yet raiding and plunder never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he sent envoys with tribute year after year, yet raiding and plunder never ceased.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，使交州刺史檀和之、振武將軍宗愨伐之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he had Jiao Province Inspector Tan Hezhi and General Who Quells Martial Affairs Zong Que attack them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he had Jiao Province Inspector Tan Hezhi and General Who Quells Martial Affairs Zong Que attack them.

sentences.zh: 和之遣司馬蕭景憲爲前鋒，陽邁聞之懼，欲輸金一萬斤，銀十萬斤，還所略日南民戶，其大臣䓯僧達諫止之，乃遣大帥范扶龍戍其北界區栗城。

translations.literal: Hezhi sent Army Adviser Xiao Jingxian as vanguard; Yang Mai hearing this was afraid and wished to deliver ten thousand jin of gold and a hundred thousand jin of silver and return the Rinan households he had seized—his great minister Zeng Sengda remonstrated and stopped him, and he then sent Grand Commander Fan Fulong to garrison Qu Li city on the northern border.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhi sent Army Adviser Xiao Jingxian as vanguard; Yang Mai hearing this was afraid and wished to deliver ten thousand jin of gold and a hundred thousand jin of silver and return the Rinan households he had seized—his great minister Zeng Sengda remonstrated and stopped him, and he then sent Grand Commander Fan Fulong to garrison Qu Li city on the northern border.

sentences.zh: 景憲攻城，剋之，斬扶龍首，獲金銀雜物，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Jingxian attacked the city and took it, beheading Fulong's head; gold, silver, and miscellaneous goods captured were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian attacked the city and took it, beheading Fulong's head; gold, silver, and miscellaneous goods captured were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 乘勝徑進，卽剋林邑。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory straight onward, they immediately took Lin Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory straight onward, they immediately took Lin Yi.

sentences.zh: 陽邁父子並挺身逃奔。

translations.literal: Yang Mai father and son both fled in person.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Mai father and son both fled in person.

sentences.zh: 獲其珍異，皆是未名之寶。

translations.literal: The rare and wondrous things captured were all treasures without names.
translations.idiomatic: The rare and wondrous things captured were all treasures without names.

sentences.zh: 又銷其金人，得黃金數十萬斤。

translations.literal: They also melted down the gold images and obtained several hundred thousand jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: They also melted down the gold images and obtained several hundred thousand jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 和之後病死，見胡神爲祟。

translations.literal: Hezhi afterward died of illness, seeing a foreign god as the cause of harm.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhi afterward died of illness, seeing a foreign god as the cause of harm.

sentences.zh: 扶南國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Funan
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Funan

sentences.zh: 扶南國，在日南郡之南海西大灣中，去日南可七千里，在林邑西南三千餘里。

translations.literal: Funan lay in the great bay west of the Southern Sea of Rinan commandery, about seven thousand li from Rinan, and over three thousand li southwest of Lin Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Funan lay in the great bay west of the Southern Sea of Rinan commandery, about seven thousand li from Rinan, and over three thousand li southwest of Lin Yi.

sentences.zh: 城去海五百里。

translations.literal: The capital was five hundred li from the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was five hundred li from the sea.

sentences.zh: 有大江廣十里，西北流，東入於海。

translations.literal: There was a great river ten li wide, flowing northwest and entering the sea to the east.
translations.idiomatic: There was a great river ten li wide, flowing northwest and entering the sea to the east.

sentences.zh: 其國輪廣三千餘里，土地洿下而平博，氣候風俗大較與林邑同。

translations.literal: The state measured over three thousand li across; the land was low, wet, and broad and flat; climate and customs largely resembled Lin Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The state measured over three thousand li across; the land was low, wet, and broad and flat; climate and customs largely resembled Lin Yi.

sentences.zh: 出金、銀、銅、錫、沉木香、象牙、孔翠、五色鸚鵡。

translations.literal: It produced gold, silver, copper, tin, aloeswood, ivory, kingfishers, and five-colored parrots.
translations.idiomatic: It produced gold, silver, copper, tin, aloeswood, ivory, kingfishers, and five-colored parrots.

sentences.zh: 其南界三千餘里有頓遜國，在海崎上，地方千里，城去海十里。

translations.literal: Three thousand li or more to its south was the kingdom of Dunsun, on a sea promontory, a thousand li in territory, the capital ten li from the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand li or more to its south was the kingdom of Dunsun, on a sea promontory, a thousand li in territory, the capital ten li from the sea.

sentences.zh: 有五王，並羈屬扶南。

translations.literal: There were five kings, all bound in submission to Funan.
translations.idiomatic: There were five kings, all bound in submission to Funan.

sentences.zh: 頓遜之東界通交州，其西界接天竺、安息徼外諸國，往還交市。

translations.literal: Dunsun's eastern border connected with Jiao Province; its western border adjoined Tianzhu and the states beyond Anxi's frontiers, trading back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Dunsun's eastern border connected with Jiao Province; its western border adjoined Tianzhu and the states beyond Anxi's frontiers, trading back and forth.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，頓遜回入海中千餘里，漲海無崖岸，船舶未曾得徑過也。

translations.literal: The reason was that Dunsun curved inward into the sea over a thousand li—the rising sea had no shore, and ships had never been able to pass straight through.
translations.idiomatic: The reason was that Dunsun curved inward into the sea over a thousand li—the rising sea had no shore, and ships had never been able to pass straight through.

sentences.zh: 其市，東西交會，日有萬餘人。

translations.literal: At its market east and west met in trade, with over ten thousand people daily.
translations.idiomatic: At its market east and west met in trade, with over ten thousand people daily.

sentences.zh: 珍物寶貨，無所不有。

translations.literal: Rare goods and precious commodities—there was nothing lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Rare goods and precious commodities—there was nothing lacking.

sentences.zh: 又有酒樹，似安石榴，采其花汁停甕中，數日成酒。

translations.literal: There was also a wine tree, resembling a pomegranate; its flower juice was gathered and left in jars, and in several days it became wine.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a wine tree, resembling a pomegranate; its flower juice was gathered and left in jars, and in several days it became wine.

sentences.zh: 頓遜之外，大海洲中，又有毗騫國，去扶南八千里。

translations.literal: Beyond Dunsun, on a great ocean isle, was also the kingdom of Piqian, eight thousand li from Funan.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Dunsun, on a great ocean isle, was also the kingdom of Piqian, eight thousand li from Funan.

sentences.zh: 傳其王身長丈二，頭長三尺，自古來不死，莫知其年。

translations.literal: Tradition says its king was ten chi tall, his head three chi long; from antiquity he had not died, and none knew his years.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition says its king was ten chi tall, his head three chi long; from antiquity he had not died, and none knew his years.

sentences.zh: 王神聖，國中人善惡及將來事，王皆知之，是以無敢欺者。

translations.literal: The king was divine and sage; the good and evil of the people of the state and affairs yet to come—the king knew them all, and therefore none dared deceive.
translations.idiomatic: The king was divine and sage; the good and evil of the people of the state and affairs yet to come—the king knew them all, and therefore none dared deceive.

sentences.zh: 南方號曰長頸王。

translations.literal: In the south they styled him the Long-Necked King.
translations.idiomatic: In the south they styled him the Long-Necked King.

sentences.zh: 國俗，有室屋、衣服，噉粳米。

translations.literal: National custom: they have houses and clothing and eat polished rice.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they live in houses, wear clothes, and eat polished rice.

sentences.zh: 其人言語，小異扶南。

translations.literal: Their speech differs slightly from Funan's.
translations.idiomatic: Their language differs a little from Funan.

sentences.zh: 有山出金，金露生石上，無所限也。

translations.literal: There is a mountain that yields gold; gold appears exposed on the rock with no limit.
translations.idiomatic: A mountain there yields gold that forms bare on the stone without end.

sentences.zh: 國法刑罪人，並于王前噉其肉。

translations.literal: By national law criminals are executed and all eat their flesh before the king.
translations.idiomatic: National law executes criminals, and all eat their flesh in the king's presence.

sentences.zh: 國內不受估客，有往者亦殺而噉之，是以商旅不敢至。

translations.literal: The realm accepts no merchants; any who come are also killed and eaten—hence traders dare not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants are not admitted; any who arrive are killed and eaten, so traders dare not come.

sentences.zh: 王常樓居，不血食，不事鬼神。

translations.literal: The king always dwells in a tower, takes no blood food, and serves no ghosts or spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The king lives in a tower, eats no blood offerings, and worships neither ghosts nor spirits.

sentences.zh: 其子孫生死如常人，唯王不死。

translations.literal: His descendants live and die like ordinary men; only the king does not die.
translations.idiomatic: His line lives and dies as other men do; only the king is immortal.

sentences.zh: 扶南王數遣使與書相報答，常遺扶南王純金五十人食器，形如圓盤，又如瓦塸，名爲多羅，受五升，又如碗者，受一升。

translations.literal: The king of Funan often sent envoys exchanging letters; he regularly gifted the Funan king fifty sets of pure-gold vessels—some round like plates, some like earthen jars called "duo luo" holding five sheng, some like bowls holding one sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Funan king often exchanged letters by envoy and regularly sent fifty sets of pure-gold tableware—round platters, earthen jars called duo luo of five sheng, and bowls of one sheng.

sentences.zh: 王亦能作天竺書，書可三千言，說其宿命所由，與佛經相似，並論善事。

translations.literal: The king could also write in Indic script—about three thousand characters—explaining the causes of his past lives, resembling Buddhist sutras and discoursing on good deeds.
translations.idiomatic: He could also compose some three thousand characters in Indic script on the causes of his former lives—much like a sutra, praising good conduct.

sentences.zh: 又傳扶南東界卽大漲海，海中有大洲，洲上有諸薄國，國東有馬五洲。

translations.literal: It is also said that east of Funan's border lies the Great Rising Sea; in the sea is a great isle, on the isle are various Bo states, and east of those states are the Five Horse Continents.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition also places the Great Rising Sea east of Funan, with a great isle bearing many Bo kingdoms and, farther east, the Five Horse Continents.

sentences.zh: 復東行漲海千餘里，至自然大洲。

translations.literal: Sailing east another thousand-odd li across the rising sea brings one to the Natural Great Isle.
translations.idiomatic: Another thousand-odd li east across the rising sea reaches the Natural Great Isle.

sentences.zh: 其上有樹生火中，洲左近人剝取其皮，紡績作布，極得數尺以爲手巾，與焦麻無異而色微青黑；

translations.literal: There grow trees that burn within fire; people nearby on the isle strip the bark, spin and weave it into cloth—several feet at most for hand towels—no different from ramie but slightly blue-black in color;
translations.idiomatic: Trees there burn from within; islanders strip the bark, spin and weave it into cloth a few feet long for towels—like ramie, but tinged blue-black;

sentences.zh: 若小垢洿，則投火中，復更精潔。

translations.literal: if slightly soiled, cast it in fire and it becomes clean again.
translations.idiomatic: slight stains vanish when the cloth is thrown into fire.

sentences.zh: 或作燈炷，用之不知盡。

translations.literal: Some make it into lamp wicks—it burns without seeming to end.
translations.idiomatic: As lamp wicks it burns as though it would never be spent.

sentences.zh: 扶南國俗本裸體，文身被髮，不制衣裳。

translations.literal: Funan by custom originally went naked, tattooed the body and wore loose hair, making no garments.
translations.idiomatic: Funan once went naked by custom, tattooed and with loose hair, wearing no clothes.

sentences.zh: 以女人爲王，號曰柳葉。

translations.literal: A woman served as king, styled Willow Leaf.
translations.idiomatic: A woman ruled as king under the name Willow Leaf.

sentences.zh: 年少壯健，有似男子。

translations.literal: Young, strong and vigorous, she resembled a man.
translations.idiomatic: She was young, strong, and almost manlike in bearing.

sentences.zh: 其南有徼國，有事鬼神者字混填，夢神賜之弓，乘賈人舶入海。

translations.literal: South of them was the border state; a man who served ghosts and spirits named Hun Tian dreamed the god granted him a bow, and he boarded a merchant ship to sea.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lay a frontier state; Hun Tian, who served spirits, dreamed a god gave him a bow and boarded a merchant vessel for the sea.

sentences.zh: 混填晨起卽詣廟，於神樹下得弓，便依夢乘船入海，遂入扶南外邑。

translations.literal: Hun Tian at dawn went straight to the shrine, found the bow beneath the sacred tree, then as the dream directed sailed the sea and entered a Funan outlying settlement.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Hun Tian went to the shrine, found the bow under the sacred tree, sailed as the dream bade, and entered a Funan outpost.

sentences.zh: 柳葉人衆見舶至，欲取之，混填卽張弓射其舶，穿度一面，矢及侍者，柳葉大懼，舉衆降混填。

translations.literal: Willow Leaf's people saw the ship arrive and meant to seize it; Hun Tian drew the bow and shot through the vessel from side to side—the arrow reaching attendants—and Willow Leaf in great fear led all her people to surrender to Hun Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Willow Leaf's people tried to take the ship; Hun Tian shot clear through it, the arrow striking attendants, and in terror she led her people to submit.

sentences.zh: 混填乃教柳葉穿布貫頭，形不復露，遂治其國，納柳葉爲妻，生子分王七邑。

translations.literal: Hun Tian then taught Willow Leaf to wear neck-cut cloth so the body was no longer exposed; he governed the realm, took Willow Leaf as wife, and his sons were apportioned to rule seven settlements.
translations.idiomatic: He taught Willow Leaf neck-cut cloth to cover her body, ruled the land, married her, and divided seven settlements among his sons.

sentences.zh: 其後王混盤況以詐力間諸邑，令相疑阻，因舉兵攻幷之，乃遣子孫中分治諸邑，號曰小王。

translations.literal: Later King Hun Pan Kuang by deceit and force set the settlements against one another till they mistrusted and blocked each other; he then raised arms to attack and merge them, sent descendants to divide rule over the settlements in the middle, styled Lesser Kings.
translations.idiomatic: Later King Hun Pan Kuang sowed distrust among the settlements by fraud and force, conquered and merged them, and set descendants to rule as Lesser Kings.

sentences.zh: 盤況年九十餘乃死，立中子盤盤，以國事委其大將范蔓。

translations.literal: Pan Kuang died past ninety; the middle son Pan Pan was enthroned, and state affairs were entrusted to his grand general Fan Man.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Kuang died in his nineties; his middle son Pan Pan succeeded, entrusting affairs to Grand General Fan Man.

sentences.zh: 盤盤立三年死，國人共舉蔓爲王。

translations.literal: Pan Pan reigned three years and died; the people together raised Man as king.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Pan ruled three years and died; the people jointly enthroned Man.

sentences.zh: 蔓勇健有權略，復以兵威攻伐旁國，咸服屬之，自號扶南大王。

translations.literal: Man was brave, strong and resourceful; again by military might he attacked neighboring states—all submitted and were annexed—and he styled himself Great King of Funan.
translations.idiomatic: Man was bold, able, and cunning; by arms he subjugated neighboring states and styled himself Great King of Funan.

sentences.zh: 乃治作大船，窮漲海，攻屈都昆、九稚、典孫等十餘國，開地五六千里。

translations.literal: He built great ships, explored the rising sea, attacked more than ten states including Qudu Kun, Jiuzhi, and Diansun, opening territory five or six thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: He built great ships, crossed the rising sea, conquered more than ten states such as Qudu Kun, Jiuzhi, and Diansun, and opened five or six thousand li of land.

sentences.zh: 次當伐金鄰國，蔓遇疾，遣太子金生代行。

translations.literal: Next, when about to attack the state of Jinlin, Man fell ill and sent Crown Prince Jin Sheng in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to attack Jinlin, Man fell ill and sent Crown Prince Jin Sheng in his place.

sentences.zh: 蔓姊子旃，時爲二千人將，因篡蔓自立，遣人詐金生而殺之。

translations.literal: Man's sister's son Zhan, then a commander of two thousand, usurped Man and proclaimed himself king, sent men pretending friendship to trick Jin Sheng and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Man's sister's son Zhan, a commander of two thousand, seized the throne, sent men to deceive Jin Sheng, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 蔓死時，有乳下兒名長，在民間，至年二十，乃結國中壯士襲殺旃，旃大將范尋又殺長而自立。

translations.literal: When Man died there was a nursing infant named Chang among the people; at twenty he gathered bold men of the realm to attack and kill Zhan—Zhan's grand general Fan Xun then killed Chang and made himself king.
translations.idiomatic: At Man's death an infant named Chang was still at the breast among the people; at twenty he rallied warriors, killed Zhan, and was in turn killed by Zhan's grand general Fan Xun, who took the throne.

sentences.zh: 更繕治國內，起觀閣遊戲之，朝旦中晡三四見客。

translations.literal: He restored and governed the interior, raised pavilions for pleasure, and received guests three or four times from morning through midday to evening.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the realm, raised pleasure towers, and received guests three or four times from dawn through noon to dusk.

sentences.zh: 民人以焦蔗龜鳥爲禮。

translations.literal: The people take sugarcane, turtles, and birds as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The people offered sugarcane, turtles, and birds as tribute.

sentences.zh: 國法無牢獄。

translations.literal: National law has no prisons.
translations.idiomatic: The realm kept no prisons.

sentences.zh: 有罪者，先齋戒三日，乃燒斧極赤，令訟者捧行七步。

translations.literal: The guilty first fast three days; then an axe is heated white-hot and litigants are made to carry it seven paces.
translations.idiomatic: Accused persons fasted three days; then a white-hot axe was carried seven paces by the litigants.

sentences.zh: 又以金鐶、雞卵投沸湯中，令探取之，若無實者，手卽焦爛，有理者則不。

translations.literal: Gold rings and chicken eggs are also cast into boiling water for them to retrieve; if unjust, the hand chars at once; if justified, not so.
translations.idiomatic: Gold rings and eggs were also thrown into boiling water to be retrieved; the guilty hand charred instantly, the innocent did not.

sentences.zh: 又於城溝中養鰐魚，門外圈猛獸，有罪者，輒以喂猛獸及鰐魚，魚獸不食爲無罪，三日乃放之。

translations.literal: Crocodiles are kept in the moat, fierce beasts penned outside the gate; the guilty are fed to beasts and crocodiles—if fish and beasts will not eat, there is no guilt, and after three days they are released.
translations.idiomatic: Crocodiles filled the moat and fierce beasts the outer pen; the accused were thrown to them—if the animals refused the flesh, innocence was declared and release came after three days.

sentences.zh: 鰐大者長二丈餘，狀如鼉，有四足，喙長六七尺，兩邊有齒，利如刀劍，常食魚，遇得麞鹿及人亦噉之，蒼梧以南及外國皆有之。

translations.literal: Large crocodiles exceed two zhang; shaped like alligators, four-footed, snouts six or seven chi, teeth along both sides sharp as swords—they usually eat fish but also deer and people when encountered; south of Cangwu and in foreign lands they all have them.
translations.idiomatic: Great crocodiles reach more than two zhang, alligator-like on four feet, with six- or seven-chi snouts and sword-sharp teeth; they feed on fish but also take deer and men. They are found south of Cangwu and in foreign lands alike.

sentences.zh: 吳時，遣中郎康泰、宣化從事朱應使於尋國，國人猶裸，唯婦人著貫頭。

translations.literal: In Wu times envoys Palace Gentleman Kang Tai and Staff Officer for Local Reform Zhu Ying were sent to Xun's state; the people still went naked—only women wore neck-cut cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wu, Kang Tai and Zhu Ying were sent to Fan Xun's state; the people still went naked, save that women wore neck-cut cloth.

sentences.zh: 泰、應謂曰：「國中實佳，但人褻露可怪耳。

translations.literal: Tai and Ying said: "The land is truly fine, only the people's indecent exposure is strange.
translations.idiomatic: Tai and Ying said, "The country is excellent, but this nakedness is strange indeed.

sentences.zh: 」尋始令國內男子著橫幅。

translations.literal: " Xun then ordered men within the realm to wear hip cloths.
translations.idiomatic: " Xun then ordered the men to wear hip cloths.

sentences.zh: 橫幅，今干漫也。

translations.literal: Hip cloth is today's ganman.
translations.idiomatic: Hip cloth is what is now called ganman.

sentences.zh: 大家乃截錦爲之，貧者乃用布。

translations.literal: Great households cut brocade for it; the poor used plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families cut brocade for it; the poor used plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，跋摩復遣使送珊瑚佛像，幷獻方物。

translations.literal: In Tianjian year 2, Bamo again sent envoys bearing a coral Buddha image and presenting local goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjian, Bamo again sent envoys with a coral Buddha image and local tribute.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「扶南王憍陳如闍邪跋摩，介居海表，世纂南服，厥誠遠著，重譯獻賝。

translations.literal: Edict: "King of Funan, Kao Chenru Jieye Bamo, set apart beyond the sea, inheriting the southern domain through generations—his sincerity renowned afar, tribute brought through double translation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran: "Kao Chenru Jieye Bamo, King of Funan, stands apart beyond the sea, inheriting the southern realm through generations; his loyalty reaches from afar and his tribute comes through double translation.

sentences.zh: 宜蒙酬納，班以榮號。

translations.literal: He should receive reward and return gifts, and be granted an honored title.
translations.idiomatic: He should be rewarded and honored with a noble title.

sentences.zh: 可安南將軍、扶南王。」

translations.literal: Let him be General Who Pacifies the South and King of Funan."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be made General Who Pacifies the South and King of Funan."

sentences.zh: 今其國人皆醜黑，拳髮。

translations.literal: Now its people are all ugly and black, with curly hair.
translations.idiomatic: Its people today are dark and plain-featured, with curled hair.

sentences.zh: 所居不穿井，數十家共一池引汲之。

translations.literal: Where they dwell they dig no wells; several tens of households share one pool for drawing water.
translations.idiomatic: They sink no wells at home; dozens of households draw from a common pool.

sentences.zh: 俗事天神，天神以銅爲像，二面者四手，四面者八手，手各有所持，或小兒，或鳥獸，或日月。

translations.literal: They worship the Celestial God; images are cast in bronze—two-faced ones have four hands, four-faced ones eight hands, each holding something: sometimes a child, sometimes birds and beasts, sometimes sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: They worship the Celestial God in bronze images: two-faced gods have four hands, four-faced gods eight, bearing children, birds and beasts, or sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 其王出入乘象，嬪侍亦然。

translations.literal: The king going out or in rides an elephant; concubines and attendants do likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The king rides an elephant when he goes abroad, and so do his consorts and attendants.

sentences.zh: 王坐則偏踞翹膝，垂左膝至地，以白疊敷前，設金盆香爐於其上。

translations.literal: When the king sits he perches sideways with one knee raised, the left knee hanging to the ground; white cotton is spread before him and a gold basin and incense burner set upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Seated, the king perches sideways with one knee raised and the left knee to the ground; white cotton lies before him with a gold basin and censer upon it.

sentences.zh: 國俗，居喪則剃除鬚髮。

translations.literal: National custom: in mourning they shave beard and hair.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning they shave beard and hair by custom.

sentences.zh: 死者有四葬：水葬則投之江流，火葬則焚爲灰燼，土葬則瘞埋之，鳥葬則棄之中野。

translations.literal: The dead have four burials: water burial casts into rivers; fire burial burns to ash; earth burial inters; bird burial abandons in open wilds.
translations.idiomatic: The dead receive one of four rites: cast into rivers, burned to ash, buried in earth, or abandoned to the wild for birds.

sentences.zh: 人性貪吝，無禮義，男女恣其奔隨。

translations.literal: Human nature is greedy and stingy, without ritual propriety—men and women indulge their wanton couplings.
translations.idiomatic: The people are grasping and without propriety; men and women follow their desires freely.

sentences.zh: 先是，三年八月，高祖改造阿育王寺塔，出舊塔下舍利及佛爪髮。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the eighth month of year 3, Gaozu rebuilt the Ashoka Temple pagoda, removing from beneath the old pagoda relics and the Buddha's nail and hair.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the eighth month of the third year, Gaozu rebuilt the Ashoka Temple pagoda and took from beneath the old tower relics and the Buddha's nail and hair.

sentences.zh: 髮青紺色，衆僧以手伸之，隨手長短，放之則旋屈爲蠡形。

translations.literal: The hair was blue-black; when monks stretched it by hand it lengthened or shortened at will; released, it coiled spirally like a shell pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The hair was blue-black; monks could stretch it to any length at a touch, and when released it curled into a spiral shell pattern.

sentences.zh: 案《僧伽經》云：「佛髮青而細，猶如藕莖絲。

translations.literal: The Sangha Sutra says: "The Buddha's hair was blue and fine, like lotus-stem filament.
translations.idiomatic: The Sangha Sutra says, "The Buddha's hair was blue and fine as lotus-stem thread.

sentences.zh: 」《佛三昧經》云：「我昔在宮沐頭，以尺量髮，長一丈二尺，放已右旋，還成蠡文。

translations.literal: " The Buddha Samadhi Sutra says: "When I bathed my head in the palace I measured the hair with a ruler—one zhang two chi long; released, it spiraled rightward into a shell pattern.
translations.idiomatic: " The Buddha Samadhi Sutra says, "When I bathed my head in the palace I measured my hair at one zhang two chi; released, it spiraled rightward into a shell pattern.

sentences.zh: 」則與高祖所得同也。

translations.literal: " This matched what Gaozu obtained.
translations.idiomatic: " This matched what Gaozu had found.

sentences.zh: 阿育王卽鐵輪王，王閻浮提，一天下，佛滅度後，一日一夜，役鬼神造八萬四千塔，此卽其一也。

translations.literal: Ashoka was the Iron-Wheel King who ruled Jambudvipa and unified the realm; within a day and night after the Buddha's nirvana he employed ghosts and spirits to make eighty-four thousand pagodas—this was one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Ashoka was the Iron-Wheel King who ruled Jambudvipa and unified the world; within a day and night after the Buddha's nirvana he set ghosts and spirits to build eighty-four thousand pagodas—this was one.

sentences.zh: 吳時有尼居其地，爲小精舍，孫綝尋毀除之，塔亦同泯。

translations.literal: In Wu times a nun dwelled there in a small hermitage; Sun Chen soon destroyed it and the pagoda vanished likewise.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu a nun lived there in a small hermitage; Sun Chen destroyed it, and the pagoda perished with it.

sentences.zh: 吳平後，諸道人復於舊處建立焉。

translations.literal: After Wu was pacified, various monks rebuilt on the old site.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell, monks rebuilt on the old ground.

sentences.zh: 晉中宗初渡江，更脩飾之。

translations.literal: When Jin Emperor Zhongzong first crossed the Yangzi, it was again repaired and adorned.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Zhongzong first crossed the Yangzi, the site was repaired again.

sentences.zh: 至簡文咸安中，使沙門安法師程造小塔，未及成而亡，弟子僧顯繼而修立。

translations.literal: By Emperor Jianwen's Xian'an era a monk Fa An was sent to build a small pagoda; before it was finished he died, and disciple Seng Xian continued construction.
translations.idiomatic: By Jianwen's Xian'an reign Fa An was sent to build a small pagoda; he died before it was finished, and his disciple Seng Xian completed it.

sentences.zh: 至孝武太元九年，上金相輪及承露。

translations.literal: By Emperor Xiaowu's ninth year of Taiyuan, a gold dharmachakra finial and dew-collector were placed atop.
translations.idiomatic: By Xiaowu's ninth Taiyuan year a gold wheel finial and dew basin were set on top.

sentences.zh: 其後西河離石縣有胡人劉薩何遇疾暴亡，而心下猶暖，其家未敢便殯，經十日更蘇。

translations.literal: Later Liu Sahe, a barbarian of Lishi County in Xihe, suddenly died of illness yet his chest remained warm; the family dared not bury him, and after ten days he revived.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Sahe, a foreigner of Lishi in Xihe, died suddenly of illness, yet his chest stayed warm; the family delayed burial ten days until he revived.

sentences.zh: 說云：「有兩吏見錄，向西北行，不測遠近，至十八地獄，隨報重輕，受諸楚毒。

translations.literal: He said: "Two clerks seized my record and led me northwest—I knew not the distance—to eighteen hells, where according to the weight of retribution I suffered every torment.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Two clerks took my register and led me northwest to eighteen hells, where I suffered torments according to my deeds.

sentences.zh: 見觀世音語云：『汝緣未盡，若得活，可作沙門。

translations.literal: I saw Guanyin who said: 'Your karmic ties are not exhausted; if you live, become a monk.
translations.idiomatic: Guanyin appeared and said, 'Your fate is not yet spent; if you live, become a monk.

sentences.zh: 洛下、齊城、丹陽、會稽並有阿育王塔，可往禮拜。

translations.literal: Luoyang, Qicheng, Danyang, and Kuaiji all have Ashoka pagodas—you may go and worship.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang, Qicheng, Danyang, and Kuaiji all have Ashoka pagodas; go and worship there.

sentences.zh: 若壽終，則不墮地獄。

translations.literal: When your life ends, you will not fall into hell.'
translations.idiomatic: When your life ends, you will not fall into hell.'

sentences.zh: 』語竟，如墮高岩，忽然醒寤。

translations.literal: When the words ended, it was like falling from a high cliff—I woke suddenly."
translations.idiomatic: When the speech ended I seemed to fall from a cliff and woke at once."

sentences.zh: 」因此出家，名慧達。

translations.literal: " For this he left the household and took the name Huida.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he left the household and was called Huida.

sentences.zh: 遊行禮塔，次至丹陽，未知塔處，乃登越城四望，見長千里有異氣色，因就禮拜，果是阿育王塔所，屢放光明。

translations.literal: He traveled worshipping pagodas; next reaching Danyang, not knowing the pagoda's site, he climbed Yue city walls and looked four ways—saw over Changli li an unusual aura, went to worship, and it was indeed the Ashoka pagoda site, repeatedly emitting light.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled worshipping pagodas; reaching Danyang and not knowing where the pagoda stood, he climbed Yue city's walls and saw over Changli li a strange radiance; worshipping there, he found the Ashoka pagoda site, which often shone with light.

sentences.zh: 由是定知必有舍利，乃集衆就掘之，入一丈，得三石碑，並長六尺。

translations.literal: Hence he knew there must be relics; gathering a crowd he dug—one zhang deep—finding three stone tablets each six chi long.
translations.idiomatic: Sure then that relics lay below, he gathered men and dug one zhang down, finding three stone tablets each six chi long.

sentences.zh: 中一碑有鐵函，函中有銀函，函中又有金函，盛三舍利及爪髮各一枚，髮長數尺。

translations.literal: In one tablet was an iron casket, inside a silver casket, inside again a gold casket holding three relics and one nail and hair each—the hair several feet long.
translations.idiomatic: One tablet held an iron casket, within it silver, within that gold, containing three relics and one nail and one hair apiece; the hair was several feet long.

sentences.zh: 卽遷舍利近北，對簡文所造塔西，造一層塔。

translations.literal: The relics were moved northward; west of the pagoda Jianwen built, a one-story pagoda was erected.
translations.idiomatic: The relics were moved north and a one-story pagoda built west of the tower Jianwen had raised.

sentences.zh: 十六年，又使沙門僧尚伽爲三層，卽高祖所開者也。

translations.literal: In year 16 a monk Seng Shangjia was sent to make three stories—the one Gaozu opened.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the monk Seng Shangjia was ordered to build three stories—the tower Gaozu had opened.

sentences.zh: 初穿土四尺，得龍窟及昔人所舍金銀鐶釧釵鑷等諸雜寶物。

translations.literal: At first digging four chi of earth revealed a dragon grotto and various treasures earlier donors had placed—gold and silver rings, bracelets, hairpins, tweezers, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Digging four chi down first revealed a dragon grotto and gifts of gold and silver rings, bracelets, hairpins, tweezers, and other treasures left by earlier donors.

sentences.zh: 可深九尺許，方至石磉，磉下有石函，函內有鐵壺，以盛銀坩，坩內有金鏤罌，盛三舍利，如粟粒大，圓正光潔。

translations.literal: About nine chi deep one reached the stone foundation; beneath was a stone casket, inside an iron jar holding a silver tripod, inside a gold filigree jar holding three relics the size of millet grains—round, upright, lustrous.
translations.idiomatic: Some nine chi down they reached the stone base; beneath it lay a stone casket with an iron jar, a silver tripod within, and a gold filigree jar holding three round, bright relics the size of millet grains.

sentences.zh: 函內又有琉璃碗，內得四舍利及髮爪，爪有四枚，並爲沉香色。

translations.literal: Inside the casket was also a glass bowl containing four relics and hair and nails—four nails, all the color of agarwood.
translations.idiomatic: The casket also held a glass bowl with four relics, hair, and four nails, all the color of agarwood.

sentences.zh: 至其月二十七日，高祖又到寺禮拜，設無导大會，大赦天下。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh of that month Gaozu again came to the temple to worship, holding an unrestricted assembly and granting a great amnesty to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh of that month Gaozu returned to worship at the temple, held an unrestricted assembly, and proclaimed a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 是日，以金缽盛水泛舍利，其最小者隱缽不出，高祖禮數十拜，舍利乃於缽內放光，旋回久之，乃當缽中而止。

translations.literal: That day, relics were floated in water in a gold bowl; the smallest hid in the bowl and would not emerge—Gaozu bowed dozens of times until the relic glowed within the bowl, revolving long before settling in the bowl's center.
translations.idiomatic: That day relics were set afloat in a gold bowl of water; the smallest would not rise until Gaozu bowed many times, whereupon it glowed within the bowl, wheeling long before coming to rest.

sentences.zh: 高祖問大僧正慧念：「今日見不可思議事不？

translations.literal: Gaozu asked the Chief Sangha Master Huinian: "Today did you see something inconceivable?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu asked Chief Sangha Master Huinian, "Did you see anything inconceivable today?"

sentences.zh: 」慧念答曰：「法身常住，湛然不動。

translations.literal: Huinian answered: "The Dharma-body eternally abides, serene and unmoving."
translations.idiomatic: Huinian answered, "The Dharma-body eternally abides, serene and unmoving."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「弟子欲請一舍利還臺供養。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "Your disciple wishes to request one relic to return to the capital for veneration."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Your disciple would ask for one relic to take back to the capital for veneration."

sentences.zh: 」至九月五日，又於寺設無导大會，遣皇太子王侯朝貴等奉迎。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the ninth month another unrestricted assembly was held at the temple; the crown prince, princes, nobles, and court grandees were sent to welcome the relic.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the ninth month another unrestricted assembly was held at the temple, and the crown prince, princes, nobles, and court grandees were sent to welcome the relic.

sentences.zh: 是日，風景明和，京師傾屬，觀者百數十萬人。

translations.literal: That day the weather was bright and mild; the capital turned out en masse—over a million onlookers.
translations.idiomatic: That day the sky was clear and mild, and more than a million people in the capital came to look on.

sentences.zh: 所設金銀供具等物，並留寺供養，並施錢一千萬爲寺基業。

translations.literal: Gold and silver offerings and the like were all left at the temple for veneration, and ten million coins granted as the temple's endowment.
translations.idiomatic: The gold and silver offerings were left at the temple for worship, and ten million coins were granted as its endowment.

sentences.zh: 至四年九月十五日，高祖又至寺設無导大會，豎二刹，各以金罌，次玉罌，重盛舍利及爪髮，內七寶塔中。

translations.literal: By the fifteenth of the ninth month, year 4, Gaozu again held an unrestricted assembly at the temple, erecting two pagodas, each with gold jars, then jade jars, again holding relics and nail and hair within seven-jewel pagodas.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth of the ninth month in the fourth year Gaozu again held an unrestricted assembly, raised two pagodas, and placed relics and nail and hair in gold and jade jars within seven-jewel towers.

sentences.zh: 又以石函盛寶塔，分入兩刹下，及王侯妃主百姓富室所舍金、銀、鐶、釧等珍寶充積。

translations.literal: Stone caskets holding jewel pagodas were placed beneath the two pagodas; gold, silver, rings, bracelets, and other treasures donated by princes, consorts, nobles, commoners, and wealthy households piled in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Stone caskets with jewel pagodas went beneath the two towers, and gold, silver, rings, bracelets, and other treasures offered by princes, consorts, nobles, commoners, and the wealthy piled high.

sentences.zh: 十一年十一月二日，寺僧又請高祖于寺發《般若經》題，爾夕二塔俱放光明，敕鎮東將軍邵陵王綸制寺《大功德碑》文。

translations.literal: On the second of the eleventh month, year 11, temple monks invited Gaozu to expound the Prajna Sutra at the temple; that evening both pagodas together emitted light; the emperor ordered Eastern Pacification General Prince of Shaoling Lun to compose the temple's Great Merit Stele text.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the eleventh month in the eleventh year the monks invited Gaozu to open the Prajna Sutra at the temple; that night both pagodas shone, and the emperor ordered Eastern Pacification General Prince of Shaoling Lun to compose the Great Merit Stele.

sentences.zh: 先是，二年，改造會稽鄮縣塔，開舊塔出舍利，遣光宅寺釋敬脫等四僧及舍人孫照暫迎還台，高祖禮拜竟，卽送還縣，入新塔下，此縣塔亦是劉薩何所得也。

translations.literal: Earlier, in year 2, the pagoda at Yin County in Kuaiji was rebuilt; opening the old pagoda yielded relics—four monks including Jingtuo of Guangzai Temple and Palace Attendant Sun Zhao were sent to escort them temporarily to the capital; after Gaozu worshipped they were sent back to the county and placed beneath the new pagoda—this county pagoda too was what Liu Sahe discovered.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the second year, the Yin County pagoda in Kuaiji was rebuilt; opening the old tower yielded relics, and four monks including Jingtuo of Guangzai Temple and Palace Attendant Sun Zhao escorted them briefly to the capital; after Gaozu worshipped, they were returned to the county and placed under the new pagoda—the same pagoda Liu Sahe had found.

sentences.zh: 初，高悝得像後，西域胡僧五人來詣悝，曰：「昔於天竺得阿育王造像，來至鄴下，值胡亂，埋像于河邊，今尋覔失所。

translations.literal: At first, after Gao Ti obtained the image, five Western Region monk-barbarians came to Ti saying: "Long ago in India we obtained an Ashoka image; coming to Ye, we met barbarian turmoil and buried the image by the river—now we seek it and have lost the place.
translations.idiomatic: At first, after Gao Ti obtained the image, five Western monks came to him saying, "Long ago in India we acquired an Ashoka image; reaching Ye in barbarian turmoil, we buried it by the river, and now we cannot find the spot.

sentences.zh: 」五人嘗一夜俱夢見像曰：「已出江東，爲高悝所得。

translations.literal: " All five one night dreamed the image said: "It has already gone east of the Yangzi and is in Gao Ti's possession.
translations.idiomatic: " All five dreamed in one night that the image said, "It has already gone east of the Yangzi and is held by Gao Ti.

sentences.zh: 」悝乃送此五僧至寺，見像噓欷涕泣，像便放光，照燭殿宇。

translations.literal: " Ti then sent these five monks to the temple; seeing the image they sobbed and wept—the image at once emitted light illuminating the hall.
translations.idiomatic: " Ti sent the five monks to the temple; seeing the image they wept, and it at once shone with light throughout the hall.

sentences.zh: 又瓦官寺慧邃欲模寫像形，寺主僧尚慮虧損金色，謂邃曰：「若能令像放光，回身西向，乃可相許。

translations.literal: Also at Waguan Temple Hui Sui wished to copy the image's form; the abbot Seng Shang feared damaging the gold and said to Sui: "If you can make the image emit light and turn westward, then I may permit it.
translations.idiomatic: At Waguan Temple Hui Sui wished to copy the image; Abbot Seng Shang, fearing harm to the gilding, said, "If you can make the image shine and turn westward, then I will allow it.

sentences.zh: 」慧邃便懇到拜請，其夜像卽轉坐放光，回身西向，明旦便許模之。

translations.literal: " Hui Sui earnestly bowed and prayed; that night the image turned in its seat, emitted light, and faced west; at dawn permission was given to copy it.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui Sui prayed earnestly; that night the image turned in its seat, shone, and faced west, and at dawn copying was permitted.

sentences.zh: 像趺先有外國書，莫有識者，後有三藏𨚗求跋摩識之，云是阿育王爲第四女所造也。

translations.literal: On the image's pedestal were foreign characters none could read; later the Tripitaka master Qiubamo read them—saying Ashoka had made it for his fourth daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign script on the pedestal none could read until Tripitaka master Qiubamo deciphered it: Ashoka had made the image for his fourth daughter.

sentences.zh: 及大同中，出舊塔舍利，敕市寺側數百家宅地，以廣寺域，造諸堂殿並瑞像周回閤等，窮於輪奐焉。

translations.literal: By the Datong era, relics were taken from the old pagoda; an edict purchased several hundred households' dwelling lands beside the temple to expand the precinct, building halls and surrounding galleries with auspicious images—ornament beyond compare.
translations.idiomatic: In the Datong era relics were taken from the old pagoda; the throne bought several hundred neighboring houses to enlarge the temple, building halls, galleries, and auspicious images in unmatched splendor.

sentences.zh: 其圖諸經變，並吳人張繇運手。

translations.literal: Murals of sutra transformations were all the work of Wu artist Zhang You.
translations.idiomatic: Murals of sutra scenes were all painted by the Wu master Zhang You.

sentences.zh: 繇丹青之工，一時冠絕。

translations.literal: You's brushwork—none could match him in his time.
translations.idiomatic: In his day none surpassed Zhang You in the art of painting.

sentences.zh: 盤盤國

translations.literal: The State of Panpan
translations.idiomatic: Panpan

sentences.zh: 丹丹國

translations.literal: The State of Dandan
translations.idiomatic: Dandan

sentences.zh: 干陁利國

translations.literal: The State of Kandhari
translations.idiomatic: Kandhari

sentences.zh: 干陁利國，在南海洲上。

translations.literal: The State of Kandhari lies on isles in the South Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Kandhari stands on South Sea isles.

sentences.zh: 其俗與林邑、扶南略同。

translations.literal: Its customs are roughly the same as Linyi and Funan.
translations.idiomatic: Its customs largely match those of Linyi and Funan.

sentences.zh: 出班布、吉貝、檳榔，檳榔特好，爲諸國之極。

translations.literal: It produces patterned cloth, kapok, and betel nut; its betel nut is especially fine—the best among all the states.
translations.idiomatic: It exports patterned cloth, kapok, and betel; the betel is the finest in the region.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武世，王釋婆羅𨚗憐陁遣長史留陁獻金銀寶器。

translations.literal: In the Xiaowu reign of Song, King Jayabharata sent Chief Clerk Zhulutuo presenting gold, silver, and precious vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song Emperor Xiaowu, King Jayabharata sent Chief Clerk Zhulutuo with gold, silver, and treasure.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，其王瞿曇脩跋陁羅以四月八日夢見一僧，謂之曰：「中國今有聖主，十年之後，佛法大興。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian, King Gautama Vijayabhadra on the eighth day of the fourth month dreamed of a monk who told him: "China now has a sage ruler; in ten years the Buddhist Law will flourish greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year one, King Gautama Vijayabhadra dreamed on the eighth day of the fourth month that a monk said, "China has a sage king; in ten years the Dharma will rise.

sentences.zh: 汝若遣使貢奉敬禮，則土地豊樂，商旅百倍；

translations.literal: If you send envoys to offer tribute and show respect, then the land will be rich and joyful and merchants will multiply a hundredfold;
translations.idiomatic: If you send tribute and honor him, your land will prosper and trade will multiply a hundredfold;

sentences.zh: 若不信我，則境土不得自安。

translations.literal: if you do not believe me, your borders will not know peace.
translations.idiomatic: if you disbelieve me, your realm will know no peace.

sentences.zh: 」脩跋陁羅初未能信，旣而又夢此僧曰：「汝若不信我，當與汝往觀之。

translations.literal: " Vijayabhadra at first could not yet believe; then he dreamed again of this monk saying: "If you do not believe me, I shall take you to see for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: " At first Vijayabhadra did not believe; then the monk appeared again in a dream: "If you doubt me, I will take you to see.

sentences.zh: 」乃於夢中來至中國，拜覲天子。

translations.literal: " Then in the dream he came to China and paid homage to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " In the dream he traveled to China and bowed to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 旣覺，心異之。

translations.literal: When he awoke, his heart was stirred.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke, he was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 陁羅本工畫，乃寫夢中所見高祖容質，飾以丹青，仍遣使幷畫工奉表獻玉盤等物。

translations.literal: Vijayabhadra was skilled at painting; he painted Gaozu's appearance as seen in the dream, colored it, and sent envoys together with painters bearing a memorial and presenting a jade platter and other objects.
translations.idiomatic: A painter by trade, he set down Gaozu's likeness from the dream in color and sent envoys and painters with a memorial, a jade platter, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 使人旣至，模寫高祖形以還其國，比本畫則符同焉。

translations.literal: When the envoys arrived, they traced Gaozu's form to take back to their state—and compared with the original painting, it matched exactly.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys traced Gaozu's portrait to carry home; it matched the dream painting exactly.

sentences.zh: 因盛以寶函，日加禮敬。

translations.literal: They therefore stored it in a precious casket and daily added their reverence.
translations.idiomatic: They enshrined it in a jeweled casket and worshipped it daily.

sentences.zh: 後跋陁羅死，子毗邪跋摩立。

translations.literal: Later Vijayabhadra died, and his son Vijayavarman succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: After Vijayabhadra died, his son Vijayavarman rose.

sentences.zh: 十七年，遣長史毗員跋摩奉表曰：「常勝天子陛下：諸佛世尊，常樂安樂，六通三達，爲世間尊，是名如來。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Chief Clerk Vijayavarman sent a memorial saying: "Ever-victorious Son of Heaven Your Majesty: the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, ever delight in peace and joy, possess the six superknowledges and three knowledges, and are honored above the world—this is called the Tathagata.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen, Chief Clerk Vijayavarman memorialized: "Ever-victorious Son of Heaven: the World-Honored Buddhas delight in peace, hold the six and three knowledges, and are lords of the world—the Tathagata.

sentences.zh: 應供正覺，遺形舍利，造諸塔像，莊嚴國土，如須彌山。

translations.literal: Worthy of offerings, rightly enlightened, leaving behind bodily relics, building pagodas and images, adorning the realm like Mount Sumeru.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy of offerings and perfect enlightenment, he left relics and raised pagodas and images, adorning the land like Mount Sumeru.

sentences.zh: 邑居聚落，次第羅滿，城郭館宇，如忉利天宮。

translations.literal: Settlements and hamlets fill the land in ordered ranks; walls, lodges, and halls are like the Trayastrimsa Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Towns and villages fill the land in ranks; walls and palaces rise like the Heaven of Thirty-Three.

sentences.zh: 具足四兵，能伏怨敵。

translations.literal: Fully equipped with the four armies, able to subdue hostile foes.
translations.idiomatic: Four armies stand ready and enemies are subdued.

sentences.zh: 國土安樂，無諸患難，人民和善，受化正法，慶無不通。

translations.literal: The realm is secure and joyous, without disaster or hardship; the people are gentle and kind, receive and transform in the true Law—all blessings reach everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is safe and glad, free of woe; the people are gentle, ruled by the true Law, and blessed without end.

sentences.zh: 猶處雪山，流注雪水，八味清淨，百川洋溢，周回屈曲，順趨大海，一切衆生，咸得受用。

translations.literal: Like dwelling beside snowy mountains, where melting snow pours forth—eight pure flavors, a hundred streams overflowing, winding and bending, all flowing toward the great sea, and every living being alike receives and enjoys.
translations.idiomatic: Like snow mountains feeding pure streams that wind to the sea, so all beings drink their fill.

sentences.zh: 於諸國土，殊勝第一，是名震旦。

translations.literal: Among all lands it is uniquely supreme—this is called Zhendan.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme among lands—this is Zhendan.

sentences.zh: 大梁揚都天子，仁廕四海，德合天心，雖人是天，降生護世，功德寶藏，救世大悲，爲我尊生，威儀具足。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven of Great Liang at Yangdu, benevolent canopy over the four seas, virtue matching Heaven's heart—though human in form, born of Heaven to guard the world, a treasury of merit, great compassion saving the world, our venerated life, complete in dignified bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Great Liang's Son of Heaven at Yangdu spreads mercy over the four seas; though in human form he guards the world—a treasury of merit and compassion, our lord in full majesty.

sentences.zh: 是故至誠敬禮天子足下，稽首問訊。

translations.literal: Therefore with utmost sincerity we reverently bow at the Son of Heaven's feet and knock our heads to inquire after your health.
translations.idiomatic: With full sincerity we bow at your feet and beg after your health.

sentences.zh: 奉獻金芙蓉、雜香藥等，願垂納受。

translations.literal: We present golden hibiscus, mixed fragrant medicaments, and the like—may you graciously accept.
translations.idiomatic: We offer golden lotus, mixed incense, and more—may you accept them.

sentences.zh: 」普通元年，復遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putong, envoys were again sent presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong year one they again sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 狼牙脩國

translations.literal: The State of Lang-ya-xiu
translations.idiomatic: Lang-ya-xiu

sentences.zh: 狼牙脩國，在南海中。

translations.literal: The State of Lang-ya-xiu lies in the South Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Lang-ya-xiu stands in the South Sea.

sentences.zh: 其界東西三十日行，南北二十日行，去廣州二萬四千里。

translations.literal: Its borders run thirty days' journey east to west and twenty days north to south; it is twenty-four thousand li from Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: It spans thirty days' travel east-west and twenty north-south, twenty-four thousand li from Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 土氣物產與扶南略同，偏多𥴈沉婆律香等。

translations.literal: Climate and products resemble Funan, but especially abundant in agarwood, aloeswood, and borneol.
translations.idiomatic: Climate and products match Funan, but agarwood, aloeswood, and borneol are especially plentiful.

sentences.zh: 其俗男女皆袒而被髮，以吉貝爲干縵。

translations.literal: The custom is for men and women alike to bare their torsos and wear their hair loose, using kapok for waist-cloths.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women go bare-chested with loose hair, wearing kapok waist-wraps.

sentences.zh: 其王及貴臣乃加雲霞布覆胛，以金繩爲絡帶，金鐶貫耳。

translations.literal: The king and great ministers add cloud-brocade cloth over the shoulders, use gold cords for belts, and wear gold rings through the ears.
translations.idiomatic: Kings and nobles drape cloud-brocade over the shoulders, belt themselves with gold cord, and pierce the ears with gold rings.

sentences.zh: 女子則被布，以瓔珞繞身。

translations.literal: Women wrap in cloth, with strings of jewels around the body.
translations.idiomatic: Women wrap in cloth adorned with jeweled chains.

sentences.zh: 其國累磚爲城，重門樓閣。

translations.literal: The state piles brick to make walls, with layered gates, towers, and pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: They build brick walls with tiered gates, towers, and halls.

sentences.zh: 王出乘象，有幡毦旗鼓，罩白蓋，兵衛甚設。

translations.literal: When the king goes out he rides an elephant, with pennants of yak-tail, drums and flags, a white canopy, and strong guard formations.
translations.idiomatic: The king rides an elephant under white canopy, with yak-tail banners, drums, flags, and heavy guard.

sentences.zh: 國人說，立國以來四百餘年，後嗣衰弱，王族有賢者，國人歸之。

translations.literal: The people say that since the founding of the state four hundred-odd years ago, later descendants grew weak; when there was a worthy man among the royal clan, the people rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: They say the kingdom is four hundred years old; when the line weakened, a worthy prince drew the people to him.

sentences.zh: 王聞知，乃加囚執，其鏁無故自斷，王以爲神，因不敢害，乃斥逐出境，遂奔天竺，天竺妻以長女。

translations.literal: When the king learned of it, he had him imprisoned and bound; the lock broke for no reason—the king took this as divine and therefore dared not harm him, but expelled him beyond the border; he fled to Central Tianzhu, and Tianzhu gave him the eldest princess in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The king imprisoned him, but his chains broke untouched; taking it for a sign, the king banished him; he fled to Central Tianzhu and married the eldest princess.

sentences.zh: 俄而狼牙王死，大臣迎還爲王。

translations.literal: Before long the Lang-ya king died, and the ministers welcomed him back as king.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Lang-ya king died and ministers recalled him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 二十餘年死，子婆伽達多立。

translations.literal: After more than twenty years he died, and his son Bhagadatta succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty-odd years he died; his son Bhagadatta succeeded.

sentences.zh: 天監十四年，遣使阿撤多奉表曰：「大吉天子足下：離淫怒癡，哀愍衆生，慈心無量。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianjian, Envoy Ashade sent a memorial saying: "Great auspicious Son of Heaven at your feet: free from lust, anger, and folly, pitying all beings, boundless in compassionate heart.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian fourteen, Envoy Ashade memorialized: "Great auspicious Son of Heaven: free of lust, anger, and folly, pitying all beings with boundless compassion.

sentences.zh: 端嚴相好，身光明朗，如水中月，普照十方。

translations.literal: Solemn and fair of appearance, body bright and clear, like the moon in water, shining on all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Your bearing is solemn, your body luminous as the moon in water, shining everywhere.

sentences.zh: 眉間白毫，其白如雪，其色照曜，亦如月光。

translations.literal: The white tuft between the brows, white as snow, its color radiant, also like moonlight.
translations.idiomatic: The white tuft between your brows gleams like snow and moonlight.

sentences.zh: 諸天善神之所供養，以垂正法寶，梵行衆增，莊嚴都邑。

translations.literal: Worshipped by heaven's good spirits, spreading the treasure of the true Law, increasing hosts who uphold Brahma conduct, adorning the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's spirits worship you; the true Law spreads, the devout increase, and the capital is adorned.

sentences.zh: 城閣高峻，如乾陁山。

translations.literal: Walls and towers high and steep, like Mount Gandhamadana.
translations.idiomatic: Walls and towers rise steep as Gandhamadana.

sentences.zh: 樓觀羅列，道途平正。

translations.literal: Pavilions and belvederes arrayed in rows; roads and paths level and straight.
translations.idiomatic: Pavilions line the avenues; roads run straight and level.

sentences.zh: 人民熾盛，快樂安穩。

translations.literal: The people flourish; joy and security abound.
translations.idiomatic: The people flourish in joy and peace.

sentences.zh: 著種種衣，猶如天服。

translations.literal: Wearing many kinds of garments, like heavenly robes.
translations.idiomatic: They wear many robes like those of heaven.

sentences.zh: 於一切國，爲極尊勝。

translations.literal: Among all lands, supremely honored and victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme and victorious among all lands.
