sentences.zh: 天王愍念羣生，民人安樂，慈心深廣，律儀清淨，正法化治，供養三寶，名稱宣揚，佈滿世界，百姓樂見，如月初生。

translations.literal: The Heavenly King pities all living beings; the people secure and glad; compassionate heart deep and vast; discipline and rites pure and clear; governed by the true Law; offerings to the Three Treasures; fame proclaimed and spread, filling the world—the common folk delight to see him, like the new moon at its first rising.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's king pities all beings; the people live secure; compassion runs deep; discipline is pure; the Three Treasures are honored; his fame fills the world, and the people rejoice like at the new moon.

sentences.zh: 譬如梵王，世界之主，人天一切，莫不歸依。

translations.literal: Like Brahma, lord of the world—all human and divine beings alike take refuge.
translations.idiomatic: Like Brahma, lord of the world, to whom human and divine alike bow.

sentences.zh: 敬禮大吉天子足下，猶如現前，忝承先業，慶嘉無量。

translations.literal: We reverently bow at the feet of the great auspicious Son of Heaven, as though he stood before us; we inherit our predecessors' legacy—our rejoicing knows no bound.
translations.idiomatic: We bow to the great auspicious Son of Heaven as though he stood before us; inheriting our fathers' duty, our joy is boundless.

sentences.zh: 今遣使問訊大意。

translations.literal: We now send envoys to inquire after your great intent.
translations.idiomatic: We send envoys now to greet your will.

sentences.zh: 欲自往，復畏大海風波不達。

translations.literal: We wished to come ourselves, but again feared the wind and waves of the great sea would prevent arrival.
translations.idiomatic: We would come ourselves but fear the sea's storms.

sentences.zh: 今奉薄獻，願大家曲垂領納。」

translations.literal: We now present these slight offerings—may Your Majesty graciously bend to receive them."
translations.idiomatic: We offer these humble gifts—may you deign to accept."

sentences.zh: 婆利國

translations.literal: The State of Pali
translations.idiomatic: Pali

sentences.zh: 婆利國，在廣州東南海中洲上，去廣州二月日行。

translations.literal: The State of Pali lies on isles in the Southeast Sea east of Guangzhou; from Guangzhou it is two months' voyage.
translations.idiomatic: Pali lies on Southeast Sea isles east of Guangzhou, two months' sail away.

sentences.zh: 國界東西五十日行，南北二十日行。

translations.literal: The border runs fifty days' journey east to west and twenty days north to south.
translations.idiomatic: It spans fifty days' travel east-west and twenty north-south.

sentences.zh: 有一百三十六聚。

translations.literal: There are one hundred thirty-six settlements.
translations.idiomatic: It holds one hundred thirty-six settlements.

sentences.zh: 土氣暑熱，如中國之盛夏。

translations.literal: The climate is hot and humid, like midsummer in China.
translations.idiomatic: The air runs hot and humid as Chinese midsummer.

sentences.zh: 穀一歲再熟，草木常榮。

translations.literal: Grain ripens twice a year; grass and trees stay green year-round.
translations.idiomatic: Grain harvests twice; trees stay green year-round.

sentences.zh: 海出文螺、紫貝。

translations.literal: The sea yields patterned shells and purple cowries.
translations.idiomatic: The sea gives patterned shells and purple cowries.

sentences.zh: 有石名蚶貝羅，初采之柔軟，及刻削爲物幹之，遂大堅強。

translations.literal: There is a stone called han-beiluo; when first quarried it is soft, but when carved into objects and dried it becomes greatly hard and strong.
translations.idiomatic: A stone called han-beiluo is soft when quarried, yet carved and dried becomes very hard.

sentences.zh: 其國人披吉貝如帊，及爲都縵。

translations.literal: The people of the state wear kapok like a wrap, and also make it into skirt-cloths.
translations.idiomatic: People wear kapok as wraps and skirt-cloths.

sentences.zh: 王乃用班絲布，以瓔珞繞身，頭著金冠高尺餘，形如弁，綴以七寶之飾，帶金裝劍，偏坐金高坐，以銀蹬支足。

translations.literal: The king alone uses figured silk cloth, with strings of jewels around the body; on his head he wears a gold crown more than a foot high, shaped like a cap, inlaid with seven-jewel ornament; at his side a gold-hilted sword; he sits askew on a high gold seat, with silver stirrups supporting the feet.
translations.idiomatic: The king alone wears figured silk jeweled at the body, a foot-high gold crown shaped like a cap set with seven treasures, a gold-hilted sword at his side, seated sidewise on a gold throne with silver footrests.

sentences.zh: 侍女皆爲金花雜寶之飾，或持白毦拂及孔雀扇。

translations.literal: Attending women all bear ornament of golden flowers and mixed jewels, or hold white yak-tail whisks and peacock fans.
translations.idiomatic: Serving women wear gold flowers and mixed gems, or carry white yak-tail whisks and peacock fans.

sentences.zh: 王出，以象駕輿，輿以雜香爲之，上施羽蓋珠簾，其導從吹螺擊鼓。

translations.literal: When the king goes out, he rides an elephant-drawn carriage; the carriage is made of mixed incense, topped with feather canopy and pearl curtains; the escort blows conches and beats drums.
translations.idiomatic: The king rides an incense-wood carriage under feather canopy and pearl curtains, escorted by conches and drums.

sentences.zh: 王姓憍陳如，自古未通中國。

translations.literal: The royal surname is Kaccayana; from antiquity it had no contact with China.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house bears the name Kaccayana; until now it had not reached China.

sentences.zh: 問其先及年數，不能記焉，而言白淨王夫人卽其國女也。

translations.literal: Asked about its founders and the count of years, they could not record them; but they say the consort of King Suddhodana was a woman of this state.
translations.idiomatic: They cannot recall founders or years, but say the consort of King Suddhodana came from Pali.

sentences.zh: 天監十六年，遣使奉表曰：「伏承聖王信重三寶，興立塔寺，校飾莊嚴，周遍國土。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Tianjian, envoys sent a memorial saying: "We have heard that the sage king faith-reveres the Three Treasures, builds and raises pagodas and temples, adorns and makes solemn, everywhere throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian sixteen they memorialized: "We hear your sage king honors the Three Treasures, builds temples, and adorns the realm.

sentences.zh: 四衢平坦，清淨無穢；

translations.literal: The four thoroughfares are level, clean and without filth;
translations.idiomatic: Crossroads lie level and clean;

sentences.zh: 臺殿羅列，狀若天宮；

translations.literal: Terraces and halls arrayed in rows, shaped like heavenly palaces;
translations.idiomatic: Terraces and halls stand in rows like heavenly palaces;

sentences.zh: 壯麗微妙，世無與等。

translations.literal: Magnificent and subtle—none in the world equals them.
translations.idiomatic: Magnificent beyond compare in all the world.

sentences.zh: 聖主出時，四兵具足，羽儀導從，佈滿左右。

translations.literal: When the sage lord goes out, the four armies are complete; feathered insignia lead the escort, filling left and right.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage lord goes forth, four armies stand complete, insignia filling left and right.

sentences.zh: 都人士女，麗服光飾。

translations.literal: Capital gentlemen and ladies, in beautiful dress and luminous ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Capital men and women shine in splendid dress.

sentences.zh: 市廛豊富，充積珍寶。

translations.literal: Markets and shops rich and full, heaped with rare treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Markets overflow with rare treasure.

sentences.zh: 王法清整，無相侵奪。

translations.literal: Royal law is pure and ordered; none seize from one another.
translations.idiomatic: Royal law is clear and none rob another.

sentences.zh: 學徒皆至，三乘競集。

translations.literal: Students all arrive; the Three Vehicles compete to gather.
translations.idiomatic: Students flock in; the Three Vehicles crowd together.

sentences.zh: 敷說正法，雲布雨潤。

translations.literal: Expounding the true Law, like clouds spreading and rain moistening.
translations.idiomatic: The true Law is preached like clouds and rain.

sentences.zh: 四海流通，交會萬國。

translations.literal: The four seas flow together; ten thousand states meet in commerce.
translations.idiomatic: The four seas trade; ten thousand realms meet.

sentences.zh: 長江眇漫，清泠深廣。

translations.literal: The Long River stretches boundless, clear, cool, deep and vast.
translations.idiomatic: The Long River runs clear, deep, and vast.

sentences.zh: 有生咸資，莫能消穢。

translations.literal: All who live draw sustenance from it; none can defile it.
translations.idiomatic: All living things drink of it; none can soil it.

sentences.zh: 陰陽和暢，災厲不作。

translations.literal: Yin and yang are harmonious and mild; pestilence and calamity do not arise.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang stay mild; plague does not come.

sentences.zh: 大梁揚都聖王無等，臨覆上國，有大慈悲，子育萬民。

translations.literal: The sage king of Great Liang at Yangdu is without equal, overlooking the upper realm, with great compassion, nurturing ten thousand folk as children.
translations.idiomatic: Great Liang's sage king at Yangdu is peerless, overlooking the realm, nurturing all people with great compassion.

sentences.zh: 平等忍辱，怨親無二。

translations.literal: Equal in patience and forbearance; foe and kin are not two.
translations.idiomatic: Patient and forbearing alike to foe and friend.

sentences.zh: 加以周窮，無所藏積。

translations.literal: Moreover relieving the destitute—nothing hoarded in store.
translations.idiomatic: He relieves the poor and keeps no store.

sentences.zh: 靡不照燭，如日之明；

translations.literal: Nothing not illumined and warmed, like the sun's brightness;
translations.idiomatic: Nothing lies outside his light, bright as the sun;

sentences.zh: 無不受樂，猶如淨月。

translations.literal: none not receiving joy, like the pure moon.
translations.idiomatic: all receive joy like the clear moon.

sentences.zh: 宰輔賢良，羣臣貞信，盡忠奉上，心無異想。

translations.literal: Chancellors are worthy; ministers and officials are upright in faith, fully loyal in serving the court, without divergent thoughts in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors are wise, ministers faithful and wholly loyal without second thought.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝是我真佛，臣是婆利國主，今敬稽首禮聖王足下，惟願大王知我此心。

translations.literal: We humbly consider: the Emperor is our true Buddha; your servant is king of Pali; now we reverently knock our heads and bow at the sage king's feet—may the Great King know this heart of ours.
translations.idiomatic: We bow our heads: the Emperor is our true Buddha; I am king of Pali; I bow at your feet—know my heart.

sentences.zh: 此心久矣，非適今也。

translations.literal: This heart is long-standing, not only now.
translations.idiomatic: This heart is old, not new today.

sentences.zh: 山海阻遠，無緣自達，今故遣使獻金席等，表此丹誠。

translations.literal: Mountains and seas block the way—we could not reach you ourselves; therefore we now send envoys presenting golden mats and the like, declaring this red sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: Mountains and seas block us from coming; we send envoys with golden mats to show our sincere hearts."

sentences.zh: 」普通三年，其王頻伽復遣使珠貝智貢白鸚鵡、青蟲、兜鍪、琉璃器、吉貝、螺杯、雜香、藥等數十種。

translations.literal: In the third year of Putong, King Pinjia again sent Envoy Zhubeizhi presenting white parrots, green worms, helmets, glassware, kapok, shell cups, mixed incense, medicaments, and several dozen kinds besides.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong three, King Pinjia sent Envoy Zhubeizhi with white parrots, green worms, helmets, glassware, kapok, shell cups, mixed incense, drugs, and dozens more.

sentences.zh: 中天竺國

translations.literal: Central Tianzhu
translations.idiomatic: Central Tianzhu

sentences.zh: 中天竺國，在大月支東南數千里，地方三萬里，一名身毒。

translations.literal: Central Tianzhu lies several thousand li southeast of the Great Yuezhi; its territory is thirty thousand li square; it is also called Shendu.
translations.idiomatic: Central Tianzhu lies thousands of li southeast of the Great Yuezhi, thirty thousand li square, also called Shendu.

sentences.zh: 漢世張騫使大夏，見卭竹杖、蜀布，國人云，市之身毒。

translations.literal: In Han times Zhang Qian went as envoy to Daxia and saw Qiong bamboo staves and Shu cloth; the people of that country said they were bought in Shendu.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, Zhang Qian reached Daxia and saw Qiong staves and Shu cloth; locals said they came from Shendu.

sentences.zh: 身毒卽天竺，蓋傳譯音字不同，其實一也。

translations.literal: Shendu is Tianzhu—the sound differs in translation, but in fact they are one.
translations.idiomatic: Shendu is Tianzhu: the names differ in transmission but it is the same land.

sentences.zh: 從月支、高附以西，南至西海，東至槃越，列國數十，每國置王，其名雖異，皆身毒也。

translations.literal: From the Yuezhi and Gaofu westward, south to the Western Sea, east to Pan Yue—several dozen states in a row, each with its own king; though the names differ, all are Shendu.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuezhi and Gaofu west to the Western Sea and east to Pan Yue, dozens of kingdoms each with its own king—all Shendu under different names.

sentences.zh: 漢時羈屬月支，其俗土著與月支同，而卑濕暑熱，民弱畏戰，弱於月支。

translations.literal: In Han times it was subordinate to the Yuezhi; its custom is settled folk like the Yuezhi, but low, damp, and hot; the people are weak and fear battle—weaker than the Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: In Han it owed fealty to Yuezhi; like Yuezhi its people were settled, but the land is low, damp, and hot; the people are soft and fear war— weaker than Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 國臨大江，名新陶，源出昆侖，分爲五江，總名曰恒水。

translations.literal: The state borders a great river called Xintao; its source rises in Kunlun and divides into five streams, all together called the Heng River.
translations.idiomatic: The realm fronts a great river, Xintao—born on Kunlun, split into five branches, and known in sum as the Heng River.

sentences.zh: 其水甘美，下有真鹽，色正白如水精。

translations.literal: Its water is sweet and fine; beneath it lies true salt, pure white like crystal.
translations.idiomatic: The water tastes sweet and clear, and true salt lies below, white as crystal.

sentences.zh: 土俗出犀、象、貂、鼲、瑇瑁、火齊、金、銀、鐵、金縷織成、金皮罽、細摩白疊、好裘、毾㲪。

translations.literal: Local products include rhinoceros horn, elephant ivory, sable, beaver, tortoiseshell, fire-glass, gold, silver, iron, gold-thread weaving, gold-skinned felt, fine white cotton cloth, fine furs, and carpets.
translations.idiomatic: The land yields rhinoceros horn, ivory, sable, beaver pelts, tortoiseshell, fire-glass, gold, silver, iron, gold-thread brocade, gold-skinned felt, fine white cotton, good furs, and carpets.

sentences.zh: 火齊狀如雲母，色如紫金，有光耀，別之則薄如蟬翼，積之則如紗縠之重沓也。

translations.literal: Fire-glass looks like mica, its color like purple gold and luminous; split apart it is thin as a cicada's wing, piled up like layered gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Fire-glass resembles mica, purple-gold and bright; peeled thin as cicada wing, stacked like folds of gauze.

sentences.zh: 其西與大秦、安息交市海中，多大秦珍物--珊瑚、琥珀、金碧珠璣、琅玕、鬱金、蘇合。

translations.literal: To the west it trades on the sea with Da Qin and Parthia; many Da Qin treasures come—coral, amber, gold, green pearls, carnelian, turmeric, and storax.
translations.idiomatic: Westward it trades at sea with Rome and Parthia, and many Roman treasures arrive—coral, amber, gold, green pearls, carnelian, turmeric, and storax.

sentences.zh: 蘇合是合諸香汁煎之，非自然一物也。

translations.literal: Storax is made by boiling together the juices of many fragrant substances—it is not a single thing found in nature.
translations.idiomatic: Storax is distilled from many fragrant juices boiled together, not a single natural product.

sentences.zh: 又云大秦人采蘇合，先笮其汁以爲香膏，乃賣其滓與諸國賈人，是以輾轉來達中國，不大香也。

translations.literal: It is also said that Da Qin men gather storax by first pressing out the juice for fragrant paste, then sell the dregs to merchants of other lands; thus by many hands it reaches China, and is not very fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: Romans are said to press storax for fragrant paste first, then sell the leavings to foreign traders—so by the time it reaches China through many hands, much of the scent is gone.

sentences.zh: 鬱金獨出罽賓國，華色正黃而細，與芙蓉華里被蓮者相似。

translations.literal: Turmeric comes only from Kasmira; its blossoms are pure yellow and fine, resembling hibiscus flowers among lotus leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Turmeric grows only in Kasmira, its flowers bright yellow and delicate, like hibiscus among lotus pads.

sentences.zh: 國人先取以上佛寺，積日香槁，乃糞去之；

translations.literal: The people first take them to Buddhist temples; after days the blossoms wither and are removed as fertilizer;
translations.idiomatic: Locals first offer the flowers at temples; when they wilt after some days, the spent blossoms are cleared away as compost;

sentences.zh: 賈人從寺中徵雇，以轉賣與佗國也。

translations.literal: merchants hire men from the temples and resell them to other countries.
translations.idiomatic: and merchants hire temple workers to buy them up and sell them abroad.

sentences.zh: 漢桓帝延熹九年，大秦王安敦遣使自日南徼外來獻，漢世唯一通焉。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yanxi under Han Emperor Huan, King Andun of Da Qin sent envoys from beyond the Rinan frontier to offer tribute—the only contact in Han times.
translations.idiomatic: In Han Huan's ninth Yanxi year, King Andun of Rome sent envoys from beyond the Rinan border with tribute—the sole Han-era contact.

sentences.zh: 其國人行賈，往往至扶南、日南、交趾，其南徼諸國人少有到大秦者。

translations.literal: Their merchants often reach Funan, Rinan, and Jiaozhi; people of the southern frontier lands rarely reach Da Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Roman traders often reach Funan, Rinan, and Jiaozhi, but folk of the southern marches seldom travel as far as Rome.

sentences.zh: 孫權黃武五年，有大秦賈人字秦論來到交趾，交趾太守吳邈遣送詣權。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Huangwu under Sun Quan, a Da Qin merchant named Qin Lun came to Jiaozhi; Administrator Wu Miao of Jiaozhi sent him on to Quan.
translations.idiomatic: In Sun Quan's fifth Huangwu year, a Roman merchant called Qin Lun arrived at Jiaozhi, and Governor Wu Miao forwarded him to Quan.

sentences.zh: 權問方土謠俗，論具以事對。

translations.literal: Quan asked about local songs and customs; Lun answered in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: Quan questioned him about lands and customs, and Lun answered at length.

sentences.zh: 時諸葛恪討丹陽，獲黝、歙短人，論見之曰：「大秦希見此人。

translations.literal: At the time Zhuge Ke was campaigning against Danyang and captured short men of You and She; when Lun saw them he said, "Da Qin rarely sees people like this."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke was then campaigning in Danyang and had captured pygmies from You and She; Lun said, "Rome seldom sees men like these."

sentences.zh: 」權以男女各十人，差吏會稽劉咸送論，咸於道物故，論乃徑還本國。

translations.literal: Quan gave ten men and ten women; he dispatched the official Liu Xian of Kuaiji to escort Lun—Xian died on the road, and Lun went straight back to his own country.
translations.idiomatic: Quan gave him ten men and ten women and sent Kuaiji official Liu Xian to escort him home; Xian died en route, and Lun returned directly to his country.

sentences.zh: 漢和帝時，天竺數遣使貢獻，後西域反叛，遂絕。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor He of Han, Tianzhu sent envoys with tribute several times; later the Western Regions rebelled and contact ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han Emperor He, India sent tribute envoys several times; after the Western Regions rebelled, contact broke off.

sentences.zh: 至桓帝延熹二年、四年，頻從日南徼外來獻。

translations.literal: By the second and fourth years of Yanxi under Emperor Huan, they came frequently from beyond the Rinan frontier to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huan, in Yanxi 2 and 4, envoys again came often from beyond Rinan with tribute.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉世，絕不復通。

translations.literal: In Wei and Jin times contact never resumed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei and Jin, the route never reopened.

sentences.zh: 唯吳時扶南王范旃遣親人蘇物使其國，從扶南發投拘利口，循海大灣中正西北入歷灣邊數國，可一年餘到天竺江口，逆水行七千里乃至焉。

translations.literal: Only in Wu times did Funan King Fan Zhan send his kinsman Su Wu to that country; from Funan they put out at Jvli mouth, followed the great bay northwest, passed several countries along the bay's edge, and in a little over a year reached the mouth of Tianzhu's river; against the current they traveled seven thousand li before arriving.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Wu did Funan's King Fan Zhan send his kinsman Su Wu thither: from Funan they sailed from Jvli mouth, tracked the great gulf northwest past many coastal states, and in little over a year reached India's river mouth; seven thousand li upstream against the current brought them at last to port.

sentences.zh: 天竺王驚曰：「海濱極遠，猶有此人。

translations.literal: The Tianzhu king was astonished: "At the farthest edge of the sea, there are still people like this."
translations.idiomatic: The Indian king marveled, "At the sea's farthest rim, such men still exist."

sentences.zh: 」卽呼令觀視國內，仍差陳、宋等二人以月支馬四匹報旃，遣物等還，積四年方至。

translations.literal: He at once had them shown through the country, and also sent Chen and Song with four Yuezhi horses to report to Zhan; Su Wu and the others returned, and four years passed before they arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He had them toured through the realm and sent Chen and Song back to Zhan with four Yuezhi horses; Su Wu's party took four years to return.

sentences.zh: 其時吳遣中郎康泰使扶南，及見陳、宋等，具問天竺土俗，云：「佛道所興國也。

translations.literal: At that time Wu sent Attendant Kang Tai as envoy to Funan; when he saw Chen, Song, and the others he asked in full about Tianzhu customs, and they said, "It is the country where the Buddha-Dharma arose."
translations.idiomatic: Wu then sent Attendant Kang Tai to Funan; meeting Chen and Song, he questioned them closely on Indian ways, and they said, "That is the land where Buddhism arose."

sentences.zh: 人民敦厖，土地饒沃。

translations.literal: The people are honest and generous; the land is rich and fertile.
translations.idiomatic: Its people are plain and generous, its soil rich and well watered.

sentences.zh: 其王號茂論。

translations.literal: Their king is titled Maolun.
translations.idiomatic: The king bears the title Maolun.

sentences.zh: 所都城郭，水泉分流，繞于渠緌，下注大江。

translations.literal: The capital city's walls and moats—springs and streams divide and flow around irrigation channels, then descend into the great river.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, springs branch into channels that ring the walls and feed the great river below.

sentences.zh: 其宮殿皆雕文鏤刻，街曲市里，屋舍樓觀，鐘鼓音樂，服飾香華；

translations.literal: Palaces are all carved and inlaid; streets and lanes, houses and towers, bells and drums and music, dress and incense and flowers—
translations.idiomatic: Palaces are carved and inlaid; streets and markets, houses and towers, bells, drums, and music, dress, incense, and flowers abound;

sentences.zh: 水陸通流，百賈交會，奇玩珍瑋，恣心所欲。

translations.literal: water and land routes connect; merchants meet; rare treasures and fine objects are had at will.
translations.idiomatic: water and land trade freely, merchants throng, and rare wonders may be had for the asking.

sentences.zh: 左右嘉維、舍衛、葉波等十六大國，去天竺或二三千里，共尊奉之，以爲在天地之中也。」

translations.literal: To left and right are sixteen great countries such as Jiawei, Shewei, and Yabo, two or three thousand li from Tianzhu; all honor and serve it, taking themselves to stand at the center of heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen great realms—Jiawei, Shewei, Yabo, and others—lie two or three thousand li away yet all honor India as standing at the world's center.

sentences.zh: 天監初，其王屈多遣長史竺羅達奉表曰：「伏聞彼國據江傍海，山川周固，衆妙悉備，莊嚴國土，猶如化城。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianjian, King Quduo sent Chief Clerk Zhuluo Da with a memorial saying, "I have heard that your state rests by river and sea, its mountains and rivers secure on every side, every excellence complete, its realm solemn as a Buddha-field.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjian, King Quduo sent Chief Clerk Zhuluo Da with a memorial: "I hear your realm rests on river and sea, walled by mountains and rivers, complete in every excellence, solemn as a pure Buddha-land.

sentences.zh: 宮殿莊飾，街巷平坦，人民充滿，歡娛安樂。

translations.literal: Palaces are stately and adorned; streets and lanes are level; the people fill the land, rejoicing in ease and delight.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces stand adorned, streets lie level, and the people fill the land in joy and peace.

sentences.zh: 大王出遊，四兵隨從，聖明仁愛，不害衆生。

translations.literal: When the Great King goes abroad, the four armies follow; he is sage and humane and harms no living being.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great King rides abroad, the four hosts attend; sage and humane, he harms no living thing.

sentences.zh: 國中臣民，循行正法，大王仁聖，化之以道，慈悲羣生，無所遺棄。

translations.literal: Within the state ministers and people all follow the upright Law; the Great King, sage and humane, transforms them with the Way, compassionate to all beings, abandoning none.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and people keep the true Law; the Great King, sage and humane, transforms them by the Way, compassionate to all, leaving none behind.

sentences.zh: 常修淨戒，式導不及，無上法船，沉溺以濟。

translations.literal: He ever keeps pure precepts, guides those not yet reached, and launches the supreme Dharma-ship to ferry the drowning.
translations.idiomatic: He keeps pure precepts, guides the unreached, and sends forth the supreme Dharma-ship to save the drowning.

sentences.zh: 百官氓庶，受樂無恐。

translations.literal: Officials and common folk receive joy without fear.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners live in joy without dread.

sentences.zh: 諸天護持，萬神侍從，天魔降服，莫不歸仰。

translations.literal: Heavenly hosts protect him; myriad spirits attend; heavenly demons are subdued—all turn toward him in reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly hosts guard him, myriad spirits attend, heavenly demons bow—all revere him.

sentences.zh: 王身端嚴，如日初出，仁澤普潤，猶如大雲，於彼震旦，最爲殊勝。

translations.literal: The King's person is upright and solemn, like the sun at first rising; his benevolent dew broadly moistens, like a great cloud—among the lands of Zhendan he is most surpassing.
translations.idiomatic: The King's bearing is upright as the newly risen sun; his grace spreads like a great cloud—in all the lands of China, none surpass him.

sentences.zh: 臣之所住國土，首羅天守護，令國安樂。

translations.literal: In the country where your servant dwells, Shakra guards the realm and keeps the state secure and glad.
translations.idiomatic: In my own land Shakra guards the realm and keeps it safe and glad.

sentences.zh: 王王相承，未曾斷絕。

translations.literal: Kings have succeeded kings without break.
translations.idiomatic: Kings have followed kings without interruption.

sentences.zh: 國中皆七寶形像，衆妙莊嚴，臣自修檢，如化王法。

translations.literal: Throughout the state are images of the seven treasures, all finely adorned; your servant has disciplined himself like a Buddha-king in the Law.
translations.idiomatic: The land holds seven-jewel images, finely adorned; I have disciplined myself as a Buddha-king in the Law.

sentences.zh: 臣名屈多，奕世王種。

translations.literal: Your servant is named Quduo, of a royal line for generations.
translations.idiomatic: I am Quduo, of royal blood for generations.

sentences.zh: 惟願大王，聖體和平。

translations.literal: I only pray the Great King's sacred person be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: I pray only that the Great King's sacred person be at peace.

sentences.zh: 今以此國羣臣民庶，山川珍重，一切歸屬，五體投地，歸誠大王。

translations.literal: Now I offer this state's ministers, people, mountains, and treasures—all to belong to you; I cast myself down in the five prostrations and return my heart to the Great King.
translations.idiomatic: Now I offer this realm's ministers, people, mountains, and treasures—all to your rule; I prostrate myself and give my heart to the Great King.

sentences.zh: 使人竺達多由來忠信，是故今遣。

translations.literal: The envoy Zhuluo Da has long been loyal and trustworthy; therefore I send him now.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy Zhuluo Da has ever been loyal and true; therefore I send him now.

sentences.zh: 大王若有所須珍奇異物，悉當奉送。

translations.literal: If the Great King should need any rare or wondrous thing, I shall send it all.
translations.idiomatic: Should the Great King desire any rare or wondrous thing, I shall send all you require.

sentences.zh: 此之境土，便是大王之國；

translations.literal: This land is itself the Great King's realm;
translations.idiomatic: this land is itself the Great King's realm;

sentences.zh: 王之法令善道，悉當承用。

translations.literal: the King's laws and good Way—I shall all receive and use.
translations.idiomatic: your laws and good Way I shall receive and follow.

sentences.zh: 願二國信使往來不絕。

translations.literal: May envoys of the two states come and go without cease.
translations.idiomatic: May envoys of our two realms pass without cease.

sentences.zh: 此信返還，願賜一使，具宣聖命，備敕所宜。

translations.literal: When this letter returns, I pray you grant one envoy to proclaim the sacred command and instruct what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: When this letter returns, grant an envoy to proclaim your sacred command and teach what is fitting.

sentences.zh: 款至之誠，望不空返，所白如允，願加採納。

translations.literal: The sincerity of this greeting—I pray it not return empty; if what I report is acceptable, I pray you receive it.
translations.idiomatic: This greeting comes in full sincerity; may it not return unanswered; if what I say is acceptable, I pray you receive it.

sentences.zh: 今奉獻琉璃唾壺、雜香、吉貝等物。」

translations.literal: Now I present glass spittoons, mixed incense, kapok cloth, and other things."
translations.idiomatic: Now I present glass spittoons, mixed incense, kapok cloth, and other gifts."

sentences.zh: 師子國

translations.literal: Lion Country
translations.idiomatic: Lion Country

sentences.zh: 師子國，天竺旁國也。

translations.literal: Lion Country is a neighboring state of Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Lion Country lies beside India.

sentences.zh: 其地和適，無冬夏之異。

translations.literal: Its land is temperate; there is no difference between winter and summer.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is mild; winter and summer scarcely differ.

sentences.zh: 五穀隨人所種，不須時節。

translations.literal: The five grains follow whatever men plant; seasons need not be observed.
translations.idiomatic: The five grains grow whenever men sow them; no season need be kept.

sentences.zh: 其國舊無人民，止有鬼神及龍居之。

translations.literal: The country originally had no people—only ghosts and spirits and dragons dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: Once the land had no people; only ghosts, spirits, and dragons lived there.

sentences.zh: 諸國商估來共市易，鬼神不見其形，但出珍寶，顯其所堪價，商人依價取之。

translations.literal: Merchants of many lands came to trade together; the ghosts and spirits showed no form, but set out treasures and named the price they would accept; merchants took goods according to the price.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants of many lands came to trade; the spirits stayed unseen, set out treasures, and marked the price; traders took goods for the price named.

sentences.zh: 諸國人聞其土樂，因此競至，或有停住者，遂成大國。

translations.literal: When people of many lands heard the land was pleasant, they raced to come; some stayed, and it gradually became a great country.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the land was pleasant, men raced thither; some remained, and it grew into a great realm.

sentences.zh: 晉義熙初，始遣獻玉像，經十載乃至。

translations.literal: At the start of Yixi under Jin, they first sent a jade Buddha-image; ten years passed before it arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jin Yixi they first sent a jade Buddha-image; ten years passed before it arrived.

sentences.zh: 像高四尺二寸，玉色潔潤，形制殊特，殆非人工。

translations.literal: The image was four chi two cun in height; the jade was lustrous and moist, its form extraordinary—hardly the work of human hands.
translations.idiomatic: The image stood four chi two cun tall; the jade glowed moist and bright, its form beyond ordinary craft.

sentences.zh: 此像歷晉、宋世在瓦官寺，寺先有徵士戴安道手制佛像五軀，及顧長康維摩畫圖，世人謂爲三絕。

translations.literal: This image through Jin and Song stood in Waguan Temple; the temple already had five Buddha-images made by the hand of Recluse Dai Andao and Gu Kaizhi's painting of Vimalakirti—men of the age called them the three supreme works.
translations.idiomatic: Through Jin and Song the image stood in Waguan Temple, which already held five Buddha-images by Recluse Dai Andao and Gu Kaizhi's Vimalakirti—called the age's three supreme works.

sentences.zh: 至齊東昏，遂毀玉像，前截臂，次取身，爲嬖妾潘貴妃作釵釧。

translations.literal: By the Dong Hun of Qi it was destroyed—the jade image first had its arms cut off, then its body taken, to make hairpins and bracelets for the favorite concubine Pan Guifei.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi's Dong Hun the image was destroyed—arms cut first, then the body taken to make hairpins and bracelets for concubine Pan Guifei.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉六年、十二年，其王刹利摩訶遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the sixth and twelfth years of Yuanjia under Song, King Shakramati sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Song Yuanjia 6 and 12, King Shakramati sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 東夷諸戎

translations.literal: Eastern Yi and Various Rong
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yi and Various Rong

sentences.zh: 東夷之國，朝鮮爲大，得箕子之化，其器物猶有禮樂云。

translations.literal: Among the states of the Eastern Yi, Korea is greatest; it received Gija's transformation, and its vessels still preserve ritual and music, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Eastern Yi, Korea is greatest; civilized by Gija, its vessels still keep ritual and music, they say.

sentences.zh: 魏時，朝鮮以東馬韓、辰韓之屬，世通中國。

translations.literal: In Wei times, east of Korea the Ma Han, Jin Han, and the like communicated with China generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei, Ma Han, Jin Han, and others east of Korea traded with China generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 自晉過江，泛海東使，有高句驪、百濟，而宋、齊間常通職貢。

translations.literal: After Jin crossed the Yangzi, sea envoys eastward included Goguryeo and Baekje; under Song and Qi they often sent tribute and office.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin crossed the river, Goguryeo and Baekje sent sea envoys; under Song and Qi they often paid tribute.

sentences.zh: 梁興，又有加焉。

translations.literal: When Liang rose, there was increase still.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang arose, contact increased further.

sentences.zh: 扶桑國，在昔未聞也。

translations.literal: Fusang Country—in former times it was unheard of.
translations.idiomatic: Fusang—in former times none had heard of it.

sentences.zh: 普通中，有道人稱自彼而至，其言元本尤悉，故幷錄焉。

translations.literal: In the Putong era a monk claimed to have come from there; his original account was especially thorough, and so it is recorded together here.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong a monk claimed to come from there; his account was unusually full, and so it is recorded here.

sentences.zh: 高句驪

translations.literal: Goguryeo
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo

sentences.zh: 高句驪者，其先出自東明。

translations.literal: The Goguryeo people trace their origin to Dongming.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo traces its origin to Dongming.

sentences.zh: 東明本北夷橐離王之子。

translations.literal: Dongming was originally the son of the Turo king of the Northern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Dongming was son of the Northern Yi king of Turo.

sentences.zh: 離王出行，其侍兒於後任娠，離王還，欲殺之。

translations.literal: The king went abroad; behind him his serving maid became pregnant; when the king returned he wished to kill her.
translations.idiomatic: The king went abroad; a serving maid conceived in his absence; on his return he meant to kill her.

sentences.zh: 侍兒曰：「前見天上有氣如大雞子，來降我，因以有娠。

translations.literal: The serving maid said, "Before this I saw qi in the sky like a great hen's egg descend upon me, and thus I became pregnant."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "I saw sky-qi like a great egg descend on me, and so I conceived."

sentences.zh: 」王囚之，後遂生男。

translations.literal: The king imprisoned her; afterward she bore a boy.
translations.idiomatic: The king imprisoned her; later she bore a son.

sentences.zh: 王置之豕牢，豕以口氣噓之，不死，王以爲神，乃聽收養。

translations.literal: The king put him in a pigsty; the pigs breathed on him with their breath and he did not die; the king thought him divine and allowed him to be raised.
translations.idiomatic: The king cast him into a pigsty; pigs breathed on him and he lived; the king took him for divine and let him be reared.

sentences.zh: 長而善射，王忌其猛，復欲殺之，東明乃奔走，南至淹滯水，以弓擊水，魚鱉皆浮爲橋，東明乘之得渡，至夫餘而王焉。

translations.literal: Grown, he was skilled at archery; the king feared his fierceness and wished to kill him again; Dongming fled south to Yanchi Water, shot the water with his bow, and fish and turtles all floated up to form a bridge; Dongming crossed and reached Buyeo, where he became king.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he excelled at archery; the king feared his fierceness and sought his life again; Dongming fled south to Yanchi Water, shot the stream, and fish and turtles rose to form a bridge; he crossed, reached Buyeo, and became king.

sentences.zh: 其後支別爲句驪種也。

translations.literal: Later a branch separated off as the Goguryeo clan.
translations.idiomatic: Later a branch split away as the Goguryeo clan.

sentences.zh: 其國，漢之玄菟郡也，在遼東之東，去遼東千里。

translations.literal: Its country was Han's Xuantu commandery, east of Liaodong, a thousand li from Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Its realm was Han's Xuantu commandery, east of Liaodong, a thousand li from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏世，南與朝鮮、穢貃，東與沃沮，北與夫餘接。

translations.literal: In Han and Wei times it bordered Korea and the Hui tribes to the south, Wolu to the east, and Buyeo to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han and Wei it touched Korea and the Hui southward, Wolu eastward, and Buyeo northward.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝元封四年，滅朝鮮，置玄菟郡，以高句驪爲縣以屬之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuannfeng under Han Emperor Wu, Korea was destroyed and Xuantu commandery was established; Goguryeo was made a county under it.
translations.idiomatic: In Han Wu's fourth Yuannfeng year Korea fell, Xuantu commandery was set up, and Goguryeo was made a county under it.

sentences.zh: 句驪地方可二千里，中有遼山，遼水所出。

translations.literal: Goguryeo territory was about two thousand li; within it is Liaoshan, whence the Liaoshui flows.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo covered some two thousand li; Liaoshan rises there, source of the Liaoshui.

sentences.zh: 其王都於丸都之下，多大山深谷，無原澤，百姓依之以居，食澗水。

translations.literal: The king's capital lay below Wandu; there were many great mountains and deep valleys, no plains or marshes; the people lived along the slopes and drank stream water.
translations.idiomatic: The king's seat lay below Wandu amid great mountains and deep valleys without plains; people clung to the slopes and drank from streams.

sentences.zh: 雖土著，無良田，故其俗節食。

translations.literal: Though settled, they had no good farmland; therefore their custom was to eat sparingly.
translations.idiomatic: Though settled, they lacked good fields; so their custom was frugal eating.

sentences.zh: 好治宮室，于所居之左立大屋，祭鬼神，又祠零星、社稷。

translations.literal: They liked to build palaces; to the left of where they dwelt they raised a great hall to sacrifice to ghosts and spirits, and also worshipped the scattered stars and the soil-altar.
translations.idiomatic: They loved grand buildings; left of each dwelling stood a hall for ghost and spirit sacrifice, and for worship of scattered stars and the soil-altar.

sentences.zh: 人性凶急，喜寇抄。

translations.literal: By nature they were fierce and hasty, fond of raiding and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and hasty by nature, they loved raiding and plunder.

sentences.zh: 其官，有相加、對盧、沛者、古鄒加、主簿、優臺、使者、皁衣先人，尊卑各有等級。

translations.literal: Their offices included xiangjia, duilu, peizhe, guzoujia, chief clerk, youtai, envoy, and zaoyi elder—high and low each had rank.
translations.idiomatic: Offices included xiangjia, duilu, peizhe, guzoujia, chief clerk, youtai, envoy, and zaoyi elder—each rank had its place.

sentences.zh: 言語諸事，多與夫餘同，其性氣、衣服有異。

translations.literal: In speech and affairs they mostly resembled Buyeo; in temperament and dress they differed.
translations.idiomatic: Speech and custom mostly matched Buyeo; temperament and dress differed.

sentences.zh: 本有五族，有消奴部、絕奴部、慎奴部、雚奴部、桂婁部。

translations.literal: Originally there were five clans: the Xiaonu, Juenu, Shennu, Huannu, and Guilou.
translations.idiomatic: Five clans originally ruled: Xiaonu, Juenu, Shennu, Huannu, and Guilou.

sentences.zh: 本消奴部爲王，微弱，桂婁部代之。

translations.literal: Originally the Xiaonu clan held kingship; weakened, the Guilou clan replaced them.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Xiaonu clan held the throne; when they weakened, the Guilou clan replaced them.

sentences.zh: 漢時賜衣幘、朝服、鼓吹，常從玄菟郡受之。

translations.literal: In Han times they were granted clothes, caps, court dress, and music; they regularly received these from Xuantu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Han granted them clothes, caps, court dress, and music; they received these regularly from Xuantu commandery.

sentences.zh: 後稍驕，不復詣郡，但於東界築小城以受之，至今猶名此城爲幘溝婁。

translations.literal: Later they grew gradually arrogant and no longer went to the commandery; they only built a small city on the eastern border to receive the gifts—and to this day that city is called Ze-gou Lou.
translations.idiomatic: Later they grew proud and ceased visiting the commandery, building only a small border town to receive gifts—still called Ze-gou Lou.

sentences.zh: 「溝婁」者，句驪名「城」也。

translations.literal: "Gou Lou" is the Goguryeo word for "city."
translations.idiomatic: "Gou Lou" means "city" in Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 其置官，有對盧則不置沛者，有沛者則不置對盧。

translations.literal: In appointing offices, if there is a duilu there is no peizhe; if there is a peizhe there is no duilu.
translations.idiomatic: In office, duilu and peizhe are not appointed together—where one stands, the other is omitted.

sentences.zh: 其俗喜歌儛，國中邑落男女，每夜羣聚歌戲。

translations.literal: Their custom loves song and dance; in settlements throughout the state, men and women each night gather in groups to sing and play.
translations.idiomatic: They love song and dance; in every settlement men and women gather nightly to sing and play.

sentences.zh: 其人潔清自喜，善藏釀，跪拜申一腳，行步皆走。

translations.literal: The people are clean and self-pleasing, skilled at brewing liquor; in bowing they extend one foot; in walking and in steps they always run.
translations.idiomatic: They are fastidious and proud of cleanliness, skilled at brewing; they kowtow on one foot and walk and run at a trot.

sentences.zh: 以十月祭天大會，名曰「東明」。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they hold a great assembly to sacrifice to Heaven, called "Dongming."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they hold a great heaven-sacrifice called "Dongming."

sentences.zh: 其公會衣服，皆錦繡金銀以自飾。

translations.literal: At public assemblies their clothes are all brocade and gold and silver for self-adornment.
translations.idiomatic: At public assemblies all dress in brocade and gold and silver adornment.

sentences.zh: 大加、主簿頭所著似幘而無後；

translations.literal: The great xiang and the chief clerk wear on the head something like a cap but without a back;
translations.idiomatic: Great xiang and chief clerks wear headgear like a cap but without a back;

sentences.zh: 其小加著折風，形如弁。

translations.literal: Lesser xiang wear zhefeng, shaped like a bian cap.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser xiang wear zhefeng caps shaped like court bian.

sentences.zh: 其國無牢獄，有罪者，則會諸加評議殺之，沒入妻子。

translations.literal: The state has no prisons; when someone is guilty, the various xiang assemble to discuss and execute him, and his wife and children are confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: There are no prisons; the guilty are judged in council by the xiang and put to death, their wives and children seized.

sentences.zh: 其俗好淫，男女多相奔誘。

translations.literal: Their custom favors licentiousness; men and women often elope and seduce one another.
translations.idiomatic: They are licentious by custom; men and women often run off together in mutual seduction.

sentences.zh: 已嫁娶，便稍作送終之衣。

translations.literal: Once married, they soon make slight preparations for burial garments.
translations.idiomatic: After marriage they quickly begin preparing modest burial clothes.

sentences.zh: 其死葬，有槨無棺。

translations.literal: In death and burial, they have outer coffins but no inner coffins.
translations.idiomatic: The dead are buried in outer coffins without inner coffins.

sentences.zh: 好厚葬，金銀財幣盡於送死。

translations.literal: They favor lavish burial; gold, silver, and currency are all spent on the dead.
translations.idiomatic: They love lavish funerals and pour gold, silver, and coin into the dead.

sentences.zh: 積石爲封，列植松柏。

translations.literal: They pile stones for the tomb mound and plant pine and cypress in rows.
translations.idiomatic: Stone mounds mark the graves, with pine and cypress planted in rows.

sentences.zh: 兄死妻嫂。

translations.literal: When an elder brother dies, the younger brother takes the widow as wife.
translations.idiomatic: A younger brother takes his dead elder brother's widow as wife.

sentences.zh: 其馬皆小，便登山。

translations.literal: Their horses are all small, suited for climbing mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Their horses are small and nimble on mountain paths.

sentences.zh: 國人尚氣力，便弓矢刀矛。

translations.literal: The people value physical strength and are skilled with bow, arrow, blade, and spear.
translations.idiomatic: The people honor strength and excel with bow, arrow, blade, and spear.

sentences.zh: 有鎧甲，習戰鬬，沃沮、東穢皆屬焉。

translations.literal: They have armor and practice warfare; Wolu and Eastern Hui all belong to them.
translations.idiomatic: They wear armor and train for battle; Wolu and Eastern Hui are subject to them.

sentences.zh: 王莽初，發高驪兵以伐胡，不欲行，強迫遣之，皆亡出塞爲寇盜。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wang Mang's reign, Goguryeo troops were levied to campaign against the Hu; unwilling to go, they were forcibly dispatched, then all fled beyond the frontier and became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wang Mang's reign Goguryeo soldiers were drafted against the Hu; forced to march, they fled beyond the passes and turned to raiding.

sentences.zh: 州郡歸咎於句驪侯騶，嚴尤誘而斬之，王莽大悅，更名高句驪爲下句驪，當此時爲侯矣。

translations.literal: The provinces and commanderies blamed Marquis Zou of Goguryeo; Yan You lured and beheaded him; Wang Mang was greatly pleased and renamed Goguryeo to Lower Goguryeo—at this time it was a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces blamed Marquis Zou of Goguryeo; Yan You tricked and killed him; Wang Mang rejoiced and renamed the realm Lower Goguryeo—it was a marquisate then.

sentences.zh: 光武八年，高句驪王遣使朝貢，始稱王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Guangwu, the king of Goguryeo sent envoys with tribute and first styled himself king.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangwu eight the Goguryeo king sent tribute envoys and first took the title of king.

sentences.zh: 至殤、安之間，其王名宮，數寇遼東，玄菟太守蔡風討之不能禁。

translations.literal: Between the reigns of Shang and An, their king was named Gong; he repeatedly raided Liaodong; Administrator Cai Feng of Xuantu campaigned against him but could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shang and An, King Gong raided Liaodong again and again; Xuantu Administrator Cai Feng could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 宮死，子伯固立。

translations.literal: Gong died; his son Bogu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Gong died and his son Bogu took the throne.

sentences.zh: 順、和之間，復數犯遼東寇抄。

translations.literal: Between Shun and He, they again repeatedly violated Liaodong with raids.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shun and He they again and again raided Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 靈帝建寧二年，玄菟太守耿臨討之，斬首虜數百級，伯固乃降屬遼東。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianning under Emperor Ling, Administrator Geng Lin of Xuantu campaigned; hundreds of heads and captives were taken; Bogu then surrendered and submitted to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In Ling's Jianning two, Xuantu Administrator Geng Lin attacked, took hundreds of heads and captives, and Bogu surrendered to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 公孫度之雄海東也，伯固與之通好。

translations.literal: When Gongsun Du dominated the eastern sea, Bogu maintained friendly relations with him.
translations.idiomatic: While Gongsun Du held sway over the eastern sea, Bogu kept friendly ties with him.

sentences.zh: 伯固死，子伊夷摸立。

translations.literal: Bogu died; his son Yiyimo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Bogu died and his son Yiyimo succeeded.

sentences.zh: 伊夷摸自伯固時已數寇遼東，又受亡胡五百餘戶。

translations.literal: Yiyimo had already repeatedly raided Liaodong since Bogu's time, and also received over five hundred households of fugitive Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Since Bogu's day Yiyimo had raided Liaodong often and sheltered more than five hundred fugitive Hu households.

sentences.zh: 建安中，公孫康出軍擊之，破其國，焚燒邑落，降胡亦叛伊夷摸，伊夷摸更作新國。

translations.literal: In the Jian'an era, Gongsun Kang marched out and attacked; he broke their state, burned settlements, the surrendered Hu also rebelled against Yiyimo, and Yiyimo built a new state.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jian'an, Gongsun Kang marched against them, broke the realm, burned towns, and the surrendered Hu turned on Yiyimo—who then built a new capital.

sentences.zh: 其後伊夷摸復擊玄菟，玄菟與遼東合擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Afterward Yiyimo again attacked Xuantu; Xuantu and Liaodong jointly struck and thoroughly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yiyimo struck Xuantu again; Xuantu and Liaodong joined forces and routed him.

sentences.zh: 伊夷摸死，子位宮立。

translations.literal: Yiyimo died; his son Weigong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyimo died and his son Weigong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 位宮有勇力，便鞍馬，善射獵。

translations.literal: Weigong had courage and strength, was skilled on saddle and horse, and excelled at hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Weigong was brave and strong, handy in the saddle, and a fine hunter.

sentences.zh: 魏景初二年，遣太傅司馬宣王率衆討公孫淵，位宮遣主簿、大加將兵千人助軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingchu under Wei, the Grand Tutor Sima the Prefectural King led an army to campaign against Gongsun Yuan; Weigong sent his chief clerk and a great xiang with a thousand troops to assist.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Jingchu two, Grand Tutor Sima the Prefectural King marched on Gongsun Yuan; Weigong sent his chief clerk and a great xiang with a thousand men to help.

sentences.zh: 正始三年，位宮寇西安、嘉平。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengshi, Weigong raided Xi'an and Jiaping.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi three Weigong raided Xi'an and Jiaping.

sentences.zh: 五年，幽州刺史母丘儉將萬人出玄菟討位宮，位宮將步騎二萬人逆軍，大戰於沸流。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Inspector Guanqiu Jian of Youzhou led ten thousand men out from Xuantu to campaign against Weigong; Weigong led twenty thousand foot and horse to meet the army; a great battle was fought at Feiliu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Youzhou Inspector Guanqiu Jian led ten thousand out of Xuantu against Weigong; Weigong met him with twenty thousand foot and horse at Feiliu.

sentences.zh: 位宮敗走，儉軍追至峴，懸車束馬，登丸都山，屠其所都，斬首虜萬餘級。

translations.literal: Weigong was defeated and fled; Jian's army pursued to Xian, unhitched chariots and hobbled horses, ascended Wandu Mountain, slaughtered their capital, and took over ten thousand heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: Weigong fled in defeat; Jian pursued to Xian, left chariots and hobbled horses, climbed Wandu Mountain, sacked the capital, and took more than ten thousand heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 位宮單將妻息遠竄。

translations.literal: Weigong alone led his wife and children far in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Weigong fled alone with wife and children.

sentences.zh: 六年，儉復討之，位宮輕將諸加奔沃沮，儉使將軍王頎追之，絕沃沮千餘里，到肅慎南界，刻石紀功；

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Jian campaigned again; Weigong fled lightly with the various xiang to Wolu; Jian sent General Wang Qi in pursuit, crossing over a thousand li of Wolu territory to the southern border of Sushen, inscribing stone to record merit;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Jian attacked again; Weigong fled lightly with the xiang to Wolu; Jian sent General Wang Qi in pursuit over a thousand li of Wolu to Sushen's southern border, carving stone to record the feat;

sentences.zh: 又到丸都山，銘不耐城而還。

translations.literal: then went again to Wandu Mountain, inscribed on Bu Nai city, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: then returned by way of Wandu Mountain, leaving an inscription at Bu Nai city.

sentences.zh: 其後，復通中夏。

translations.literal: Afterward, they again opened contact with central China.
translations.idiomatic: After that they reopened ties with central China.

sentences.zh: 晉永嘉亂，鮮卑慕容廆據昌黎大棘城，元帝授平州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Yongjia turmoil of Jin, the Xianbei Murong Hui held Daji city in Changli; Emperor Yuan appointed him Governor of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin's Yongjia chaos Murong Hui the Xianbei held Daji in Changli; Emperor Yuan made him governor of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 句驪王乙弗利頻寇遼東，廆不能制。

translations.literal: Goguryeo King Yifuli repeatedly raided Liaodong; Hui could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo King Yifuli raided Liaodong again and again; Hui could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 弗利死，子釗代立。

translations.literal: Fuli died; his son Zhao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Fuli died and his son Zhao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 康帝建元元年，慕容廆子晃率兵伐之，釗與戰，大敗，單馬奔走。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan under Emperor Kang, Murong Hui's son Huang led troops to attack; Zhao fought and was thoroughly defeated, fleeing alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: In Kang's Jianyuan one, Murong Hui's son Huang attacked; Zhao was routed and fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 晃乘勝追至丸都，焚其宮室，掠男子五萬餘口以歸。

translations.literal: Huang pressed the victory to Wandu, burned their palaces, and carried off over fifty thousand men in captivity.
translations.idiomatic: Huang pursued to Wandu, burned the palaces, and carried off more than fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 孝武太元十年，句驪攻遼東、玄菟郡，後燕慕容垂遣弟農伐句驪，復二郡。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, Goguryeo attacked Liaodong and Xuantu commanderies; Later Yan's Murong Chui sent his brother Nong to campaign against Goguryeo and recovered the two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaowu's Taiyuan ten Goguryeo struck Liaodong and Xuantu; Later Yan's Murong Chui sent his brother Nong against Goguryeo and retook both commanderies.

sentences.zh: 垂死，子寶立，以句驪王安爲平州牧，封遼東、帶方二國王。

translations.literal: Chui died; his son Bao succeeded, appointing Goguryeo King An as Governor of Pingzhou and enfeoffing him as king of the two states of Liaodong and Daifang.
translations.idiomatic: Chui died; his son Bao made Goguryeo King An governor of Pingzhou and king of Liaodong and Daifang.

sentences.zh: 安始置長史、司馬、參軍官，後略有遼東郡。

translations.literal: An first established offices of Chief Clerk, Marshal, and Staff Officer; later he gradually occupied Liaodong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An first set up chief clerk, marshal, and staff officer posts, then gradually seized Liaodong commandery.

sentences.zh: 至孫高璉，晉安帝義熙中，始奉表通貢職，歷宋、齊並授爵位，年百餘歲死。

translations.literal: Down to his grandson Gao Lian, in the Yixi era under Emperor An of Jin he first submitted memorials and opened tribute duties; through Song and Qi he received ranks and titles; he died aged over a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Gao Lian, in Jin An's Yixi era, first sent memorials and tribute; Song and Qi both granted him rank; he died past a hundred.

sentences.zh: 子雲，齊隆昌中，以爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督營、平二州、征東大將軍、樂浪公。

translations.literal: His son Yun—in Longchang of Qi—was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander of Ying and Ping two provinces, General Who Conquers the East, and Duke of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yun, in Qi Longchang, became Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, commander of Ying and Ping, General Who Conquers the East, and Duke of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 高祖卽位，進雲車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Yun was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu ascended, Yun was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 天監七年，詔曰：「高驪王樂浪郡公雲，乃誠款著，貢驛相尋，宜隆秩命，式弘朝典。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianjian, an edict said: "King Yun of Goguryeo, Duke of Lelang commandery, has shown sincere devotion; tribute envoys follow in succession—his rank and mandate should be exalted to glorify the court's standards.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian seven an edict read, "Goguryeo King Yun, Duke of Lelang, has shown true loyalty; tribute envoys come in steady succession—his rank should rise to honor the court's standards.

sentences.zh: 可撫東大將軍、開府儀同三司，持節、常侍、都督、王並如故。

translations.literal: Let him be General Who Pacifies the East, Honorific Equal to the Three Excellencies with an opening office, Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, Commander—the kingship as before."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be General Who Pacifies the East, Honorific Equal to the Three Excellencies with an opening office, Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, and Commander—the kingship unchanged."

sentences.zh: 」十一年、十五年，累遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In the eleventh and fifteenth years, envoys were repeatedly sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh and fifteenth years they sent tribute envoys again and again.

sentences.zh: 十七年，雲死，子安立。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Yun died; his son An succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Yun died and his son An succeeded.

sentences.zh: 普通元年，詔安纂襲封爵，持節、督營、平二州諸軍事、寧東將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putong, an edict had An inherit the enfeoffment and rank: Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of Ying and Ping two provinces, General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong one an edict had An inherit the title: Bearer of the Staff, commander of Ying and Ping military affairs, General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 七年，安卒，子延立，遣使貢獻，詔以延襲爵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, An died; his son Yan succeeded; envoys were sent with tribute; an edict had Yan inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year An died; his son Yan succeeded, sent tribute envoys, and received an edict inheriting the title.

sentences.zh: 中大通四年、六年，大同元年、七年，累奉表獻方物。

translations.literal: In the fourth and sixth years of Zhongdatong, and the first and seventh years of Datong, memorials and local products were repeatedly offered.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong four and six and Datong one and seven they repeatedly sent memorials and local goods.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，延卒，詔以其子襲延爵位。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing, Yan died; an edict had his son inherit Yan's title and rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing two Yan died; an edict had his son inherit Yan's title.

sentences.zh: 百濟者，其先東夷有三韓國，一曰馬韓，二曰辰韓，三曰弁韓。

translations.literal: Baekje—in antiquity among the Eastern Yi there were three Han states: the first called Ma Han, the second Jin Han, the third Byeon Han.
translations.idiomatic: Baekje arose among the Eastern Yi's three Han realms—Ma Han, Jin Han, and Byeon Han.

sentences.zh: 弁韓、辰韓各十二國，馬韓有五十四國。

translations.literal: Byeon Han and Jin Han each had twelve states; Ma Han had fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Byeon Han and Jin Han held twelve states each; Ma Han held fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 大國萬餘家，小國數千家，總十餘萬戶，百濟卽其一也。

translations.literal: Large states had over ten thousand households, small ones several thousand; altogether over a hundred thousand households—Baekje was one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Great states held ten thousand households or more, small ones a few thousand—over a hundred thousand households in all; Baekje was one.

sentences.zh: 後漸強大，兼諸小國。

translations.literal: Later it gradually grew powerful and absorbed the smaller states.
translations.idiomatic: Later it grew strong and swallowed the lesser states.

sentences.zh: 其國本與句驪在遼東之東，晉世句驪旣略有遼東，百濟亦據有遼西、晉平二郡地矣，自置百濟郡。

translations.literal: Its state originally lay with Goguryeo east of Liaodong; in Jin times, once Goguryeo had occupied Liaodong, Baekje also held the territory of Liaoxi and Jinping two commanderies and established its own Baekje commandery.
translations.idiomatic: It once shared Liaodong's east with Goguryeo; when Goguryeo seized Liaodong in Jin, Baekje took Liaoxi and Jinping and set up its own Baekje commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉太元中，王須；

translations.literal: In Taiyuan of Jin, King Xu;
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Taiyuan, King Xu;

sentences.zh: 義熙中，王餘映；

translations.literal: In Yixi, King Yuying;
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi, King Yuying;

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉中，王餘毗；

translations.literal: In Yuanjia of Song, King Yubi;
translations.idiomatic: In Song Yuanjia, King Yubi;

sentences.zh: 並遣獻生口。

translations.literal: all sent captives as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: all sent living captives as tribute.

sentences.zh: 餘毗死，立子慶。

translations.literal: Yubi died; his son Qing was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Yubi died and his son Qing succeeded.

sentences.zh: 慶死，子牟都立。

translations.literal: Qing died; his son Moudu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Qing died and Moudu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 都死，立子牟太。

translations.literal: Moudu died; his son Outai was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Moudu died and his son Outai succeeded.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，除太都督百濟諸軍事、鎮東大將軍、百濟王。

translations.literal: In Yongming of Qi he was appointed Grand Commander of all Baekje military affairs, General Who Guards the East, and King of Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Yongming he became Grand Commander of Baekje military affairs, General Who Guards the East, and King of Baekje.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，進太號征東將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian, his grand title was advanced to General Who Campaigns East.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian one his grand title rose to General Who Campaigns East.

sentences.zh: 尋爲高句驪所破，衰弱者累年，遷居南韓地。

translations.literal: Soon he was broken by Goguryeo; weakened for many years, they moved to settle in southern Han territory.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Goguryeo broke them; weakened for years, they moved to southern Han lands.

sentences.zh: 普通二年，王餘隆始復遣使奉表，稱「累破句驪，今始與通好」，而百濟更爲強國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putong, King Yulong first again sent envoys with a memorial, stating "Having repeatedly broken Goguryeo, we now first establish friendly relations"—and Baekje again became a powerful state.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong two King Yulong sent envoys again, reporting repeated victories over Goguryeo and a new opening of friendly ties—and Baekje grew strong once more.

sentences.zh: 其年，高祖詔曰：「行都督百濟諸軍事、鎮東大將軍、百濟王餘隆，守籓海外，遠脩貢職，乃誠款到，朕有嘉焉。

translations.literal: That year, Gaozu's edict said: "Acting Commander of all Baekje military affairs, General Who Guards the East, King Yulong of Baekje guards the frontier beyond the seas and maintains tribute from afar—sincerity has arrived; We commend this.
translations.idiomatic: That year Gaozu's edict said, "Acting Commander of Baekje military affairs, General Who Guards the East, King Yulong of Baekje keeps the overseas frontier and sends distant tribute—your sincerity reaches Us and We commend it.

sentences.zh: 宜率舊章，授茲榮命。

translations.literal: Following established statutes, We grant this honorable mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Following old statutes, We grant this honorable mandate.

sentences.zh: 可使持節、都督百濟諸軍事、寧東大將軍、百濟王。

translations.literal: Let him be Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all Baekje military affairs, General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Baekje."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Baekje military affairs, General Who Pacifies the East, and King of Baekje."

sentences.zh: 」五年，隆死，詔復以其子明爲持節、督百濟諸軍事、綏東將軍、百濟王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Long died; an edict had his son Ming succeed as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Baekje military affairs, General Who Assuages the East, and King of Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Long died; an edict made his son Ming Bearer of the Staff, commander of Baekje military affairs, General Who Assuages the East, and King of Baekje.

sentences.zh: 號所治城曰固麻，謂邑曰簷魯，如中國之言郡縣也。

translations.literal: They call their capital city Guma, and settlements Cheon-nok—like China's terms for commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Their capital is called Guma and their towns Cheon-nok—like China's commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 其國有二十二簷魯，皆以子弟宗族分據之。

translations.literal: The state has twenty-two cheon-nok, all held separately by sons, younger relatives, and clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has twenty-two cheon-nok, each held by sons, younger kin, and clansmen.

sentences.zh: 其人形長，衣服淨潔。

translations.literal: The people are tall in form; their clothes are clean.
translations.idiomatic: The people are tall and keep their dress clean.

sentences.zh: 其國近倭，頗有文身者。

translations.literal: Their country lies near Wa; many practice tattooing.
translations.idiomatic: Their land lies near Wa; tattooing is common.

sentences.zh: 今言語服章略與高驪同，行不張拱、拜不申足則異。

translations.literal: Now speech and dress largely resemble Goguryeo; they differ in that they do not spread their arms when walking or extend both feet when bowing.
translations.idiomatic: Speech and dress now mostly match Goguryeo; they differ in walking without spread arms and bowing without both feet extended.

sentences.zh: 呼帽曰冠，襦曰複衫，袴曰褌。

translations.literal: They call a cap a guan, a jacket a fushan, trousers a kun.
translations.idiomatic: They call hats guan, jackets fushan, and trousers kun.

sentences.zh: 其言參諸夏，亦秦、韓之遺俗云。

translations.literal: Their speech partakes of the Central States—it is said to preserve customs of Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Their language mixes with the Central States—said to preserve Qin and Han customs.

sentences.zh: 中大通六年、大同七年，累遣使獻方物；

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhongdatong and the seventh of Datong, envoys were repeatedly sent offering local products;
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong six and Datong seven they sent envoys again and again with local goods;

sentences.zh: 幷請《涅盤》等經義、《毛詩》博士，幷工匠、畫師等，敕並給之。

translations.literal: and requested masters of the Nirvana Sutra and other doctrinal texts, a Doctor of the Mao Odes, together with craftsmen and painters—the court ordered all to be granted.
translations.idiomatic: and asked for masters of the Nirvana Sutra and other scriptures, a Doctor of the Mao Odes, plus craftsmen and painters—all were granted by edict.

sentences.zh: 太清三年，不知京師寇賊，猶遣使貢獻；

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing, unaware of bandits ravaging the capital, they still sent envoys with tribute;
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing three, not knowing bandits had ravaged the capital, they still sent tribute envoys;

sentences.zh: 旣至，見城闕荒毀，並號慟涕泣。

translations.literal: once arrived, seeing the capital gates in ruin, they all wailed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: on arrival, seeing ruined gates and walls, they wailed and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 侯景怒，囚執之，及景平，方得還國。

translations.literal: Hou Jing grew angry and imprisoned them; only when Jing was pacified could they return home.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing in anger seized and held them; only after his defeat could they return home.

sentences.zh: 新羅者，其先本辰韓種也。

translations.literal: Silla—their ancestors were originally of the Jin Han stock.
translations.idiomatic: Silla—its people originally came from Jin Han stock.

sentences.zh: 辰韓亦曰秦韓，相去萬里，傳言秦世亡人避役來適馬韓，馬韓亦割其東界居之，以秦人，故名之曰秦韓。

translations.literal: Jin Han is also called Qin Han; they lie ten thousand li apart; tradition says that in Qin times fugitives fleeing corvée came to Ma Han; Ma Han also ceded its eastern border for them to dwell—the name Qin Han comes from these Qin people.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Han is also Qin Han; the lands lie ten thousand li apart. Tradition holds that Qin-era fugitives fleeing corvée reached Ma Han, which ceded its eastern marches for them—hence Qin Han, for Qin people.

sentences.zh: 其言語名物有似中國人，名國爲邦，弓爲弧，賊爲寇，行酒爲行觴。

translations.literal: Their speech and nomenclature resemble Chinese: they call a state bang, a bow hu, a bandit kou, and serving wine xingshang.
translations.idiomatic: Their words and names echo China: realm is bang, bow is hu, bandit is kou, and passing wine is xingshang.

sentences.zh: 相呼皆爲徒，不與馬韓同。

translations.literal: They address one another as tu—it differs from Ma Han.
translations.idiomatic: They call one another tu—not as Ma Han does.

sentences.zh: 又辰韓王常用馬韓人作之，世相係，辰韓不得自立爲王，明其流移之人故也；

translations.literal: Moreover the king of Jin Han was usually a Ma Han man appointed to the post, generation after generation; Jin Han could not establish its own king—clear evidence they were displaced people;
translations.idiomatic: Jin Han kings were usually Ma Han appointees, generation after generation; Jin Han could not crown its own king—proof they were migrants;

sentences.zh: 恒爲馬韓所制。

translations.literal: always controlled by Ma Han.
translations.idiomatic: always under Ma Han's control.

sentences.zh: 辰韓始有六國，稍分爲十二，新羅則其一也。

translations.literal: Jin Han originally had six states, gradually dividing into twelve—Silla is one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Han began with six states and later split into twelve; Silla is one.

sentences.zh: 其國在百濟東南五千餘里。

translations.literal: Its state lies over five thousand li southeast of Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: The realm lies more than five thousand li southeast of Baekje.

sentences.zh: 其地東濱大海，南北與句驪、百濟接。

translations.literal: Its territory fronts the great sea to the east; north and south it borders Goguryeo and Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: It faces the eastern sea; north and south it touches Goguryeo and Baekje.

sentences.zh: 魏時曰新盧，宋時曰新羅，或曰斯羅。

translations.literal: Under Wei it was called Sin Lu; under Song, Silla—or Sila.
translations.idiomatic: Wei called it Sin Lu; Song called it Silla, or Sila.

sentences.zh: 其國小，不能自通使聘。

translations.literal: The state is small and could not on its own dispatch envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was small and could not send envoys on its own.

sentences.zh: 普通二年，王募名秦，始使使隨百濟奉獻方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putong, King Munjin first sent envoys following Baekje to offer local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong two King Munjin first sent envoys with Baekje to present local goods.

sentences.zh: 其俗呼城曰健牟羅，其邑在內曰啄評，在外曰邑勒，亦中國之言郡縣也。

translations.literal: Their custom calls a city Geonmullara; settlements within are called chokpyeong, without are called eollok—again like China's commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: They call a city Geonmullara; inner towns are chokpyeong, outer ones eollok—again like China's commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 國有六啄評，五十二邑勒。

translations.literal: The state has six chokpyeong and fifty-two eollok.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has six chokpyeong and fifty-two eollok.

sentences.zh: 土地肥美，宜植五穀。

translations.literal: The land is rich and fair, suited for planting the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: The soil is rich and good for the five grains.

sentences.zh: 多桑麻，作縑布。

translations.literal: Mulberry and hemp are abundant; they make fine cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberry and hemp abound; they weave fine cloth.

sentences.zh: 服牛乘馬，男女有別。

translations.literal: They use oxen for draft and horses for riding; men and women keep apart.
translations.idiomatic: They draft with oxen, ride horses, and keep the sexes separate.

sentences.zh: 其官名，有子賁旱支、齊旱支、謁旱支、壹告支、奇貝旱支。

translations.literal: Their office titles include zibenhanzhi, qihanzhi, yehanzhi, yigaozhi, and qibeihanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Offices include zibenhanzhi, qihanzhi, yehanzhi, yigaozhi, and qibeihanzhi.

sentences.zh: 其冠曰遺子禮，襦曰尉解，洿曰柯半，靴曰洗。

translations.literal: Their crown is called yizili, their jacket wei-jie, their skirt ke-ban, their boots xi.
translations.idiomatic: They call the crown yizili, the jacket wei-jie, the skirt ke-ban, and boots xi.

sentences.zh: 其拜及行與高驪相類。

translations.literal: Their bows and their gait resemble Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Their bows and gait match Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 無文字，刻木爲信。

translations.literal: They have no writing; they carve wood for tokens of trust.
translations.idiomatic: Without writing, they carve wood for tokens.

sentences.zh: 語言待百濟而後通焉。

translations.literal: Their speech requires Baekje before it can be understood.
translations.idiomatic: Their language needs a Baekje interpreter.

sentences.zh: 倭者，自云太伯之後，俗皆文身。

translations.literal: Wa—they say themselves they are descendants of Taibo; by custom all tattoo the body.
translations.idiomatic: Wa claim descent from Taibo and tattoo by custom.

sentences.zh: 去帶方萬二千餘里，大抵在會稽之東，相去絕遠。

translations.literal: More than twelve thousand li from Daifang, broadly east of Kuaiji—the distance is utterly remote.
translations.idiomatic: Over twelve thousand li from Daifang, east of Kuaiji—utterly remote.

sentences.zh: 從帶方至倭，循海水行，歷韓國，乍東乍南，七千餘里始度一海；

translations.literal: From Daifang to Wa, following the sea, passing through the Han states, now east now south, more than seven thousand li before crossing one sea;
translations.idiomatic: From Daifang to Wa one sails the coast through Han lands, veering east and south seven thousand li before the first sea crossing;

sentences.zh: 海闊千餘里，名瀚海，至一支國；

translations.literal: the sea is more than a thousand li wide, called the Han Sea, reaching the land of Itsu;
translations.idiomatic: a thousand-li sea called the Han Sea leads to Itsu;

sentences.zh: 又度一海千餘里，名未盧國；

translations.literal: crossing another sea of more than a thousand li reaches the land of Miro;
translations.idiomatic: another thousand-li crossing reaches Miro;

sentences.zh: 又東南陸行五百里，至伊都國；

translations.literal: southeast by land five hundred li reaches the land of Ito;
translations.idiomatic: five hundred li southeast by land brings one to Ito;

sentences.zh: 又東南行百里，至奴國；

translations.literal: southeast another hundred li reaches the land of Nu;
translations.idiomatic: a hundred li farther southeast lies Nu;

sentences.zh: 又東行百里，至不彌國；

translations.literal: east another hundred li reaches the land of Fumi;
translations.idiomatic: a hundred li east lies Fumi;

sentences.zh: 又南水行二十日，至投馬國；

translations.literal: south by water twenty days reaches the land of Tuma;
translations.idiomatic: twenty days south by water reaches Tuma;

sentences.zh: 又南水行十日，陸行一月日，至邪馬臺國，卽倭王所居。

translations.literal: south by water ten days, by land one month, reaches Yamatai—the seat of the Wa king.
translations.idiomatic: ten days south by water and one month by land reaches Yamatai, where the Wa king dwells.

sentences.zh: 其官有伊支馬，次曰彌馬獲支，次曰奴往鞮。

translations.literal: Its offices include ikima, next mimakazhi, next nuchangti.
translations.idiomatic: Offices run ikima, then mimakazhi, then nuchangti.

sentences.zh: 民種禾稻紵麻，蠶桑織績。

translations.literal: The people plant millet, rice, hemp, and mulberry; they raise silkworms and weave.
translations.idiomatic: They grow grain, hemp, and mulberry, raise silkworms, and weave.

sentences.zh: 有薑、桂、橘、椒、蘇。

translations.literal: They have ginger, cassia, oranges, pepper, and perilla.
translations.idiomatic: Ginger, cassia, oranges, pepper, and perilla grow there.

sentences.zh: 出黑雉、真珠、青玉。

translations.literal: They produce black pheasants, pearls, and green jade.
translations.idiomatic: Black pheasants, pearls, and green jade come from the land.

sentences.zh: 有獸如牛，名山鼠；

translations.literal: There is a beast like an ox, called the mountain rat;
translations.idiomatic: A beast like an ox, called the mountain rat, lives there;

sentences.zh: 又有大蛇吞此獸。

translations.literal: there is also a great serpent that swallows this beast.
translations.idiomatic: and a great serpent that devours it.

sentences.zh: 蛇皮堅不可斫，其上有孔，乍開乍閉，時或有光，射之中，蛇則死矣。

translations.literal: The serpent's hide is hard and cannot be cut; on it are holes that now open, now close; at times light shines from them—shoot through one and the serpent dies.
translations.idiomatic: Its hide is uncuttable, pierced with holes that open and shut and sometimes shine; a shot through a hole kills the serpent.

sentences.zh: 物產略與儋耳、朱崖同。

translations.literal: Products are roughly the same as Dan'er and Zhuya.
translations.idiomatic: Local products resemble Dan'er and Zhuya.

sentences.zh: 地溫暖，風俗不淫。

translations.literal: The land is warm; custom is not licentious.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is mild and morals restrained.

sentences.zh: 男女皆露紒。

translations.literal: Men and women all wear their hair loose.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women wear loose hair.

sentences.zh: 富貴者以錦繡雜采爲帽，似中國胡公頭。

translations.literal: The wealthy make caps of brocade and mixed colors, resembling the Hu gong head of China.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy men wear brocade caps like the Hu gong head of China.

sentences.zh: 食飲用籩豆。

translations.literal: For food and drink they use platters and bowls.
translations.idiomatic: Meals are served on platters and in bowls.

sentences.zh: 其死，有棺無槨，封土作冢。

translations.literal: At death there is an inner coffin but no outer shell; earth is piled to make the mound.
translations.idiomatic: The dead receive an inner coffin without an outer shell, and earth is heaped for the tomb.

sentences.zh: 人性皆嗜酒。

translations.literal: By nature the people all love wine.
translations.idiomatic: The people are fond of wine.

sentences.zh: 俗不知正歲，多壽考，多至八九十，或至百歲。

translations.literal: Custom does not know the proper New Year; many live long, often reaching eighty or ninety, sometimes a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: They keep no proper calendar year; many live to eighty or ninety, some to a hundred.

sentences.zh: 其俗女多男少，貴者至四五妻，賤者猶兩三妻。

translations.literal: Custom has more women than men; the noble may have four or five wives, the lowly still two or three.
translations.idiomatic: Women outnumber men; nobles take four or five wives, commoners two or three.

sentences.zh: 婦人無淫妬。

translations.literal: Wives feel no jealous rage over licentiousness.
translations.idiomatic: Wives do not grow jealous over affairs.

sentences.zh: 無盜竊，少諍訟。

translations.literal: There is no theft; lawsuits are few.
translations.idiomatic: Theft is rare and lawsuits few.

sentences.zh: 若犯法，輕者沒其妻子，重則滅其宗族。

translations.literal: If one breaks the law, the lighter penalty enslaves wife and children; the heavier exterminates the whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: Light crimes cost wife and children; grave ones wipe out the clan.

sentences.zh: 漢靈帝光和中，倭國亂，相攻伐歷年，乃共立一女子卑彌呼爲王。

translations.literal: In the Guanghe era of Han Emperor Ling, Wa fell into disorder and attacked one another for years; then together they set up one woman, Himiko, as king.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han Ling's Guanghe era Wa warred for years until the realms jointly raised the woman Himiko as king.

sentences.zh: 彌呼無夫婿，挾鬼道，能惑衆，故國人立之。

translations.literal: Himiko had no husband; she clung to ghost-craft and could beguile the masses—therefore the people of the state set her up.
translations.idiomatic: Himiko had no husband, ruled through spirit-craft, and swayed the people—so they made her queen.

sentences.zh: 有男弟佐治國。

translations.literal: She had a younger brother who assisted in governing the state.
translations.idiomatic: A younger brother helped govern.

sentences.zh: 自爲王，少有見者，以婢千人自侍，唯使一男子出入傳教令。

translations.literal: Since becoming king she was seldom seen; a thousand maidservants waited on her, and only one man was allowed in and out to transmit edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned she was rarely seen; a thousand maids served her while a single man carried edicts in and out.

sentences.zh: 所處宮室，常有兵守衛。

translations.literal: The palace where she dwelt was always guarded by soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Armed guards always ringed her dwelling.

sentences.zh: 至魏景初三年，公孫淵誅後，卑彌呼始遣使朝貢，魏以爲親魏王，假金印紫綬。
