translations.literal: By the third year of Jingchu under Wei, after Gongsun Yuan was executed, Himiko first sent envoys with tribute; Wei made her King Who Honors Wei and granted a gold seal with purple cord.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Jingchu 3, after Gongsun Yuan's execution, Himiko first sent tribute; Wei titled her King Who Honors Wei and gave a gold seal on purple cord.

sentences.zh: 正始中，卑彌呼死，更立男王，國中不服，更相誅殺，復立卑彌呼宗女臺與爲王。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era Himiko died; a male king was set up, but the state would not obey; they killed one another again and restored Himiko's clan-daughter Iyo as king.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi Himiko died; a male king failed to command loyalty, bloodshed resumed, and Himiko's kinswoman Iyo was crowned.

sentences.zh: 其後復立男王，並受中國爵命。

translations.literal: Later a male king was set up again, and both received titles and commands from China.
translations.idiomatic: Later a male king ruled again, and both received Chinese investiture.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝時，有倭王贊。

translations.literal: In the time of Jin Emperor An there was a Wa king called Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin Emperor An a Wa king named Zan reigned.

sentences.zh: 贊死，立弟彌；

translations.literal: When Zan died, his brother Chen was set up;
translations.idiomatic: Zan's death brought his brother Chen to the throne;

sentences.zh: 彌死，立子濟；

translations.literal: when Chen died, his son Ji was set up;
translations.idiomatic: Chen's death brought his son Ji;

sentences.zh: 濟死，立子興；

translations.literal: when Ji died, his son Xing was set up;
translations.idiomatic: Ji's death brought his son Xing;

sentences.zh: 興死，立弟武。

translations.literal: when Xing died, his brother Wu was set up.
translations.idiomatic: Xing's death brought his brother Wu.

sentences.zh: 齊建元中，除武持節、督倭新羅任那伽羅秦韓慕韓六國諸軍事、鎮東大將軍。

translations.literal: In Qi Jianyuan, Wu was made Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Wa, Silla, Imna, Kara, Jinhan, and Mahan, and General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Jianyuan Wu received the staff, command over Wa, Silla, Imna, Kara, Jinhan, and Mahan, and the title General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 高祖卽位，進武號征東將軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Wu's title was advanced to General Who Campaigns East.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu promoted Wu to General Who Campaigns East.

sentences.zh: 其南有侏儒國，人長三四尺。

translations.literal: South of them is the Dwarf Country; the people are three or four feet tall.
translations.idiomatic: South lies the Dwarf Country, whose people stand three or four feet.

sentences.zh: 又南黑齒國、裸國，去倭四千餘里，船行可一年至。

translations.literal: Farther south are the Black-Tooth Country and the Naked Country, more than four thousand li from Wa—a year's voyage by ship.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south lie Black-Tooth and Naked countries, four thousand li from Wa and a year's sail away.

sentences.zh: 又西南萬里有海人，身黑眼白，裸而醜。

translations.literal: Still farther southwest, ten thousand li off, are sea people—black of body, white of eye, naked and ugly.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand li southwest live sea people, black-skinned and white-eyed, naked and foul.

sentences.zh: 其肉美，行者或射而食之。

translations.literal: Their flesh is savory; travelers sometimes shoot and eat them.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers find their flesh savory and sometimes shoot them for food.

sentences.zh: 文身國

translations.literal: Tattooed Country
translations.idiomatic: Tattooed Country

sentences.zh: 文身國，在倭國東北七千餘里。

translations.literal: The Tattooed Country lies more than seven thousand li northeast of Wa.
translations.idiomatic: Tattooed Country stands seven thousand li northeast of Wa.

sentences.zh: 人體有文如獸，其額上有三文，文直者貴，文小者賤。

translations.literal: People's bodies bear marks like beasts; on the forehead are three marks—straight marks mean nobility, small marks mean baseness.
translations.idiomatic: Bodies are tattooed like beasts; three forehead marks rank the person—straight for noble, small for low.

sentences.zh: 土俗歡樂，物豊而賤，行客不齎糧。

translations.literal: Local custom is joyous; goods are plentiful and cheap; travelers need not carry provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Life is merry, goods cheap and abundant; travelers carry no rations.

sentences.zh: 有屋宇，無城郭。

translations.literal: They have houses but no walled cities.
translations.idiomatic: They build houses without city walls.

sentences.zh: 其王所居，飾以金銀珍麗。

translations.literal: Where the king dwells is adorned with gold, silver, and rare splendor.
translations.idiomatic: The king's residence gleams with gold, silver, and rare finery.

sentences.zh: 繞屋爲緌，廣一丈，實以水銀，雨則流于水銀之上。

translations.literal: Around the house runs a fringe one zhang wide, filled with mercury; when it rains the water flows atop the mercury.
translations.idiomatic: A one-zhang fringe rings the house, filled with mercury; rain runs over the mercury's surface.

sentences.zh: 市用珍寶。

translations.literal: The market uses precious gems.
translations.idiomatic: Markets trade in precious gems.

sentences.zh: 犯輕罪者則鞭杖；

translations.literal: Light crimes are punished with the whip and staff;
translations.idiomatic: Light offenses bring the whip and staff;

sentences.zh: 犯死罪則置猛獸食之，有枉則猛獸避而不食，經宿則赦之。

translations.literal: capital crimes are punished by setting fierce beasts to devour the offender—if there is injustice the beasts avoid and will not eat; after one night he is pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: capital crimes are judged by fierce beasts—if the man is wronged the beasts refuse him; after a night he goes free.

sentences.zh: 大漢國

translations.literal: Great Han Country
translations.idiomatic: Great Han Country

sentences.zh: 大漢國，在文身國東五千餘里。

translations.literal: The Great Han Country lies more than five thousand li east of the Tattooed Country.
translations.idiomatic: Great Han Country lies five thousand li east of Tattooed Country.

sentences.zh: 無兵戈，不攻戰。

translations.literal: They have no weapons of war and do not make battle.
translations.idiomatic: They keep no arms and make no war.

sentences.zh: 風俗並與文身國同而言語異。

translations.literal: Custom is the same as the Tattooed Country, but the language differs.
translations.idiomatic: Custom matches Tattooed Country; speech differs.

sentences.zh: 扶桑國

translations.literal: Fusang Country
translations.idiomatic: Fusang Country

sentences.zh: 扶桑國者，齊永元元年，其國有沙門慧深來至荊州，說云：「扶桑在大漢國東二萬餘里，地在中國之東，其土多扶桑木，故以爲名。

translations.literal: Fusang Country—in the first year of Qi Yongyuan a monk of that land, Hui Shen, came to Jing Province and said: "Fusang lies more than twenty thousand li east of the Great Han Country, its land east of China; the soil has much fusang wood, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: Fusang—in Qi Yongyuan 1 the monk Hui Shen reached Jing Province and reported, "Fusang lies twenty thousand li east of Great Han, east of China; fusang trees abound, giving the land its name.

sentences.zh: 」扶桑葉似桐，而初生如笋，國人食之，實如梨而赤，績其皮爲布以爲衣，亦以爲綿。

translations.literal: " Fusang leaves resemble paulownia and when first sprouting are like bamboo shoots; the people eat them; the fruit is like a pear and red; they spin the bark into cloth for clothing, also using it as cotton.
translations.idiomatic: " Leaves resemble paulownia, new shoots like bamboo; the people eat them; fruit is red like pears; bark is spun into cloth for dress and padding.

sentences.zh: 作板屋，無城郭。

translations.literal: They build plank houses and have no walled cities.
translations.idiomatic: They live in plank houses without walled cities.

sentences.zh: 有文字，以扶桑皮爲紙。

translations.literal: They have writing and use fusang bark for paper.
translations.idiomatic: They write on paper made from fusang bark.

sentences.zh: 無兵甲，不攻戰。

translations.literal: They have no armor or weapons and do not make battle.
translations.idiomatic: They keep no armor or arms and make no war.

sentences.zh: 其國法，有南北獄。

translations.literal: By the law of the state there are southern and northern prisons.
translations.idiomatic: State law divides prisons into south and north.

sentences.zh: 若犯輕者入南獄，重罪者入北獄。

translations.literal: Light offenders enter the southern prison; grave offenders enter the northern prison.
translations.idiomatic: Light crimes go to the south prison, grave crimes to the north.

sentences.zh: 有赦則赦南獄，不赦北獄。

translations.literal: When there is an amnesty the southern prison is pardoned; the northern prison is not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesties free the south prison, never the north.

sentences.zh: 在北獄者，男女相配，生男八歲爲奴，生女九歲爲婢。

translations.literal: Those in the northern prison are paired man and woman; a boy at eight becomes a slave, a girl at nine a maid.
translations.idiomatic: Northern prisoners are paired; boys become slaves at eight, girls maids at nine.

sentences.zh: 犯罪之身，至死不出。

translations.literal: The bodies of the condemned never leave until death.
translations.idiomatic: Condemned bodies never leave until death.

sentences.zh: 貴人有罪，國乃大會，坐罪人於坑，對之宴飲，分訣若死別焉。

translations.literal: When a noble commits a crime the state holds a great assembly, seating the guilty in a pit while feasting opposite him—parting words as at a final farewell.
translations.idiomatic: When nobles sin the realm feasts above a pit where the condemned sit, taking leave as at death.

sentences.zh: 以灰繞之，其一重則一身摒退，二重則及子孫，三重則及七世。

translations.literal: Ash is piled around them; one layer of ash removes one person from the company, two layers reach sons and grandsons, three layers reach seven generations.
translations.idiomatic: Ash rings the pit—one layer dismisses the offender, two reach sons and grandsons, three reach seven generations.

sentences.zh: 名國王爲乙祁；

translations.literal: The king is called yiji;
translations.idiomatic: They call the king yiji;

sentences.zh: 貴人第一者爲大對盧，第二者爲小對盧，第三者爲納咄沙。

translations.literal: the first-rank noble is called dadu-lu, the second xiaodu-lu, the third nazuo-sha.
translations.idiomatic: first nobles are dadu-lu, second xiaodu-lu, third nazuo-sha.

sentences.zh: 國王行有鼓角導從。

translations.literal: When the king travels drums and horns lead the procession.
translations.idiomatic: The king travels to drum and horn.

sentences.zh: 其衣色隨年改易，甲乙年青，丙丁年赤，戊己年黃，庚辛年白，壬癸年黑。

translations.literal: Garment colors change with the year—green in jia and yi years, red in bing and ding, yellow in wu and ji, white in geng and xin, black in ren and gui.
translations.idiomatic: Dress color follows the year—green for jia-yi, red for bing-ding, yellow for wu-ji, white for geng-xin, black for ren-gui.

sentences.zh: 有牛角甚長，以角載物，至勝二十斛。

translations.literal: Ox horns are very long and used to carry goods, bearing up to twenty hu.
translations.idiomatic: Long ox horns serve as load-bearers, holding twenty hu.

sentences.zh: 車有馬車、牛車、鹿車。

translations.literal: Carts include horse-carts, ox-carts, and deer-carts.
translations.idiomatic: They use horse-carts, ox-carts, and deer-carts.

sentences.zh: 國人養鹿，如中國畜牛，以乳爲酪。

translations.literal: The people raise deer as China raises cattle, making curds from the milk.
translations.idiomatic: They herd deer as China herds cattle and make curds from the milk.

sentences.zh: 有桑梨，經年不壞。

translations.literal: They have mulberry pears that keep for years without spoiling.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberry pears keep for years.

sentences.zh: 多蒲桃。

translations.literal: Grapes are plentiful.
translations.idiomatic: Grapes abound.

sentences.zh: 其地無鐵有銅，不貴金銀。

translations.literal: The land has no iron but has copper; gold and silver are not prized.
translations.idiomatic: Iron is absent, copper present; gold and silver are cheap.

sentences.zh: 市無租估。

translations.literal: Markets levy no tolls or appraisals.
translations.idiomatic: Markets take no toll or appraisal fee.

sentences.zh: 其婚姻，婿往女家門外作屋，晨夕灑掃，經年而女不悅，卽驅之，相悅乃成婚。

translations.literal: In marriage the bridegroom builds a house outside the bride's family gate, sweeping morning and evening; if after a year the girl is not pleased she drives him off—only when both are pleased do they marry.
translations.idiomatic: The groom builds a hut outside the bride's gate and sweeps it daily; if she is displeased after a year she sends him away—marriage comes only by mutual consent.

sentences.zh: 婚禮大抵與中國同。

translations.literal: The wedding rites are broadly the same as China's.
translations.idiomatic: Wedding rites largely match China's.

sentences.zh: 親喪，七日不食；

translations.literal: For a parent's death one does not eat for seven days;
translations.idiomatic: On a parent's death one fasts seven days;

sentences.zh: 祖父母喪，五日不食；

translations.literal: for grandparents' death, five days without eating;
translations.idiomatic: for grandparents, five days;

sentences.zh: 兄弟伯叔姑姊妹，三日不食。

translations.literal: for brothers, uncles, aunts, and sisters, three days without eating.
translations.idiomatic: for siblings, uncles, aunts, and sisters, three days.

sentences.zh: 設靈爲神像，朝夕拜奠，不制縗絰。

translations.literal: Spirit tablets are set up as spirit-images; morning and evening they bow and offer sacrifice—no hemp mourning garments are prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit-images stand for the dead; morning and evening bring bowing and offerings—no hemp mourning garb is required.

sentences.zh: 嗣王立，三年不視國事。

translations.literal: When the heir succeeds he does not attend to state affairs for three years.
translations.idiomatic: A new king leaves state affairs untouched for three years.

sentences.zh: 其俗舊無佛法，宋大明二年，罽賓國嘗有比丘五人遊行至其國，流通佛法、經像，教令出家，風俗遂改。」

translations.literal: By old custom there was no Buddhist Law; in the second year of Song Daming, five monks from Gandhara once traveled to that country, spreading Buddhist Law and sutra-images, teaching men to leave the household—and custom was thereby changed."
translations.idiomatic: Once there was no Buddhism; in Song Daming 2 five Gandharan monks reached the land, spread the Law and images, and taught renunciation—and custom changed."

sentences.zh: 慧深又云：「扶桑東千餘里有女國，容貌端正，色甚潔白，身體有毛，髮長委地。

translations.literal: Huishen also said: "More than a thousand li east of Fusang is a land of women; their features are proper, their color very pure white, their bodies have hair, and their hair trails to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Huishen also said that east of Fusang, a thousand li and more away, lay a realm of women—handsome of face, very fair in complexion, hairy of body, with hair that spilled to the ground.

sentences.zh: 至二、三月，競入水則任娠，六七月產子。

translations.literal: When the second and third months come, they rush into the water and become pregnant; in the sixth or seventh month they bear children.
translations.idiomatic: In the second and third months they all plunge into the water and conceive; by the sixth or seventh month they give birth.

sentences.zh: 女人胸前無乳，項後生毛，根白，毛中有汁，以乳子，一百日能行，三四年則成人矣。

translations.literal: The women have no breasts on their chests; hair grows behind the nape, white at the root, and the hair contains sap with which they nurse their children—the children can walk at a hundred days, and in three or four years reach adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: Women have no breasts on the chest; behind the neck grows hair, white at the root, and sap within the hair feeds the child. At a hundred days the child can walk; in three or four years it is grown.

sentences.zh: 見人驚避，偏畏丈夫。

translations.literal: They startle and flee at the sight of people, and especially fear men.
translations.idiomatic: They startle at the sight of people and flee, and fear men above all.

sentences.zh: 食鹹草如禽獸。

translations.literal: They eat salt-grass like birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: They eat salt-grass as birds and beasts do.

sentences.zh: 鹹草葉似邪蒿，而氣香味鹹。

translations.literal: Salt-grass leaves resemble wormwood, but its fragrance is salty.
translations.idiomatic: Salt-grass leaves resemble wormwood, yet its scent is salty and fragrant.

sentences.zh: 」天監六年，有晉安人渡海，爲風所飄至一島，登岸，有人居止。

translations.literal: " In Tianjian 6, a man of Jin'an crossed the sea and was blown by wind to an island; landing ashore, he found people dwelling there.
translations.idiomatic: " In Tianjian 6 a man of Jin'an crossed the sea, was blown by wind to an island, went ashore, and found people living there.

sentences.zh: 女則如中國，而言語不可曉；

translations.literal: The women were like those of China, but their speech could not be understood;
translations.idiomatic: The women resembled Chinese women, but their speech could not be understood;

sentences.zh: 男則人身而狗頭，其聲如吠。

translations.literal: the men had human bodies and dogs' heads, their voices like barking.
translations.idiomatic: the men had human bodies and dogs' heads, and barked when they spoke.

sentences.zh: 其食有小豆，其衣如布。

translations.literal: Their food included small beans; their clothing was like cloth.
translations.idiomatic: They ate small beans; their clothes were like cloth.

sentences.zh: 築土爲牆，其形圓，其戶如竇云。

translations.literal: They built walls of earth, round in form, with doorways like burrows, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: They built earthen walls, round in shape, with doorways like burrows—or so it is said.

sentences.zh: 西北諸戎

translations.literal: The Northwestern Barbarians
translations.idiomatic: The Northwestern Barbarians

sentences.zh: 西北諸戎，漢世張騫始發西域之迹，甘英遂臨西海，或遣侍子，或奉貢獻，于時雖窮兵極武，僅而克捷，比之前代，其略遠矣。

translations.literal: The northwestern barbarians—in Han times Zhang Qian first opened the trail to the Western Regions, and Gan Ying reached the Western Sea; some sent hostages, some presented tribute; even then, though martial might was pushed to the limit, success came barely, and compared with earlier ages the reach was much greater.
translations.idiomatic: The northwestern barbarians: in Han, Zhang Qian first traced the Western Regions, and Gan Ying reached the Western Sea. Some sent hostages, some brought tribute. Even then, for all the empire's martial exertion, victory came only narrowly—and compared with earlier dynasties, the reach was vastly greater.

sentences.zh: 魏時三方鼎跱，日事干戈，晉氏平吳以後，少獲寧息，徒置戊己之官，諸國亦未賓從也。

translations.literal: Under Wei the three powers stood like tripod legs, daily at war; after Jin pacified Wu there was little peace—only garrison officers of Wu and Ji were placed, and the states still did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei the three realms stood tripod-locked, daily at war. After Jin pacified Wu there was scant peace; garrison officers alone were posted, and the states still did not submit.

sentences.zh: 繼以中原喪亂，胡人遞起，西域與江東隔礙，重譯不交。

translations.literal: Then came chaos in the Central Plains, barbarians rising one after another; the Western Regions and Jiangdong were cut off, and no embassies passed through multiple interpreters.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Central Plains fell into chaos and barbarians rose in succession; the Western Regions and Jiangdong were cut off, and no embassies came through layers of translation.

sentences.zh: 呂光之涉龜茲，亦獲蠻夷之伐蠻夷，非中國之意也。

translations.literal: When Lü Guang marched on Kucha, it was likewise barbarians fighting barbarians—not China's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Guang marched on Kucha, it was barbarians cutting down barbarians—not China's design.

sentences.zh: 自是諸國分幷，勝負強弱，難得詳載。

translations.literal: From then the states divided and merged; victors and vanquished, strong and weak—hard to record in detail.
translations.idiomatic: From then the states split and merged, strong and weak trading places—too much to record in full.

sentences.zh: 明珠翠羽，雖仞於後宮；

translations.literal: Bright pearls and kingfisher feathers, though piled in the rear palace;
translations.idiomatic: Bright pearls and kingfisher feathers might pile up in the rear palace,

sentences.zh: 蒲梢龍文，希入於外署。

translations.literal: fine horses named Pu Shao and Long Wen rarely entered the outer offices.
translations.idiomatic: yet fine horses like Pu Shao and Long Wen seldom reached the outer offices.

sentences.zh: 有梁受命，其奉正朔而朝闕庭者，則仇池、宕昌、高昌、鄧至、河南、龜茲、于闐、滑諸國焉。

translations.literal: When Liang received the mandate, those observing the calendar and attending the imperial court were Qiuchi, Dangchang, Gaochang, Dengzhi, Henan, Kucha, Yutian, and Hua states.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang received the mandate, those who kept the calendar and came to court were Qiuchi, Dangchang, Gaochang, Dengzhi, Henan, Kucha, Yutian, and Hua.

sentences.zh: 今綴其風俗，爲《西北戎傳》云。

translations.literal: Now I arrange their customs and present the "Account of the Northwestern Barbarians," thus.
translations.idiomatic: Now I gather their customs into the Account of the Northwestern Barbarians, thus.

sentences.zh: 河南國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Henan
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Henan

sentences.zh: 河南王者，其先出自鮮卑慕容氏。

translations.literal: The kings of Henan originally came from the Xianbei Murong clan.
translations.idiomatic: The kings of Henan traced their line to the Xianbei Murong clan.

sentences.zh: 初，慕容奕洛干有二子，庶長曰吐谷渾，嫡曰廆。

translations.literal: At the start, Murong Yiluoqian had two sons—the elder by a concubine was called Tuyuhun, the heir was called Hui.
translations.idiomatic: At first Murong Yiluoqian had two sons: the elder by a concubine was Tuyuhun; the heir was Hui.

sentences.zh: 洛干卒，廆嗣位，吐谷渾避之西徙。

translations.literal: When Yiluoqian died, Hui succeeded; Tuyuhun fled west to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yiluoqian died, Hui took the throne and Tuyuhun fled west to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 廆追留之，而牛馬皆西走，不肯還，因遂徙上隴，度枹罕，出涼州西南，至赤水而居之。

translations.literal: Hui pursued to keep him back, but cattle and horses all ran west and would not return—so Tuyuhun migrated up to Long, crossed Fuhan, passed southwest of Liangzhou, and settled at Chishui.
translations.idiomatic: Hui pursued to bring him back, but cattle and horses all ran west and would not return. Tuyuhun therefore moved up onto Long, crossed Fuhan, passed southwest of Liangzhou, and settled at Chishui.

sentences.zh: 其地則張掖之南，隴西之西，在河之南，故以爲號。

translations.literal: The land lay south of Zhangye, west of Longxi, and south of the river—hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: The land lay south of Zhangye, west of Longxi, and south of the river—hence the name Henan.

sentences.zh: 其界東至壘川，西鄰于闐，北接高昌，東北通秦嶺，方千餘里，蓋古之流沙地焉。

translations.literal: Its borders reached Leichuan in the east, adjoined Yutian in the west, connected with Gaochang in the north, and linked to the Qin Mountains in the northeast—over a thousand li square, largely the ancient land of shifting sands.
translations.idiomatic: Its borders ran east to Leichuan, west to Yutian, north to Gaochang, and northeast to the Qin Mountains—over a thousand li on a side, largely the old land of shifting sands.

sentences.zh: 乏草木，少水潦，四時恒有冰雪，唯六七月雨雹甚盛；

translations.literal: It lacked grass and trees, had little rain and flood; ice and snow persisted through the four seasons—only in the sixth and seventh months hail and rain were abundant;
translations.idiomatic: Grass and trees were scarce, rain and flood rare; ice and snow held through the four seasons—only in the sixth and seventh months did hail and rain fall heavily;

sentences.zh: 若晴則風飄沙礫，常蔽光景。

translations.literal: when skies cleared, wind blew sand and gravel, often blotting out the light.
translations.idiomatic: when skies cleared, wind whipped sand and gravel and often blotted out the light.

sentences.zh: 其地有麥無穀。

translations.literal: The land had wheat but no millet.
translations.idiomatic: The land grew wheat but not millet.

sentences.zh: 有青海方數百里，放牝馬其側，輒生駒，土人謂之龍種，故其國多善馬。

translations.literal: There was Qinghai Sea, several hundred li square—mares pastured beside it would bear foals; locals called them dragon stock, so the state had many fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghai Sea spread several hundred li across; mares pastured beside it would foal, and locals called the offspring dragon stock—hence the realm's many fine horses.

sentences.zh: 有屋宇，雜以百子帳，卽穹廬也。

translations.literal: They had houses, mixed with hundred-son tents—that is, yurt tents.
translations.idiomatic: They had houses mixed with hundred-son tents—that is, felt yurts.

sentences.zh: 著小袖袍、小口袴、大頭長裙帽。

translations.literal: They wore small-sleeved robes, narrow trousers, and large-headed long-skirt caps.
translations.idiomatic: They wore small-sleeved robes, narrow trousers, and large-headed caps with long skirts.

sentences.zh: 女子披髮爲辮。

translations.literal: Women wore their hair loose in braids.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore their hair loose and braided.

sentences.zh: 其後吐谷渾孫葉延，頗識書記，自謂曾祖奕洛干始封昌黎公，吾蓋公孫之子也。

translations.literal: Later Tuyuhun's grandson Yeyan knew books and records well; he said his great-grandfather Yiluoqian was first enfeoffed as Duke of Changli—"I am the duke's grandson's son."
translations.idiomatic: Later Tuyuhun's grandson Yeyan was well versed in writing; he said his great-grandfather Yiluoqian was first enfeoffed Duke of Changli—"I am the duke's grandson's son."

sentences.zh: 禮以王父字爲國氏，因姓吐谷渾，亦爲國號。

translations.literal: By ritual one takes the paternal grandfather's name as the clan name—thus they surnamed Tuyuhun, which also became the state name.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual the paternal grandfather's name becomes the clan name; they therefore took Tuyuhun as surname and as the name of the state.

sentences.zh: 至其末孫阿豺，始受中國官爵。

translations.literal: Down to his last descendant Achen, they first received Chinese office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the last descendant Achen did they first receive Chinese offices and ranks.

sentences.zh: 弟子慕延，宋元嘉末又自號河南王。

translations.literal: His younger brother's son Muyan, at the end of Song Yuanjia, styled himself King of Henan again.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Muyan, at the end of Song Yuanjia, again styled himself King of Henan.

sentences.zh: 慕延死，從弟拾寅立，乃用書契，起城池，築宮殿，其小王並立宅。

translations.literal: When Muyan died, his cousin Shibin succeeded; then they used written records, raised walls and cities, built palaces—and lesser kings all built residences.
translations.idiomatic: When Muyan died, his cousin Shibin succeeded. Then they used written records, raised walls and cities, built palaces, and lesser kings all built houses of their own.

sentences.zh: 國中有佛法。

translations.literal: Buddhism existed within the state.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism was present in the realm.

sentences.zh: 拾寅死，子度易侯立；

translations.literal: When Shibin died, his son Duyihou succeeded;
translations.idiomatic: When Shibin died, his son Duyihou succeeded;

sentences.zh: 易侯死，子休留代立。

translations.literal: When Duyihou died, his son Xiuliudai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Duyihou died, his son Xiuliudai succeeded.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，以代爲使持節、都督西秦、河、沙三州、鎮西將軍、護羌校尉、西秦、河二州刺史。

translations.literal: In Qi Yongming, Xiuliudai was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Area Commander of West Qin, He, and Sha commanderies, General Who Pacifies the West, Protector of the Qiang, and Inspector of West Qin and He.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Yongming, Xiuliudai was made bearer of the staff, area commander of West Qin, He, and Sha, General Who Pacifies the West, Protector of the Qiang, and inspector of West Qin and He.

sentences.zh: 高昌國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Gaochang
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Gaochang

sentences.zh: 高昌國，闞氏爲主，其後爲河西王沮渠茂虔弟無諱襲破之，其王闞爽奔于芮芮。

translations.literal: In Gaochang the Kan clan were lords; later Wuwei, brother of Hexi King Juqu Maoqian, attacked and broke them—their king Kan Shuang fled to Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaochang the Kan clan held sway; later Wuwei, brother of Hexi King Juqu Maoqian, attacked and overthrew them, and King Kan Shuang fled to Rouran.

sentences.zh: 無諱據之稱王，一世而滅。

translations.literal: Wuwei seized it and styled himself king; one generation and it perished.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei seized the realm and styled himself king; one generation later it was gone.

sentences.zh: 國人又立麹氏爲王，名嘉，元魏授車騎將軍、司空公、都督秦州諸軍事、秦州刺史、金城郡開國公。

translations.literal: The people again set up the Qu clan as kings—named Jia; Northern Wei granted him General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of Works, Area Commander of Qinzhou, Inspector of Qinzhou, and Duke of Jincheng with a state domain.
translations.idiomatic: The people again raised the Qu clan to kingship—Jia by name. Northern Wei made him General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of Works, area commander of Qinzhou, inspector of Qinzhou, and Duke of Jincheng with a state domain.

sentences.zh: 在位二十四年卒，諡曰昭武王。

translations.literal: He ruled twenty-four years and died; his posthumous title was Bright Martial King.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled twenty-four years and died; his posthumous title was Bright Martial King.

sentences.zh: 子子堅，使持節、驃騎大將軍、散騎常侍、都督瓜州諸軍事、瓜州刺史、河西郡開國公、儀同三司高昌王嗣位。

translations.literal: His son Zijian—Bearer of the Staff, General of Flying Cavalry, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Area Commander of Guazhou, Inspector of Guazhou, Duke of Hexi with a state domain, Equal in Glory to the Three Dukes, King of Gaochang—succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zijian—bearer of the staff, General of Flying Cavalry, regular attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, area commander of Guazhou, inspector of Guazhou, Duke of Hexi with a state domain, equal in glory to the Three Dukes, King of Gaochang—succeeded.

sentences.zh: 其國蓋車師之故地也。

translations.literal: The state roughly occupies the old land of Cheshi.
translations.idiomatic: The realm roughly occupies the old territory of Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 南接河南，東連燉煌，西次龜茲，北鄰敕勒。

translations.literal: South it adjoins Henan, east it links to Dunhuang, west it reaches to Kucha, north it neighbors the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: South it adjoins Henan, east it connects to Dunhuang, west it reaches Kucha, north it borders the Tiele.

sentences.zh: 置四十六鎮，交河、田地、高寧、臨川、橫截、柳婆、洿林、新興、由寧、始昌、篤進、白力等，皆其鎮名。

translations.literal: It set up forty-six garrison towns—Jiaohe, Tiandi, Gaoning, Linchuan, Hengjie, Liupo, Wulin, Xinxing, Youning, Shichang, Dujin, Baili, and others—all garrison names.
translations.idiomatic: It maintained forty-six garrison towns—Jiaohe, Tiandi, Gaoning, Linchuan, Hengjie, Liupo, Wulin, Xinxing, Youning, Shichang, Dujin, Baili, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 官有四鎮將軍及雜號將軍、長史、司馬、門下校郎、中兵校郎、通事舍人、通事令史、諮議、校尉、主簿。

translations.literal: Offices included four-garrison generals and miscellaneous-title generals, chief clerks, marshals, gate-section adjutants, central-army adjutants, liaison attendants, liaison clerks, advisers, commandants, and chief recorders.
translations.idiomatic: Offices included four-garrison generals and miscellaneous-title generals, chief clerks, marshals, gate-section adjutants, central-army adjutants, liaison attendants, liaison clerks, advisers, commandants, and chief recorders.

sentences.zh: 國人言語與中國略同。

translations.literal: The people's speech was roughly like China's.
translations.idiomatic: The people's speech was roughly like that of China.

sentences.zh: 有《五經》、歷代史、諸子集。

translations.literal: They had the Five Classics, dynastic histories, and collected works of the masters.
translations.idiomatic: They possessed the Five Classics, dynastic histories, and collected works of the masters.

sentences.zh: 面貌類高驪，辮髮垂之於背，著長身小袖袍、縵襠袴。

translations.literal: Faces resembled Goguryeo's; hair was braided and hung down the back; they wore long-bodied small-sleeved robes and patterned trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Their faces resembled Goguryeo's; hair was braided and hung down the back; they wore long-bodied small-sleeved robes and patterned trousers.

sentences.zh: 女子頭髮辮而不垂，著錦纈纓珞環釧。

translations.literal: Women braided their hair without letting it hang, and wore brocade patterned head ornaments, chains, rings, and bracelets.
translations.idiomatic: Women braided their hair without letting it hang, and wore brocade head ornaments, chains, rings, and bracelets.

sentences.zh: 姻有六禮。

translations.literal: Marriage had the six rites.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage followed the six rites.

sentences.zh: 其地高燥，築土爲城，架木爲屋，土覆其上。

translations.literal: The land was high and dry; they built cities of earth, framed houses of wood, and roofed them with earth.
translations.idiomatic: The land was high and dry; they built earthen cities, framed houses of wood, and roofed them with earth.

sentences.zh: 寒暑與益州相似。

translations.literal: Cold and heat resembled Yizhou's.
translations.idiomatic: Cold and heat were much like Yizhou's.

sentences.zh: 備植九穀，人多噉麨及羊牛肉。

translations.literal: They planted all nine grains; people mostly ate griddle-cakes and mutton and beef.
translations.idiomatic: They planted all nine grains; people mostly ate griddle-cakes, mutton, and beef.

sentences.zh: 出良馬、蒲陶酒、石鹽。

translations.literal: They produced fine horses, grape wine, and rock salt.
translations.idiomatic: They produced fine horses, grape wine, and rock salt.

sentences.zh: 多草木，草實如繭，繭中絲如細纑，名爲白疊子，國人多取織以爲布。

translations.literal: Grass and trees were abundant; grass seed pods were like cocoons, and the silk inside was like fine floss—called "white pile seed"; people often gathered them to weave cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Grass and trees were abundant; grass seed came in pods like cocoons, with silk inside fine as floss—called white pile seed—and people often gathered it to weave cloth.

sentences.zh: 布甚軟白，交市用焉。

translations.literal: The cloth was very soft and white, used in trade.
translations.idiomatic: The cloth was very soft and white and served in trade.

sentences.zh: 有朝烏者，旦旦集王殿前，爲行列，不畏人，日出然後散去。

translations.literal: There were "court-birds"—each dawn they assembled before the royal hall in ranks, unafraid of people, and only dispersed after sunrise.
translations.idiomatic: There were court-birds: each dawn they gathered before the royal hall in ranks, unafraid of people, and only scattered after sunrise.

sentences.zh: 大同中，子堅遣使獻鳴鹽枕、蒲陶、良馬、氍毹等物。

translations.literal: In Datong, Zijian sent envoys presenting singing-salt pillows, grapes, fine horses, carpets, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong, Zijian sent envoys with singing-salt pillows, grapes, fine horses, carpets, and the like.

sentences.zh: 元魏之居桑乾也，滑猶爲小國，屬芮芮。

translations.literal: When Northern Wei dwelt at Sanggan, Hua was still a small state, subject to Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Wei dwelt at Sanggan, Hua was still a small state under Rouran.

sentences.zh: 後稍強大，征其旁國波斯、盤盤、罽賓、焉耆、龜茲、疏勒、姑墨、于闐、句盤等國，開地千餘里。

translations.literal: Later it grew somewhat powerful, campaigning against neighboring states—Persia, Panpan, Kasmira, Karasahr, Kucha, Shule, Gumo, Yutian, Gupan, and others—opening territory over a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Later it grew stronger and campaigned against neighboring states—Persia, Panpan, Kasmira, Karasahr, Kucha, Shule, Gumo, Yutian, Gupan, and others—opening territory over a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 土地溫暖，多山川樹木，有五穀。

translations.literal: The land was warm; mountains, rivers, and trees were many; there were the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: The land was warm, with many mountains, rivers, and trees, and the five grains grew there.

sentences.zh: 國人以罝及羊肉爲糧。

translations.literal: The people used nets and mutton as food.
translations.idiomatic: The people lived on game taken in nets and on mutton.

sentences.zh: 其獸有師子、兩腳駱駝，野驢有角。

translations.literal: Their beasts included lions and two-legged camels; wild asses had horns.
translations.idiomatic: Their beasts included lions and two-legged camels; wild asses bore horns.

sentences.zh: 人皆善射，著小袖長身袍，用金玉爲帶。

translations.literal: All were skilled archers; they wore small-sleeved long-bodied robes, with belts of gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: All were skilled archers; they wore small-sleeved long-bodied robes with belts of gold and jade.

sentences.zh: 女人被裘，頭上刻木爲角，長六尺，以金銀飾之。

translations.literal: Women wore furs; on their heads they carved wooden horns six feet long, adorned with gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore furs and carved wooden horns six feet long for their heads, adorned with gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 少女子，兄弟共妻。

translations.literal: There were few women; brothers shared wives.
translations.idiomatic: Women were scarce; brothers shared a wife.

sentences.zh: 無城郭，氊屋爲居，東向開戶。

translations.literal: There were no walled cities—they lived in felt tents, doors opening east.
translations.idiomatic: They had no walled cities and lived in felt tents with doors facing east.

sentences.zh: 其王坐金床，隨太歲轉，與妻並坐接客。

translations.literal: Their king sat on a golden bed, turning with the Grand Year Star, and received guests seated together with his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Their king sat on a golden bed that turned with the Grand Year Star and received guests seated beside his wife.

sentences.zh: 無文字，以木爲契。

translations.literal: They had no writing; wood served as tokens.
translations.idiomatic: They had no writing and used wood for tokens.

sentences.zh: 與旁國通，則使旁國胡爲胡書，羊皮爲紙。

translations.literal: When dealing with neighboring states, they had neighboring barbarians write in barbarian script, sheepskin serving as paper.
translations.idiomatic: When dealing with neighbors, they had neighboring barbarians write in barbarian script on sheepskin for paper.

sentences.zh: 無職官。

translations.literal: There were no official posts.
translations.idiomatic: They had no official posts.

sentences.zh: 事天神、火神，每日則出戶祀神而後食。

translations.literal: They served Heaven-god and Fire-god; each day they left the door to worship the gods before eating.
translations.idiomatic: They served Heaven-god and Fire-god; each day they went out to worship before eating.

sentences.zh: 其跪一拜而止。

translations.literal: Their kneeling bow was one prostration and stop.
translations.idiomatic: Their kneeling bow was a single prostration and no more.

sentences.zh: 葬以木爲槨。

translations.literal: Burial used wooden coffins.
translations.idiomatic: Burial was in wooden coffins.

sentences.zh: 父母死，其子截一耳，葬訖卽吉。

translations.literal: When parents died, their sons cut off one ear; mourning ended as soon as burial was done.
translations.idiomatic: When parents died, sons cut off one ear; mourning ended as soon as burial was finished.

sentences.zh: 其言語待河南人譯然後通。

translations.literal: Their speech required Henan people as interpreters before it could be understood.
translations.idiomatic: Their speech had to be rendered by Henan interpreters before it could be understood.

sentences.zh: 周古柯國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Zhou Guke
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Zhou Guke

sentences.zh: 周古柯國，滑旁小國也。

translations.literal: Zhou Guke was a small state beside Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Guke was a small state beside Hua.

sentences.zh: 普通元年，使使隨滑來獻方物。

translations.literal: In Putong 1, envoys came with Hua to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong 1 envoys came with Hua to present local products.

sentences.zh: 呵跋檀國

translations.literal: Kingdom of He Batan
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of He Batan

sentences.zh: 呵跋檀國，亦滑旁小國也。

translations.literal: He Batan was also a small state beside Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He Batan was also a small state beside Hua.

sentences.zh: 凡滑旁之國，衣服容貌皆與滑同。

translations.literal: All states beside Hua—clothing and faces all matched Hua's.
translations.idiomatic: All states beside Hua wore the same clothes and looked the same as Hua.

sentences.zh: 普通元年，使使隨滑使來獻方物。

translations.literal: In Putong 1, envoys came with Hua's embassy to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong 1 envoys came with Hua's embassy to present local products.

sentences.zh: 胡蜜丹國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Hu Midan
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Hu Midan

sentences.zh: 胡蜜丹國，亦滑旁小國也。

translations.literal: Hu Midan was also a small state beside Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Midan was also a small state beside Hua.

sentences.zh: 普通元年，使使隨滑使來獻方物。

translations.literal: In Putong 1, envoys came with Hua's embassy to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong 1 envoys came with Hua's embassy to present local products.

sentences.zh: 白題國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Baiti
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Baiti

sentences.zh: 白題國，王姓支名史稽毅，其先蓋匈奴之別種胡也。

translations.literal: In Baiti the king's surname was Zhi, name Shi Jiyi; his ancestors were probably a separate branch of the Xiongnu barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In Baiti the king's surname was Zhi and his name Shi Jiyi; his ancestors were likely a separate branch of the Xiongnu barbarians.

sentences.zh: 漢灌嬰與匈奴戰，斬白題騎一人。

translations.literal: In Han, Guan Ying fought the Xiongnu and cut down one Baiti horseman.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, Guan Ying fought the Xiongnu and cut down one Baiti horseman.

sentences.zh: 今在滑國東，去滑六日行，西極波斯。

translations.literal: Now it lies east of Hua, six days' travel from Hua; west it reaches to Persia.
translations.idiomatic: Now it lies east of Hua, six days' travel away; west it reaches as far as Persia.

sentences.zh: 土地出粟、麥、瓜果，食物略與滑同。

translations.literal: The land produced millet, wheat, melons, and fruits; food was roughly like Hua's.
translations.idiomatic: The land produced millet, wheat, melons, and fruits; food was much like Hua's.

sentences.zh: 普通三年，遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the third year of Putong, envoys were sent presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong 3 they sent envoys with tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 龜茲者，西域之舊國也。

translations.literal: Kucha was an ancient state of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha was an old kingdom of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 後漢光武時，其王名弘，爲莎車王賢所殺，滅其族。

translations.literal: In Later Han during Emperor Guangwu's reign, its king named Hong was killed by Shache King Xian, who wiped out his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Han's Emperor Guangwu, King Hong was killed by Shache's King Xian, who exterminated his clan.

sentences.zh: 賢使其子則羅爲龜茲王，國人又殺則羅。

translations.literal: Xian installed his son Zeluo as king of Kucha; the people of the state killed Zeluo.
translations.idiomatic: Xian set his son Zeluo on the throne; the Kuchans killed him.

sentences.zh: 匈奴立龜茲貴人身毒爲王，由是屬匈奴。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu installed the Kucha noble Shendu as king; from then it belonged to the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu raised the Kucha noble Shendu to the throne, and Kucha passed under Xiongnu control.

sentences.zh: 然龜茲在漢世常爲大國，所都曰延城。

translations.literal: Yet in Han times Kucha was often a great state; its capital was called Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yet under Han Kucha was commonly a great power, with its capital at Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝初卽位，遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: When Wei Emperor Wen first took the throne, he sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Wen of Wei's reign, envoys brought tribute.

sentences.zh: 晉太康中，遣子入侍。

translations.literal: In Jin's Taikang era, a son was sent to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin's Taikang period a royal son was sent to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 太元七年，秦主苻堅遣將呂光伐西域。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taiyuan, Qin ruler Fu Jian sent General Lü Guang to campaign in the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyuan 7, Fu Jian of Former Qin sent General Lü Guang against the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 至龜茲，龜茲王帛純載寶出奔，光入其城。

translations.literal: Reaching Kucha, King Bo Chun loaded treasure and fled; Guang entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Kucha, King Bo Chun fled with his treasure loaded; Lü Guang took the city.

sentences.zh: 城有三重，外城與長安城等，室屋壯麗，飾以琅玕金玉。

translations.literal: The city had triple walls; the outer wall matched Chang'an in size; houses and halls were grand and splendid, adorned with coral, gems, and gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Triple-walled, its outer rampart rivaled Chang'an; halls stood grand and bright, trimmed in coral, gems, gold, and jade.

sentences.zh: 光立帛純弟震爲王而歸，自此與中國絕不通。

translations.literal: Guang installed Bo Chun's younger brother Zhen as king and returned; from then contact with China ceased entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang set Bo Chun's brother Zhen on the throne and withdrew; from that time Kucha broke all contact with China.

sentences.zh: 普通二年，王尼瑞摩珠那勝遣使奉表貢獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putong, King Niruimozhunasheng sent envoys presenting a memorial with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong 2, King Niruimozhunasheng sent envoys with a formal tribute memorial.

sentences.zh: 于闐國，西域之屬也。

translations.literal: The state of Khotan was a dependency of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan belonged to the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 後漢建武末，王俞爲莎車王賢所破，徙爲驪歸王，以其弟君得爲于闐王，暴虐，百姓患之。

translations.literal: At the end of Later Han Jianwu, King Yu was defeated by Shache King Xian, removed to be king of Ligui, and Yu's younger brother Junde was made king of Khotan—cruel and tyrannical, the people suffered under him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jianwu in Later Han, King Yu was broken by Shache's King Xian, demoted to king of Ligui, and Yu's brother Junde installed in Khotan—fierce and brutal, the people groaned beneath him.

sentences.zh: 永平中，其種人都末殺君得，大人休莫霸又殺都末，自立爲王。

translations.literal: In Yongping, the tribesman Dumo killed Junde; the elder Xiumoba killed Dumo and set himself up as king.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongping the tribesman Dumo killed Junde; the elder Xiumoba killed Dumo and proclaimed himself king.

sentences.zh: 霸死，兄子廣得立，後擊虜莎車王賢以歸，殺之，遂爲強國，西北諸小國皆服從。

translations.literal: When Ba died, his elder brother's son Guangde succeeded; later he captured Shache King Xian and brought him back, killed him, and became a powerful state—all the small states of the northwest submitted.
translations.idiomatic: After Ba's death his nephew Guangde took the throne; he later captured Shache's King Xian, brought him back, and killed him—Khotan became a great power and every small northwestern realm bowed.

sentences.zh: 其地多水潦沙石，氣溫，宜稻、麥、蒲桃。

translations.literal: Its land has much standing water, sand, and stone; the climate is warm; rice, wheat, and grapes thrive.
translations.idiomatic: The country is wet and stony, warm in climate, suited to rice, wheat, and grapes.

sentences.zh: 有水出玉，名曰玉河。

translations.literal: A river yields jade; it is called the Jade River.
translations.idiomatic: A river bearing jade runs there—the Jade River.

sentences.zh: 國人善鑄銅器。

translations.literal: The people of the state are skilled at casting bronze vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The people excel at casting bronze ware.

sentences.zh: 其治曰西山城，有屋室市井。

translations.literal: Its seat of government is called West Mountain City; there are dwellings, markets, and lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital is West Mountain City, with houses, streets, and markets.

sentences.zh: 果蓏菜蔬與中國等。

translations.literal: Fruits, melons, and vegetables match those of China.
translations.idiomatic: Its fruits, melons, and vegetables are much like China's.

sentences.zh: 尤敬佛法。

translations.literal: They revere the Buddhist Law above all.
translations.idiomatic: They hold the Buddhist Dharma in special reverence.

sentences.zh: 王所居室，加以朱畫。

translations.literal: The king's residence is painted in cinnabar red.
translations.idiomatic: The royal dwelling is painted red throughout.

sentences.zh: 王冠金幘，如今胡公帽；

translations.literal: The king wears a golden kerchief-cap, like today's foreign chieftain's hat;
translations.idiomatic: The king wears a gold head-wrap, like a foreign lord's cap;

sentences.zh: 與妻並坐接客。

translations.literal: he and his wife sit side by side to receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: and receives guests seated beside his queen.

sentences.zh: 國中婦人皆辮髮，衣裘袴。

translations.literal: Women throughout the state wear braided hair and fur coats and trousers.
translations.idiomatic: All women braid their hair and dress in furs and trousers.

sentences.zh: 其人恭，相見則跪，其跪則一膝至地。

translations.literal: The people are deferential; when they meet they kneel, and in kneeling one knee touches the ground.
translations.idiomatic: They are courteous; on meeting they kneel on one knee to the ground.

sentences.zh: 書則以木爲筆劄，以玉爲印。

translations.literal: For writing they use wood as stylus and tablets, and jade as seal.
translations.idiomatic: They write on wooden slips with wooden styluses and seal with jade.

sentences.zh: 國人得書，戴於首而後開劄。

translations.literal: When natives receive a letter, they wear it on the head before opening the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Recipients place a letter on the head before breaking the seal and opening it.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝時，王山習獻名馬。

translations.literal: In Wei Emperor Wen's time, King Shanxi presented famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen of Wei, King Shanxi sent famed horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 天監九年，遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianjian, envoys were sent presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 9 they sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 十三年，又獻波羅婆步鄣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year they again presented a prasada hanging screen.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 they again offered a prasada screen.

sentences.zh: 十八年，又獻琉璃罌。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year they again presented a glass jar.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 they sent a glass vessel.

sentences.zh: 大同七年，又獻外國刻玉佛。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Datong, they again presented a foreign carved jade Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 7 they sent a foreign-carved jade Buddha.

sentences.zh: 渴盤陁國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Kepantuo
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Kepantuo

sentences.zh: 渴盤陁國，于闐西小國也。

translations.literal: The state of Kepantuo is a small state west of Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Kepantuo was a small kingdom west of Khotan.

sentences.zh: 西鄰滑國，南接罽賓國，北連沙勒國。

translations.literal: West it borders Hua; south it adjoins Jibin; north it connects with Shale.
translations.idiomatic: It bordered Hua to the west, Jibin to the south, and Shale to the north.

sentences.zh: 所治在山谷中，城周回十餘里，國有十二城。

translations.literal: Its seat lies in a mountain valley; the city wall runs over ten li round; the state has twelve cities.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital stood in a mountain valley, walled for more than ten li, ruling twelve towns.

sentences.zh: 風俗與于闐相類。

translations.literal: Customs resemble Khotan's.
translations.idiomatic: Its customs were much like Khotan's.

sentences.zh: 衣吉貝布，著長身小袖袍、小口袴。

translations.literal: They wear kapok cloth, long-bodied small-sleeved robes, and narrow trousers.
translations.idiomatic: They dressed in kapok cloth, long tight-sleeved coats, and narrow trousers.

sentences.zh: 地宜小麥，資以爲糧。

translations.literal: The land suits wheat, which supplies their grain.
translations.idiomatic: Wheat flourished there and fed the people.

sentences.zh: 多牛馬駱駝羊等。

translations.literal: Cattle, horses, camels, sheep, and the like are many.
translations.idiomatic: Cattle, horses, camels, and sheep were abundant.

sentences.zh: 出好氈、金、玉。

translations.literal: It produces fine felt, gold, and jade.
translations.idiomatic: It yielded fine felt, gold, and jade.

sentences.zh: 王姓葛沙氏。

translations.literal: The royal surname is Gesa.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house bore the surname Gesa.

sentences.zh: 中大同元年，遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongdatong, envoys were sent presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong 1 they sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 末國，漢世且末國也。

translations.literal: The state of Mo was Han-era Qimo.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was the Han-era kingdom of Qimo.

sentences.zh: 勝兵萬餘戶。

translations.literal: Fighting men exceed ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: It could field more than ten thousand fighting households.

sentences.zh: 北與丁零，東與白題，西與波斯接。

translations.literal: North it borders Dingling; east Baiti; west Persia.
translations.idiomatic: Dingling lay to the north, Baiti to the east, and Persia to the west.

sentences.zh: 土人剪髮，著氈帽、小袖衣，爲衫則開頸而縫前。

translations.literal: Natives crop their hair, wear felt caps and small-sleeved coats; when making a jacket they open the neck and sew the front closed.
translations.idiomatic: The people cropped their hair, wore felt caps and short-sleeved coats, and stitched their tunics closed at the neck and front.

sentences.zh: 多牛羊騾驢。

translations.literal: Sheep, cattle, mules, and donkeys are many.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep, cattle, mules, and donkeys were plentiful.

sentences.zh: 其王安末深盤，普通五年，遣使來貢獻。

translations.literal: Its king Anmo Shenpan—in the fifth year of Putong sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: King Anmo Shenpan sent tribute envoys in Putong 5.

sentences.zh: 波斯國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Persia
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Persia

sentences.zh: 波斯國，其先有波斯匿王者，子孫以王父字爲氏，因爲國號。

translations.literal: Persia: formerly there was a king named Bosini; descendants took their father's name character as surname, hence the state's name.
translations.idiomatic: Persia took its name from an early king called Bosini, whose descendants adopted his personal name as their clan surname.

sentences.zh: 國有城，周回三十二里，城高四丈，皆有樓觀，城內屋宇數百千間，城外佛寺二三百所。

translations.literal: The state has a walled city, thirty-two li round, walls four zhang high, all with towered pavilions; within the city are hundreds of thousands of buildings; outside are two or three hundred Buddhist temples.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital ran thirty-two li around, with walls four zhang high and towered watchposts; inside stood hundreds of thousands of houses, and outside two or three hundred Buddhist temples.

sentences.zh: 西去城十五里有土山，山非過高，其勢連接甚遠，中有鷲鳥噉羊，土人極以爲患。

translations.literal: Fifteen li west of the city is an earthen mountain—not especially high, but its ridges stretch far; vultures there devour sheep, and the natives find it a grave affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen li west stood a low earthen ridge running far; vultures there preyed on sheep, and the people counted it a great plague.

sentences.zh: 國中有優缽曇花，鮮華可愛。

translations.literal: In the state is the udumbara flower—fresh and lovely.
translations.idiomatic: The udumbara flower grew there, bright and fair.

sentences.zh: 出龍駒馬。

translations.literal: Dragon colts are produced.
translations.idiomatic: It bred dragon colts.

sentences.zh: 咸池生珊瑚樹，長一二尺。

translations.literal: At Xianchi coral trees grow, one or two feet long.
translations.idiomatic: Coral trees grew at Xianchi, a foot or two in height.

sentences.zh: 亦有琥珀、馬腦、真珠、玫㻁等，國內不以爲珍。

translations.literal: There are also amber, carnelian, pearls, and rose quartz—these are not considered precious within the country.
translations.idiomatic: Amber, carnelian, pearls, and rose quartz were common and not prized at home.

sentences.zh: 市買用金銀。

translations.literal: Market trade uses gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Markets traded in gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 婚姻法：下聘訖，女婿將數十人迎婦，婿著金線錦袍、師子錦袴，戴天冠，婦亦如之。

translations.literal: Marriage law: after the bride-price is settled, the son-in-law leads several dozen men to welcome the bride; the groom wears gold-thread brocade robe and lion brocade trousers, crowned with a heavenly cap, and the bride likewise.
translations.idiomatic: By marriage custom, once the bride-price was paid the groom led dozens of men to fetch the bride, dressed in gold-thread brocade and lion-pattern trousers with a heavenly crown—the bride wore the same.

sentences.zh: 婦兄弟便來捉手付度，夫婦之禮，于茲永畢。

translations.literal: The bride's brothers at once come and take her by the hand to give her over—the rites of husband and wife are from this forever complete.
translations.idiomatic: Her brothers then took her hand and passed her to the groom—the wedding rites ended there.

sentences.zh: 國東與滑國，西及南俱與婆羅門國，北與汎慄國接。

translations.literal: East it borders Hua; west and south alike Brahman; north Fanli.
translations.idiomatic: Hua lay to the east; Brahman to the west and south; Fanli to the north.

sentences.zh: 中大通二年，遣使獻佛牙。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong, envoys were sent presenting a Buddha tooth.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong 2 they sent a Buddha tooth as tribute.

sentences.zh: 宕昌國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Dangchang
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Dangchang

sentences.zh: 宕昌國，在河南之東南，益州之西北，隴西之西，羌種也。

translations.literal: Dangchang lies southeast of Henan, northwest of Yizhou, west of Longxi—a Qiang people.
translations.idiomatic: Dangchang stood southeast of Henan, northwest of Yizhou, and west of Longxi—a Qiang people.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武世，其王梁瓘忽始獻方物。

translations.literal: In Song Emperor Xiaowu's reign, its king Liang Guanhu first presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song Emperor Xiaowu, King Liang Guanhu first sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 天監四年，王梁彌博來獻甘草、當歸，詔以爲使持節、都督河、涼二州諸軍事、安西將軍、東羌校尉、河、涼二州刺史、隴西公、宕昌王，佩以金章。

translations.literal: In Tianjian 4, King Liang Mibo came presenting licorice and angelica; an edict made him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Area Commander of military affairs of He and Liang provinces, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of the Eastern Qiang, Governor of He and Liang provinces, Duke of Longxi, and King of Dangchang, invested with a gold seal.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 4, King Liang Mibo brought licorice and angelica; the throne made him bearer of the staff, area commander of He and Liang, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of the Eastern Qiang, governor of both provinces, Duke of Longxi, and King of Dangchang, with a gold seal.

sentences.zh: 彌博死，子彌泰立；

translations.literal: When Mibo died, his son Mitai succeeded;
translations.idiomatic: When Mibo died, his son Mitai succeeded;

sentences.zh: 大同七年，復授以父爵位。

translations.literal: In Datong 7, his father's titles were again granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 7 the throne restored his father's titles.

sentences.zh: 其衣服、風俗與河南略同。

translations.literal: Their dress and customs broadly match Henan's.
translations.idiomatic: Their clothing and customs closely resembled Henan's.

sentences.zh: 鄧至國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Dengzhi
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Dengzhi

sentences.zh: 武興國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Wuxing
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Wuxing

sentences.zh: 武興國，本仇池。

translations.literal: Wuxing was originally Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxing had originally been Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 楊難當自立爲秦王，宋文帝遣裴方明討之，難當奔魏。

translations.literal: Yang Nandang set himself up as King of Qin; Song Emperor Wen sent Pei Fangming against him; Nandang fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nandang declared himself King of Qin; Song Emperor Wen sent Pei Fangming to suppress him, and Nandang fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 其兄子文德又聚衆茄盧，宋因授以爵位，魏又攻之，文德奔漢中。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Wendé gathered forces at Jialu; Song therefore granted him titles; Wei attacked again and Wendé fled to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Wendé rallied men at Jialu; Song enfeoffed him, but Wei attacked again and Wendé fled to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 從弟僧嗣又自立，復戍茄盧。

translations.literal: His younger clansman Wensie set himself up and again garrisoned Jialu.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Wensie then declared himself ruler and reoccupied Jialu.

sentences.zh: 卒，文德弟文度立，以弟文洪爲白水太守，屯武興，宋世以爲武都王。

translations.literal: When he died, Wendé's younger brother Wendu succeeded; he made his younger brother Wen Hong prefect of Baishui, encamped at Wuxing—under Song he was titled King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Wendé's brother Wendu took over, made Wen Hong prefect of Baishui, and encamped at Wuxing—Song titled him King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 武興之國，自於此矣。

translations.literal: The state of Wuxing dates from this.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Wuxing began here.

sentences.zh: 難當族弟廣香又攻殺文度，自立爲陰平王、茄盧鎮主。

translations.literal: Nandang's clansman Guangxiang attacked and killed Wendu, set himself up as King of Yinping and commandant of Jialu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang's kinsman Guangxiang killed Wendu and made himself King of Yinping and commandant of Jialu.

sentences.zh: 卒，子炅立；

translations.literal: When he died, his son Jiong succeeded;
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Jiong succeeded;

sentences.zh: 炅死，子崇祖立；

translations.literal: When Jiong died, his son Chongzu succeeded;
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong died, his son Chongzu succeeded;

sentences.zh: 崇祖死，子孟孫立。

translations.literal: When Chongzu died, his son Mengersun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongzu died, his son Mengersun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，魏氏南梁州刺史、仇池公楊靈珍據泥功山歸款，齊世以靈珍爲北梁州刺史、仇池公。

translations.literal: In Qi Yongming, Wei's Southern Liangzhou inspector and Duke of Qiuchi Yang Lingzhen held Migong Mountain and submitted; under Qi, Lingzhen was made Northern Liangzhou inspector and Duke of Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Yongming, Yang Lingzhen—Wei's southern Liangzhou inspector and Duke of Qiuchi—held Migong Mountain and submitted; Qi made him northern Liangzhou inspector and Duke of Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 文洪死，以族人集始爲北秦州刺史、武都王。

translations.literal: When Wen Hong died, clansman Jishi was made Northern Qinzhou inspector and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: After Wen Hong died, the clansman Jishi became northern Qinzhou inspector and King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 天監初，以集始爲使持節、都督秦、雍二州諸軍事、輔國將軍、平羌校尉、北秦州刺史、武都王，靈珍爲冠軍將軍，孟孫爲假節、督沙州刺史、陰平王。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianjian, Jishi was made Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander of Qin and Yong military affairs, General Who Assists the State, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Northern Qinzhou inspector, and King of Wudu; Lingzhen was made Champion General; Mengersun was made Acting Staff, Commander of Shazhou, and King of Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianjian, Jishi became bearer of the staff, area commander of Qin and Yong, General Who Assists the State, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, northern Qinzhou inspector, and King of Wudu; Lingzhen became champion general; Mengersun acting staff, commander of Shazhou, and King of Yinping.

sentences.zh: 集始死，子紹先襲爵位。

translations.literal: When Jishi died, his son Shaoxian inherited the titles.
translations.idiomatic: When Jishi died, his son Shaoxian inherited the titles.

sentences.zh: 二年，以靈珍爲持節、督隴右諸軍事、左將軍、北梁州刺史、仇池王。

translations.literal: In year 2, Lingzhen was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Longyou military affairs, Left General, Northern Liangzhou inspector, and King of Qiuchi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 Lingzhen became bearer of the staff, commander of Longyou, left general, northern Liangzhou inspector, and King of Qiuchi.

sentences.zh: 十年，孟孫死，詔贈安沙將軍、北雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In year 10, Mengersun died; an edict posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the Sands and Northern Yongzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 Mengersun died; the throne posthumously made him General Who Pacifies the Sands and northern Yongzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 子定襲封爵。

translations.literal: His son Ding inherited the enfeoffment and titles.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ding inherited the fief and titles.

sentences.zh: 紹先死，子智慧立。

translations.literal: When Shaoxian died, his son Zhihui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoxian died, his son Zhihui succeeded.

sentences.zh: 大同元年，剋復漢中，智慧遣使上表，求率四千戶歸國，詔許焉，卽以爲東益州。

translations.literal: In Datong 1, Hanzhong was recovered; Zhihui sent envoys with a memorial asking to lead four thousand households back to the realm; an edict permitted it, and the area was made Eastern Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 1, after Hanzhong was retaken, Zhihui asked by memorial to bring four thousand households home; the throne agreed and made the region Eastern Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 其國東連秦嶺，西接宕昌，去宕昌八百里，南去漢中四百里，北去岐州三百里，東去長安九百里。

translations.literal: Its state adjoins Qinling to the east and Dangchang to the west—eight hundred li from Dangchang, four hundred li south of Hanzhong, three hundred li north of Qizhou, nine hundred li east of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: It touched Qinling on the east and Dangchang on the west—eight hundred li from Dangchang, four hundred south of Hanzhong, three hundred north of Qizhou, nine hundred east of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 本有十萬戶，世世分減。

translations.literal: Originally there were a hundred thousand households; generation by generation the count diminished.
translations.idiomatic: It once held a hundred thousand households, but the numbers shrank with each generation.

sentences.zh: 其大姓有符氏、薑氏。

translations.literal: Great surnames include Fu and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Leading clans were Fu and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 言語與中國同。

translations.literal: Their speech matches China's.
translations.idiomatic: They spoke the same language as China.

sentences.zh: 著烏皁突騎帽、長身小袖袍、小口袴、皮靴。

translations.literal: They wear black-felt chieftain's riding caps, long-bodied small-sleeved robes, narrow trousers, and leather boots.
translations.idiomatic: They wore black felt riding caps, long tight-sleeved coats, narrow trousers, and leather boots.

sentences.zh: 地植九穀。

translations.literal: The land grows the nine grains.
translations.idiomatic: The land yielded the nine grains.

sentences.zh: 婚姻備六禮。

translations.literal: Marriage observes all six rites.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage followed the full six rites.

sentences.zh: 知書疏。

translations.literal: They know letters and documents.
translations.idiomatic: They were literate in correspondence.

sentences.zh: 種桑麻。

translations.literal: They plant mulberry and hemp.
translations.idiomatic: They cultivated mulberry and hemp.

sentences.zh: 出紬、絹、精布、漆、蠟、椒等。

translations.literal: They produce pongee, silk, fine cloth, lacquer, wax, pepper, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: They exported pongee, silk, fine cloth, lacquer, wax, pepper, and similar goods.

sentences.zh: 山出銅鐵。

translations.literal: Their mountains yield copper and iron.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains produced copper and iron.

sentences.zh: 芮芮國

translations.literal: Kingdom of Ruru
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom of Ruru

sentences.zh: 其國能以術祭天而致風雪，前對皎日，後則泥潦橫流，故其戰敗莫能追及。

translations.literal: Their state can by art sacrifice to Heaven and bring wind and snow; facing it one meets bright sun, behind one muddy flood streams across—thus when they are defeated none can pursue them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ruru could perform rituals to Heaven and summon wind and snow; bright sun lay ahead while muddy floods swept behind, so when they broke and fled no pursuer could catch them.

sentences.zh: 或於中夏爲之，則曀而不雨，問其故，以㬉云。

translations.literal: If performed within Central China, then it grows dim but does not rain; asked the reason, they say it is because of warmth.
translations.idiomatic: Performed in China proper, the rite only darkened the sky without bringing rain; asked why, they said the land was too warm.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：海南東夷西北戎諸國，地窮邊裔，各有疆域。

translations.literal: The historian writes: The states of the Southern Sea, Eastern Yi, and Northwestern Rong—all lands at the utter edge of the realm, each with its own territory.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: From the Southern Sea to the Eastern Yi and Northwestern Rong, these states lay at the far edge of the world, each with its own domain.

sentences.zh: 若山奇海異，怪類殊種，前古未聞，往牒不記。

translations.literal: As for strange mountains and wondrous seas, monstrous kinds and exotic species—none heard of in former antiquity, not recorded in prior documents.
translations.idiomatic: Strange peaks and curious seas, freakish breeds and alien peoples—nothing former ages had heard of, nothing old annals had set down.

sentences.zh: 故知九州之外，八荒之表，辯方物土，莫究其極。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that beyond the Nine Provinces and outside the Eight Wastes, in discerning regional products and soils, none can exhaust the furthest limit.
translations.idiomatic: So it is clear: beyond the Nine Provinces and past the Eight Wastes, cataloguing every land and tribute would never reach the end.

sentences.zh: 高祖以德懷之，故朝貢歲至，美矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu embraced them through virtue, and so tribute arrived year after year—how fine.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu drew them in through virtue, and tribute came year after year—a thing of beauty.
